luke/3/1.text: 3 In the 15th year of the reign of Ti·beʹri·us Caesar, when Pontius Pilate was governor of Ju·deʹa, Herod was district ruler of Galʹi·lee, Philip his brother was district ruler of the country of It·u·raeʹa and Trach·o·niʹtis, and Ly·saʹni·as was district ruler of Ab·i·leʹne,

luke/3/2.text: in the days of chief priest Anʹnas and of Caʹia·phas, God’s declaration came to John the son of Zech·a·riʹah in the wilderness.

luke/3/3.text: So he went into all the country around the Jordan, preaching baptism in symbol of repentance for forgiveness of sins,

luke/3/4.text: just as it is written in the book of the words of Isaiah the prophet: “A voice of one crying out in the wilderness: ‘Prepare the way of Jehovah! Make his roads straight.

luke/3/5.text: Every valley must be filled up, and every mountain and hill leveled; the crooked ways must become straight, and the rough ways smooth;

luke/3/6.text: and all flesh will see the salvation of God.’”

luke/3/7.text: So he began to say to the crowds coming out to be baptized by him: “You offspring of vipers, who has warned you to flee from the coming wrath?

luke/3/8.text: Therefore, produce fruits that befit repentance. Do not start saying to yourselves, ‘We have Abraham as our father.’ For I say to you that God is able to raise up children for Abraham from these stones.

luke/3/9.text: Indeed, the ax is already lying at the root of the trees. Every tree, then, that does not produce fine fruit will be cut down and thrown into the fire.”

luke/3/10.text: And the crowds were asking him: “What, then, should we do?”

luke/3/11.text: In reply he said to them: “Let the man who has two garments share with the man who has none, and let the one who has something to eat do the same.”

luke/3/12.text: Even tax collectors came to be baptized, and they said to him: “Teacher, what should we do?”

luke/3/13.text: He said to them: “Do not demand anything more than the tax rate.”

luke/3/14.text: Also, those in military service were asking him: “What should we do?” And he said to them: “Do not harass anybody or accuse anybody falsely, but be satisfied with your provisions.”

luke/3/15.text: Now the people were in expectation and all of them were reasoning in their hearts about John, “May he perhaps be the Christ?”

luke/3/16.text: John gave the answer, saying to all: “I, for my part, baptize you with water, but the one stronger than I am is coming, the lace of whose sandals I am not worthy to untie. He will baptize you with holy spirit and with fire.

luke/3/17.text: His winnowing shovel is in his hand to clean up his threshing floor completely and to gather the wheat into his storehouse, but the chaff he will burn up with fire that cannot be put out.”

luke/3/18.text: He also gave many other exhortations and continued declaring good news to the people.

luke/3/19.text: But Herod the district ruler, because of being reproved by John concerning He·roʹdi·as the wife of his brother and concerning all the wicked deeds that Herod had done,

luke/3/20.text: added this also to all those deeds: He locked John up in prison.

luke/3/21.text: Now when all the people were baptized, Jesus too was baptized. As he was praying, the heaven was opened up,

luke/3/22.text: and the holy spirit in bodily form like a dove came down upon him, and a voice came out of heaven: “You are my Son, the beloved; I have approved you.”

luke/3/23.text: When Jesus began his work, he was about 30 years old, being the son, as the opinion was, of Joseph, son of Heʹli,

luke/3/24.text: son of Matʹthat, son of Leʹvi, son of Melʹchi, son of Janʹna·i, son of Joseph,

luke/3/25.text: son of Mat·ta·thiʹas, son of Aʹmos, son of Naʹhum, son of Esʹli, son of Nagʹga·i,

luke/3/26.text: son of Maʹath, son of Mat·ta·thiʹas, son of Semʹe·in, son of Joʹsech, son of Joʹda,

luke/3/27.text: son of Jo·anʹan, son of Rheʹsa, son of Ze·rubʹba·bel, son of She·alʹti·el, son of Neʹri,

luke/3/28.text: son of Melʹchi, son of Adʹdi, son of Coʹsam, son of El·maʹdam, son of Er,

luke/3/29.text: son of Jesus, son of E·li·eʹzer, son of Joʹrim, son of Matʹthat, son of Leʹvi,

luke/3/30.text: son of Symʹe·on, son of Judas, son of Joseph, son of Joʹnam, son of E·liʹa·kim,

luke/3/31.text: son of Meʹle·a, son of Menʹna, son of Matʹta·tha, son of Nathan, son of David,

luke/3/32.text: son of Jesʹse, son of Oʹbed, son of Boʹaz, son of Salʹmon, son of Nahʹshon,

luke/3/33.text: son of Am·minʹa·dab, son of Arʹni, son of Hezʹron, son of Peʹrez, son of Judah,

luke/3/34.text: son of Jacob, son of Isaac, son of Abraham, son of Teʹrah, son of Naʹhor,

luke/3/35.text: son of Seʹrug, son of Reʹu, son of Peʹleg, son of Eʹber, son of Sheʹlah,

luke/3/36.text: son of Ca·iʹnan, son of Ar·pachʹshad, son of Shem, son of Noah, son of Laʹmech,

luke/3/37.text: son of Me·thuʹse·lah, son of Eʹnoch, son of Jaʹred, son of Ma·haʹla·le·el, son of Ca·iʹnan,

luke/3/38.text: son of Eʹnosh, son of Seth, son of Adam, son of God.

genesis/5/1.text: 5 This is the book of Adam’s history. In the day that God created Adam, he made him in the likeness of God.

genesis/5/2.text: Male and female he created them. On the day they were created, he blessed them and named them Man.

genesis/5/3.text: Adam lived for 130 years and then became father to a son in his likeness, in his image, and he named him Seth.

genesis/5/4.text: After becoming father to Seth, Adam lived for 800 years. And he became father to sons and daughters.

genesis/5/5.text: So all the days of Adam’s life amounted to 930 years, and then he died.

genesis/5/6.text: Seth lived for 105 years and then became father to Eʹnosh.

genesis/5/7.text: After becoming father to Eʹnosh, Seth lived for 807 years. And he became father to sons and daughters.

genesis/5/8.text: So all the days of Seth amounted to 912 years, and then he died.

genesis/5/9.text: Eʹnosh lived for 90 years and then became father to Keʹnan.

genesis/5/10.text: After becoming father to Keʹnan, Eʹnosh lived for 815 years. And he became father to sons and daughters.

genesis/5/11.text: So all the days of Eʹnosh amounted to 905 years, and then he died.

genesis/5/12.text: Keʹnan lived for 70 years and then became father to Ma·halʹa·lel.

genesis/5/13.text: After becoming father to Ma·halʹa·lel, Keʹnan lived for 840 years. And he became father to sons and daughters.

genesis/5/14.text: So all the days of Keʹnan amounted to 910 years, and then he died.

genesis/5/15.text: Ma·halʹa·lel lived for 65 years and then became father to Jaʹred.

genesis/5/16.text: After becoming father to Jaʹred, Ma·halʹa·lel lived for 830 years. And he became father to sons and daughters.

genesis/5/17.text: So all the days of Ma·halʹa·lel amounted to 895 years, and then he died.

genesis/5/18.text: Jaʹred lived for 162 years and then became father to Eʹnoch.

genesis/5/19.text: After becoming father to Eʹnoch, Jaʹred lived for 800 years. And he became father to sons and daughters.

genesis/5/20.text: So all the days of Jaʹred amounted to 962 years, and then he died.

genesis/5/21.text: Eʹnoch lived for 65 years and then became father to Me·thuʹse·lah.

genesis/5/22.text: After becoming father to Me·thuʹse·lah, Eʹnoch continued to walk with the true God for 300 years. And he became father to sons and daughters.

genesis/5/23.text: So all the days of Eʹnoch amounted to 365 years.

genesis/5/24.text: Eʹnoch kept walking with the true God. Then he was no more, for God took him.

genesis/5/25.text: Me·thuʹse·lah lived for 187 years and then became father to Laʹmech.

genesis/5/26.text: After becoming father to Laʹmech, Me·thuʹse·lah lived for 782 years. And he became father to sons and daughters.

genesis/5/27.text: So all the days of Me·thuʹse·lah amounted to 969 years, and then he died.

genesis/5/28.text: Laʹmech lived for 182 years and then became father to a son.

genesis/5/29.text: He named him Noah, saying: “This one will bring us comfort from our labor and from the painful toil of our hands because of the ground that Jehovah has cursed.”

genesis/5/30.text: After becoming father to Noah, Laʹmech lived for 595 years. And he became father to sons and daughters.

genesis/5/31.text: So all the days of Laʹmech amounted to 777 years, and then he died.

genesis/5/32.text: After Noah reached 500 years of age, he became father to Shem, Ham, and Jaʹpheth.

genesis/4/1.text: 4 Now Adam had sexual relations with his wife Eve, and she became pregnant. When she gave birth to Cain, she said: “I have produced a male child with the help of Jehovah.”

genesis/4/2.text: Later she again gave birth, to his brother Abel. Abel became a shepherd of the flock, but Cain became a cultivator of the ground.

genesis/4/3.text: After some time, Cain brought some fruits of the land as an offering to Jehovah.

genesis/4/4.text: But Abel brought some firstlings of his flock, including their fat. While Jehovah looked with favor on Abel and on his offering,

genesis/4/5.text: he did not look with any favor on Cain and on his offering. So Cain grew hot with anger and was dejected.

genesis/4/6.text: Then Jehovah said to Cain: “Why are you so angry and dejected?

genesis/4/7.text: If you turn to doing good, will you not be restored to favor? But if you do not turn to doing good, sin is crouching at the door, and its craving is to dominate you; but will you get the mastery over it?”

genesis/4/8.text: After that Cain said to his brother Abel: “Let us go over into the field.” So while they were in the field, Cain assaulted his brother Abel and killed him.

genesis/4/9.text: Later on, Jehovah said to Cain: “Where is your brother Abel?” and he said: “I do not know. Am I my brother’s guardian?”

genesis/4/10.text: At this He said: “What have you done? Listen! Your brother’s blood is crying out to me from the ground.

genesis/4/11.text: And now you are cursed in banishment from the ground that has opened its mouth to receive your brother’s blood from your hand.

genesis/4/12.text: When you cultivate the ground, it will not give you back its produce. You will become a wanderer and a fugitive in the earth.”

genesis/4/13.text: At this Cain said to Jehovah: “The punishment for my error is too great to bear.

genesis/4/14.text: Today you are driving me from the land, and I will be hidden from your face; and I will become a wanderer and a fugitive on the earth, and anyone who finds me will certainly kill me.”

genesis/4/15.text: So Jehovah said to him: “For that reason, anyone who kills Cain will suffer vengeance seven times.” So Jehovah set up a sign for Cain in order that no one finding him would strike him.

genesis/4/16.text: Then Cain went away from before Jehovah and took up residence in the land of Exile, to the east of Eʹden.

genesis/4/17.text: Afterward Cain had sexual relations with his wife, and she became pregnant and gave birth to Eʹnoch. Then he engaged in building a city and named the city after his son Eʹnoch.

genesis/4/18.text: Later Iʹrad was born to Eʹnoch. And Iʹrad became father to Me·huʹja·el, and Me·huʹja·el became father to Me·thuʹsha·el, and Me·thuʹsha·el became father to Laʹmech.

genesis/4/19.text: Laʹmech took two wives for himself. The name of the first was Aʹdah, and the name of the second was Zilʹlah.

genesis/4/20.text: Aʹdah gave birth to Jaʹbal. He was the founder of those who dwell in tents and have livestock.

genesis/4/21.text: His brother’s name was Juʹbal. He was the founder of all those who play the harp and the pipe.

genesis/4/22.text: Also, Zilʹlah gave birth to Tuʹbal-cain, who forged every sort of tool of copper and iron. And the sister of Tuʹbal-cain was Naʹa·mah.

genesis/4/23.text: Then Laʹmech composed these words for his wives Aʹdah and Zilʹlah: “Hear my voice, you wives of Laʹmech;Give ear to my saying: A man I have killed for wounding me, Yes, a young man for striking me.

genesis/4/24.text: If 7 times Cain is to be avenged, Then Laʹmech 77 times.”

genesis/4/25.text: Adam again had sexual relations with his wife, and she gave birth to a son. She named him Seth because, as she said, “God has appointed for me another offspring in place of Abel, because Cain killed him.”

genesis/4/26.text: There was also born to Seth a son, and he named him Eʹnosh. At that time people began calling on the name of Jehovah.

genesis/11/1.text: 11 Now all the earth continued to be of one language and of one set of words.

genesis/11/2.text: As they traveled eastward, they discovered a valley plain in the land of Shiʹnar, and they began dwelling there.

genesis/11/3.text: Then they said to one another: “Come! Let us make bricks and bake them with fire.” So they used bricks instead of stone, and bitumen as mortar.

genesis/11/4.text: They now said: “Come! Let us build a city for ourselves and a tower with its top in the heavens, and let us make a celebrated name for ourselves, so that we will not be scattered over the entire face of the earth.”

genesis/11/5.text: Then Jehovah went down to see the city and the tower that the sons of men had built.

genesis/11/6.text: Jehovah then said: “Look! They are one people with one language, and this is what they have started to do. Now there is nothing that they may have in mind to do that will be impossible for them.

genesis/11/7.text: Come! Let us go down there and confuse their language in order that they may not understand one another’s language.”

genesis/11/8.text: So Jehovah scattered them from there over the entire face of the earth, and they gradually left off building the city.

genesis/11/9.text: That is why it was named Baʹbel, because there Jehovah confused the language of all the earth, and Jehovah scattered them from there over the entire face of the earth.

genesis/11/10.text: This is the history of Shem. Shem was 100 years old when he became father to Ar·pachʹshad two years after the Flood.

genesis/11/11.text: After becoming father to Ar·pachʹshad, Shem continued to live 500 years. And he became father to sons and daughters.

genesis/11/12.text: Ar·pachʹshad lived for 35 years and then became father to Sheʹlah.

genesis/11/13.text: After becoming father to Sheʹlah, Ar·pachʹshad continued to live 403 years. And he became father to sons and daughters.

genesis/11/14.text: Sheʹlah lived for 30 years and then became father to Eʹber.

genesis/11/15.text: After becoming father to Eʹber, Sheʹlah continued to live 403 years. And he became father to sons and daughters.

genesis/11/16.text: Eʹber lived for 34 years and then became father to Peʹleg.

genesis/11/17.text: After becoming father to Peʹleg, Eʹber continued to live 430 years. And he became father to sons and daughters.

genesis/11/18.text: Peʹleg lived for 30 years and then became father to Reʹu.

genesis/11/19.text: After becoming father to Reʹu, Peʹleg continued to live 209 years. And he became father to sons and daughters.

genesis/11/20.text: Reʹu lived for 32 years and then became father to Seʹrug.

genesis/11/21.text: After becoming father to Seʹrug, Reʹu continued to live 207 years. And he became father to sons and daughters.

genesis/11/22.text: Seʹrug lived for 30 years and then became father to Naʹhor.

genesis/11/23.text: After becoming father to Naʹhor, Seʹrug continued to live 200 years. And he became father to sons and daughters.

genesis/11/24.text: Naʹhor lived for 29 years and then became father to Teʹrah.

genesis/11/25.text: After becoming father to Teʹrah, Naʹhor continued to live 119 years. And he became father to sons and daughters.

genesis/11/26.text: Teʹrah lived for 70 years, after which he became father to Aʹbram, Naʹhor, and Haʹran.

genesis/11/27.text: This is the history of Teʹrah. Teʹrah became father to Aʹbram, Naʹhor, and Haʹran; and Haʹran became father to Lot.

genesis/11/28.text: While his father Teʹrah was still alive, Haʹran died in the land of his birth, in Ur of the Chal·deʹans.

genesis/11/29.text: Aʹbram and Naʹhor took wives for themselves. The name of Aʹbram’s wife was Sarʹai, and the name of Naʹhor’s wife was Milʹcah, the daughter of Haʹran, the father of Milʹcah and Isʹcah.

genesis/11/30.text: Now Sarʹai was barren; she had no child.

genesis/11/31.text: Teʹrah then took Aʹbram his son and Lot his grandson, the son of Haʹran, and Sarʹai his daughter-in-law, the wife of Aʹbram his son, and they went with him out of Ur of the Chal·deʹans to go to the land of Caʹnaan. In time they came to Haʹran and began dwelling there.

genesis/11/32.text: The days of Teʹrah were 205 years. Then Teʹrah died in Haʹran.

genesis/10/1.text: 10 This is the history of Noah’s sons, Shem, Ham, and Jaʹpheth. Sons were born to them after the Flood.

genesis/10/2.text: The sons of Jaʹpheth were Goʹmer, Maʹgog, Maʹda·i, Jaʹvan, Tuʹbal, Meʹshech, and Tiʹras.

genesis/10/3.text: The sons of Goʹmer were Ashʹke·naz, Riʹphath, and To·garʹmah.

genesis/10/4.text: The sons of Jaʹvan were E·liʹshah, Tarʹshish, Kitʹtim, and Doʹda·nim.

genesis/10/5.text: From these the inhabitants of the islands spread into their lands, according to their languages and their families and by their nations.

genesis/10/6.text: The sons of Ham were Cush, Mizʹra·im, Put, and Caʹnaan.

genesis/10/7.text: The sons of Cush were Seʹba, Havʹi·lah, Sabʹtah, Raʹa·mah, and Sabʹte·ca. The sons of Raʹa·mah were Sheʹba and Deʹdan.

genesis/10/8.text: Cush became father to Nimʹrod. He was the first to become a mighty one on the earth.

genesis/10/9.text: He became a mighty hunter in opposition to Jehovah. That is why there is a saying: “Just like Nimʹrod, a mighty hunter in opposition to Jehovah.”

genesis/10/10.text: The beginning of his kingdom was Baʹbel, Eʹrech, Acʹcad, and Calʹneh, in the land of Shiʹnar.

genesis/10/11.text: From that land he went into As·syrʹi·a and built Ninʹe·veh, Re·hoʹboth-Ir, Caʹlah,

genesis/10/12.text: and Reʹsen, between Ninʹe·veh and Caʹlah: This is the great city.

genesis/10/13.text: Mizʹra·im became father to Luʹdim, Anʹa·mim, Le·haʹbim, Naph·tuʹhim,

genesis/10/14.text: Path·ruʹsim, Cas·luʹhim (from whom the Phi·lisʹtines came), and Caphʹto·rim.

genesis/10/15.text: Caʹnaan became father to Siʹdon, his firstborn, and Heth,

genesis/10/16.text: as well as the Jebʹu·site, the Amʹor·ite, the Girʹga·shite,

genesis/10/17.text: the Hiʹvite, the Arkʹite, the Siʹnite,

genesis/10/18.text: the Arʹvad·ite, the Zemʹa·rite, and the Haʹmath·ite. Afterward, the families of the Caʹnaan·ites were scattered.

genesis/10/19.text: So the boundary of the Caʹnaan·ites was from Siʹdon as far as Geʹrar, near Gazʹa, as far as Sodʹom, Go·morʹrah, Adʹmah, and Ze·boiʹim, near Laʹsha.

genesis/10/20.text: These were the sons of Ham according to their families and their languages, by their lands and their nations.

genesis/10/21.text: Children were also born to Shem, the forefather of all the sons of Eʹber and the brother of Jaʹpheth the oldest.

genesis/10/22.text: The sons of Shem were Eʹlam, Asʹshur, Ar·pachʹshad, Lud, and Aʹram.

genesis/10/23.text: The sons of Aʹram were Uz, Hul, Geʹther, and Mash.

genesis/10/24.text: Ar·pachʹshad became father to Sheʹlah, and Sheʹlah became father to Eʹber.

genesis/10/25.text: Two sons were born to Eʹber. The name of the one was Peʹleg, because in his lifetime the earth was divided. The name of his brother was Jokʹtan.

genesis/10/26.text: Jokʹtan became father to Al·moʹdad, Sheʹleph, Ha·zar·maʹveth, Jeʹrah,

genesis/10/29.text: Oʹphir, Havʹi·lah, and Joʹbab; all of these were the sons of Jokʹtan.

genesis/10/30.text: Their place of dwelling extended from Meʹsha as far as Seʹphar, the mountainous region of the East.

genesis/10/31.text: These were the sons of Shem according to their families and their languages, by their lands and their nations.

genesis/10/32.text: These were the families of the sons of Noah according to their family lines and by their nations. From these the nations were spread abroad in the earth after the Flood.

genesis/22/1.text: 22 Now after this the true God put Abraham to the test, and he said to him: “Abraham!” to which he replied: “Here I am!”

genesis/22/2.text: Then he said: “Take, please, your son, your only son whom you so love, Isaac, and travel to the land of Mo·riʹah and offer him up there as a burnt offering on one of the mountains that I will designate to you.”

genesis/22/3.text: So Abraham got up early in the morning and saddled his donkey and took two of his servants along with him and his son Isaac. He split the wood for the burnt offering, and then he rose and traveled to the place that the true God indicated to him.

genesis/22/4.text: On the third day, Abraham looked up and saw the place from a distance.

genesis/22/5.text: Abraham now said to his servants: “You stay here with the donkey, but the boy and I will go over there and worship and return to you.”

genesis/22/6.text: So Abraham took the wood for the burnt offering and put it on his son Isaac. Then he took in his hands the fire and the knife, and the two of them walked on together.

genesis/22/7.text: Then Isaac said to his father Abraham: “My father!” He replied: “Yes, my son!” So he continued: “Here are the fire and the wood, but where is the sheep for the burnt offering?”

genesis/22/8.text: To this Abraham said: “God himself will provide the sheep for the burnt offering, my son.” And both of them walked on together.

genesis/22/9.text: Finally they reached the place that the true God had indicated to him, and Abraham built an altar there and arranged the wood on it. He bound his son Isaac hand and foot and put him on the altar on top of the wood.

genesis/22/10.text: Then Abraham reached out his hand and took the knife to kill his son.

genesis/22/11.text: But Jehovah’s angel called to him from the heavens and said: “Abraham, Abraham!” to which he answered: “Here I am!”

genesis/22/12.text: Then he said: “Do not harm the boy, and do not do anything at all to him, for now I do know that you are God-fearing because you have not withheld your son, your only one, from me.”

genesis/22/13.text: At that Abraham looked up, and there just beyond him was a ram caught by its horns in a thicket. So Abraham went and took the ram and offered it up as a burnt offering in place of his son.

genesis/22/14.text: And Abraham named that place Je·hoʹvah-jiʹreh. This is why it is still said today: “In the mountain of Jehovah it will be provided.”

genesis/22/15.text: And Jehovah’s angel called to Abraham a second time from the heavens,

genesis/22/16.text: saying: “‘By myself I swear, ’ declares Jehovah, ‘that because you have done this and you have not withheld your son, your only one,

genesis/22/17.text: I will surely bless you and I will surely multiply your offspring like the stars of the heavens and like the grains of sand on the seashore, and your offspring will take possession of the gate of his enemies.

genesis/22/18.text: And by means of your offspring all nations of the earth will obtain a blessing for themselves because you have listened to my voice.’”

genesis/22/19.text: After that Abraham returned to his servants, and they got up and went back together to Beʹer-sheʹba; and Abraham continued to dwell at Beʹer-sheʹba.

genesis/22/20.text: After this it was reported to Abraham: “Here Milʹcah has also borne sons to Naʹhor your brother:

genesis/22/21.text: Uz his firstborn, Buz his brother, Kem·uʹel the father of Aʹram,

genesis/22/22.text: Cheʹsed, Haʹzo, Pilʹdash, Jidʹlaph, and Be·thuʹel.”

genesis/22/23.text: Be·thuʹel became the father of Re·bekʹah. Milʹcah bore these eight to Naʹhor the brother of Abraham.

genesis/22/24.text: His concubine, whose name was Reuʹmah, also bore sons: Teʹbah, Gaʹham, Taʹhash, and Maʹa·cah.

genesis/25/1.text: 25 Now Abraham again took a wife, and her name was Ke·tuʹrah.

genesis/25/2.text: In time she bore him Zimʹran, Jokʹshan, Meʹdan, Midʹi·an, Ishʹbak, and Shuʹah.

genesis/25/3.text: Jokʹshan became father to Sheʹba and Deʹdan. The sons of Deʹdan were As·shuʹrim, Le·tuʹshim, and Le·umʹmim.

genesis/25/4.text: The sons of Midʹi·an were Eʹphah, Eʹpher, Haʹnoch, A·biʹda, and El·daʹah. All of these were the sons of Ke·tuʹrah.

genesis/25/5.text: Later on Abraham gave everything he had to Isaac,

genesis/25/6.text: but Abraham gave gifts to his sons by his concubines. Then while he was still alive, he sent them eastward, away from Isaac his son, to the land of the East.

genesis/25/7.text: The years of Abraham’s life were 175 years.

genesis/25/8.text: Then Abraham breathed his last and died at a good old age, old and satisfied, and was gathered to his people.

genesis/25/9.text: His sons Isaac and Ishʹma·el buried him in the cave of Mach·peʹlah in the field of Eʹphron the son of Zoʹhar the Hitʹtite that is in front of Mamʹre,

genesis/25/10.text: the field that Abraham had purchased from the sons of Heth. There Abraham was buried, with his wife Sarah.

genesis/25/11.text: After Abraham’s death, God continued to bless his son Isaac, and Isaac was dwelling near Beʹer-laʹhai-roi.

genesis/25/12.text: This is the history of Ishʹma·el the son of Abraham whom Haʹgar the Egyptian, the servant of Sarah, bore to Abraham.

genesis/25/13.text: Now these are the names of the sons of Ishʹma·el, by their names according to their family origins: Ishʹma·el’s firstborn Ne·baʹioth, then Keʹdar, Adʹbe·el, Mibʹsam,

genesis/25/15.text: Haʹdad, Teʹma, Jeʹtur, Naʹphish, and Kedʹe·mah.

genesis/25/16.text: These are the sons of Ishʹma·el, and these are their names by their settlements and by their encampments, 12 chieftains according to their clans.

genesis/25/17.text: And Ishʹma·el lived for 137 years. Then he breathed his last and died and was gathered to his people.

genesis/25/18.text: And they took up dwelling from Havʹi·lah near Shur, which is close to Egypt, as far as As·syrʹi·a. He settled near all his brothers.

genesis/25/19.text: And this is the history of Isaac the son of Abraham. Abraham became father to Isaac.

genesis/25/20.text: Isaac was 40 years old when he married Re·bekʹah, the daughter of Be·thuʹel the A·ra·maeʹan of Padʹdan-aʹram, the sister of Laʹban the A·ra·maeʹan.

genesis/25/21.text: And Isaac kept pleading with Jehovah regarding his wife, because she was barren; so Jehovah responded to his plea, and his wife Re·bekʹah became pregnant.

genesis/25/22.text: And the sons within her began to struggle with each other, so that she said: “If this is the way it is, why should I go on living?” So she inquired of Jehovah.

genesis/25/23.text: And Jehovah said to her: “Two nations are in your womb, and two peoples will be separated from within you; and the one nation will be stronger than the other nation, and the older will serve the younger.”

genesis/25/24.text: When the time came for her to give birth, look! twins were in her womb.

genesis/25/25.text: Then the first came out red all over and was like a garment of hair, so they named him Eʹsau.

genesis/25/26.text: After that his brother came out and his hand was holding onto the heel of Eʹsau, so he named him Jacob. Isaac was 60 years old when she gave birth to them.

genesis/25/27.text: As the boys got bigger, Eʹsau became a skilled hunter, a man of the field, but Jacob was a blameless man, dwelling in tents.

genesis/25/28.text: And Isaac loved Eʹsau because it meant game in his mouth, whereas Re·bekʹah loved Jacob.

genesis/25/29.text: On one occasion Jacob was boiling some stew when Eʹsau returned from the field exhausted.

genesis/25/30.text: So Eʹsau said to Jacob: “Quick, please, give me some of the red stew that you have there, for I am exhausted!” That is why his name was Eʹdom.

genesis/25/31.text: To this Jacob said: “First sell me your right as firstborn!”

genesis/25/32.text: And Eʹsau continued: “Here I am about to die! What use is a birthright to me?”

genesis/25/33.text: And Jacob added: “Swear to me first!” So he swore to him and sold his right as firstborn to Jacob.

genesis/25/34.text: Then Jacob gave Eʹsau bread and lentil stew, and he ate and drank, and he got up and went away. Thus Eʹsau despised the birthright.

genesis/35/1.text: 35 After that God said to Jacob: “Rise, go up to Bethʹel and dwell there, and make an altar there to the true God, who appeared to you when you were running away from Eʹsau your brother.”

genesis/35/2.text: Then Jacob said to his household and to all who were with him: “Get rid of the foreign gods that are in your midst, and cleanse yourselves and change your garments,

genesis/35/3.text: and let us rise and go up to Bethʹel. There I will make an altar to the true God, who answered me in the day of my distress and who has been with me wherever I have gone.”

genesis/35/4.text: So they gave Jacob all the foreign gods they had and the earrings that were in their ears, and Jacob buried them under the big tree that was close to Sheʹchem.

genesis/35/5.text: When they traveled on, the terror of God struck the cities around them, so they did not chase after the sons of Jacob.

genesis/35/6.text: Jacob eventually came to Luz, that is, Bethʹel, in the land of Caʹnaan, he and all the people with him.

genesis/35/7.text: There he built an altar and called the place El-bethʹel, because there the true God had revealed himself to him when he had run away from his brother.

genesis/35/8.text: Later Debʹo·rah, Re·bekʹah’s nurse, died and was buried at the foot of Bethʹel under an oak. So he named it Alʹlon-bacʹuth.

genesis/35/9.text: God appeared to Jacob once again while he was coming from Padʹdan-aʹram and blessed him.

genesis/35/10.text: God said to him: “Your name is Jacob. Your name will no longer be Jacob, but Israel will be your name.” And he began to call him Israel.

genesis/35/11.text: God further said to him: “I am God Almighty. Be fruitful and become many. Nations and a congregation of nations will come from you, and kings will descend from you.

genesis/35/12.text: As for the land that I have given to Abraham and to Isaac, to you I will give it, and to your offspring after you I will give the land.”

genesis/35/13.text: Then God went up from him at the place where he had spoken with him.

genesis/35/14.text: So Jacob set up a pillar in the place where he had spoken with him, a pillar of stone, and he poured a drink offering on it and poured oil on it.

genesis/35/15.text: And Jacob continued to call the place where God had spoken with him Bethʹel.

genesis/35/16.text: Then they pulled away from Bethʹel. And while they were still some distance from Ephʹrath, Rachel began to give birth, and her labor was very difficult.

genesis/35/17.text: But while she was struggling to deliver the child, the midwife said to her: “Do not be afraid, for you will have this son also.”

genesis/35/18.text: Just as her life was slipping away (for she was dying), she named him Ben-oʹni, but his father called him Benjamin.

genesis/35/19.text: So Rachel died and was buried on the way to Ephʹrath, that is, Bethʹle·hem.

genesis/35/20.text: Jacob set up a pillar over her grave; it is the pillar of Rachel’s grave to this day.

genesis/35/21.text: After that Israel pulled away and pitched his tent a distance beyond the tower of Eʹder.

genesis/35/22.text: Once while Israel was dwelling in that land, Reuʹben went and lay down with Bilʹhah his father’s concubine, and Israel heard about it. So there were 12 sons of Jacob.

genesis/35/23.text: The sons by Leʹah were Jacob’s firstborn Reuʹben, then Simʹe·on, Leʹvi, Judah, Isʹsa·char, and Zebʹu·lun.

genesis/35/24.text: The sons by Rachel were Joseph and Benjamin.

genesis/35/25.text: And the sons by Bilʹhah, Rachel’s servant, were Dan and Naphʹta·li.

genesis/35/26.text: And the sons by Zilʹpah, Leʹah’s servant, were Gad and Ashʹer. These are Jacob’s sons, who were born to him in Padʹdan-aʹram.

genesis/35/27.text: Jacob eventually came to where his father Isaac was at Mamʹre, to Kirʹi·ath-arʹba, that is, Hebʹron, where Abraham and also Isaac had resided as foreigners.

genesis/35/28.text: Isaac lived to be 180 years old.

genesis/35/29.text: Then Isaac breathed his last and died and was gathered to his people, after a long and satisfying life; and his sons Eʹsau and Jacob buried him.

genesis/36/1.text: 36 This is the history of Eʹsau, that is, Eʹdom.

genesis/36/2.text: Eʹsau took his wives from the daughters of Caʹnaan: Aʹdah the daughter of Eʹlon the Hitʹtite; and O·hol·i·baʹmah the daughter of Aʹnah, the granddaughter of Zibʹe·on the Hiʹvite;

genesis/36/3.text: and Basʹe·math, Ishʹma·el’s daughter, the sister of Ne·baʹioth.

genesis/36/4.text: And Aʹdah bore Elʹi·phaz to Eʹsau, and Basʹe·math bore Reuʹel,

genesis/36/5.text: and O·hol·i·baʹmah bore Jeʹush, Jaʹlam, and Korʹah. These are the sons of Eʹsau, who were born to him in the land of Caʹnaan.

genesis/36/6.text: After that Eʹsau took his wives, his sons, his daughters, all the members of his household, his herd and all his other beasts, and all the wealth he had accumulated in the land of Caʹnaan and he went to another land some distance away from Jacob his brother.

genesis/36/7.text: For their goods had become too many for them to dwell together, and the land where they were residing was not able to sustain them because of their herds.

genesis/36/8.text: So Eʹsau took up dwelling in the mountainous region of Seʹir. Eʹsau is Eʹdom.

genesis/36/9.text: And this is the history of Eʹsau the father of Eʹdom in the mountainous region of Seʹir.

genesis/36/10.text: These are the names of the sons of Eʹsau: Elʹi·phaz the son of Aʹdah, Eʹsau’s wife; Reuʹel the son of Basʹe·math, Eʹsau’s wife.

genesis/36/11.text: The sons of Elʹi·phaz were Teʹman, Oʹmar, Zeʹpho, Gaʹtam, and Keʹnaz.

genesis/36/12.text: Timʹna became the concubine of Elʹi·phaz, Eʹsau’s son. In time she bore to Elʹi·phaz, Amʹa·lek. These are the sons of Aʹdah, Eʹsau’s wife.

genesis/36/13.text: These are the sons of Reuʹel: Naʹhath, Zeʹrah, Shamʹmah, and Mizʹzah. These were the sons of Basʹe·math, Eʹsau’s wife.

genesis/36/14.text: These were the sons of O·hol·i·baʹmah the daughter of Aʹnah, the granddaughter of Zibʹe·on, Eʹsau’s wife, whom she bore to Eʹsau: Jeʹush, Jaʹlam, and Korʹah.

genesis/36/15.text: These are the sheikhs of the sons of Eʹsau: The sons of Elʹi·phaz, Eʹsau’s firstborn: Sheikh Teʹman, Sheikh Oʹmar, Sheikh Zeʹpho, Sheikh Keʹnaz,

genesis/36/16.text: Sheikh Korʹah, Sheikh Gaʹtam, and Sheikh Amʹa·lek. These are the sheikhs of Elʹi·phaz in the land of Eʹdom. These are the sons by Aʹdah.

genesis/36/17.text: These are the sons of Reuʹel, Eʹsau’s son: Sheikh Naʹhath, Sheikh Zeʹrah, Sheikh Shamʹmah, and Sheikh Mizʹzah. These are the sheikhs of Reuʹel in the land of Eʹdom. These are the sons by Basʹe·math, Eʹsau’s wife.

genesis/36/18.text: Finally these are the sons of O·hol·i·baʹmah, Eʹsau’s wife: Sheikh Jeʹush, Sheikh Jaʹlam, and Sheikh Korʹah. These are the sheikhs of O·hol·i·baʹmah the daughter of Aʹnah, Eʹsau’s wife.

genesis/36/19.text: These are the sons of Eʹsau, and these are their sheikhs. He is Eʹdom.

genesis/36/20.text: These are the sons of Seʹir the Horʹite, the inhabitants of the land: Loʹtan, Shoʹbal, Zibʹe·on, Aʹnah,

genesis/36/21.text: Diʹshon, Eʹzer, and Diʹshan. These are the sheikhs of the Horʹites, the sons of Seʹir, in the land of Eʹdom.

genesis/36/22.text: The sons of Loʹtan were Hoʹri and Heʹmam, and Loʹtan’s sister was Timʹna.

genesis/36/23.text: These are the sons of Shoʹbal: Alʹvan, Manʹa·hath, Eʹbal, Sheʹpho, and Oʹnam.

genesis/36/24.text: These are the sons of Zibʹe·on: Aʹiah and Aʹnah. This is the Aʹnah who found the hot springs in the wilderness while he was tending the donkeys for Zibʹe·on his father.

genesis/36/25.text: These are the children of Aʹnah: Diʹshon and O·hol·i·baʹmah the daughter of Aʹnah.

genesis/36/26.text: These are the sons of Diʹshon: Hemʹdan, Eshʹban, Ithʹran, and Cheʹran.

genesis/36/27.text: These are the sons of Eʹzer: Bilʹhan, Zaʹa·van, and Aʹkan.

genesis/36/28.text: These are the sons of Diʹshan: Uz and Aʹran.

genesis/36/29.text: These are the sheikhs of the Horʹites: Sheikh Loʹtan, Sheikh Shoʹbal, Sheikh Zibʹe·on, Sheikh Aʹnah,

genesis/36/30.text: Sheikh Diʹshon, Sheikh Eʹzer, and Sheikh Diʹshan. These are the sheikhs of the Horʹites according to their sheikhs in the land of Seʹir.

genesis/36/31.text: Now these are the kings who reigned in the land of Eʹdom before any king reigned over the Israelites.

genesis/36/32.text: Beʹla son of Beʹor reigned in Eʹdom, and the name of his city was Dinʹha·bah.

genesis/36/33.text: When Beʹla died, Joʹbab son of Zeʹrah from Bozʹrah began to reign in his place.

genesis/36/34.text: When Joʹbab died, Huʹsham from the land of the Teʹman·ites began to reign in his place.

genesis/36/35.text: When Huʹsham died, Haʹdad son of Beʹdad, who defeated the Midʹi·an·ites in the territory of Moʹab, began to reign in his place, and the name of his city was Aʹvith.

genesis/36/36.text: When Haʹdad died, Samʹlah from Mas·reʹkah began to reign in his place.

genesis/36/37.text: When Samʹlah died, Shaʹul from Re·hoʹboth by the River began to reign in his place.

genesis/36/38.text: When Shaʹul died, Baʹal-haʹnan the son of Achʹbor began to reign in his place.

genesis/36/39.text: When Baʹal-haʹnan the son of Achʹbor died, Haʹdar began to reign in his place. The name of his city was Paʹu, and the name of his wife was Me·hetʹa·bel the daughter of Maʹtred the daughter of Meʹza·hab.

genesis/36/40.text: So these are the names of the sheikhs of Eʹsau according to their families, according to their places, by their names: Sheikh Timʹna, Sheikh Alʹvah, Sheikh Jeʹtheth,

genesis/36/41.text: Sheikh O·hol·i·baʹmah, Sheikh Eʹlah, Sheikh Piʹnon,

genesis/36/42.text: Sheikh Keʹnaz, Sheikh Teʹman, Sheikh Mibʹzar,

genesis/36/43.text: Sheikh Magʹdi·el, and Sheikh Iʹram. These are the sheikhs of Eʹdom according to their settlements in the land of their possession. This is Eʹsau the father of Eʹdom.

genesis/16/1.text: 16 Now Aʹbram’s wife Sarʹai had borne him no children, but she had an Egyptian servant whose name was Haʹgar.

genesis/16/2.text: So Sarʹai said to Aʹbram: “Please now! Jehovah has prevented me from bearing children. Please, have relations with my servant. Perhaps I can have children by means of her.” So Aʹbram listened to what Sarʹai said.

genesis/16/3.text: After Aʹbram had lived for ten years in the land of Caʹnaan, Aʹbram’s wife Sarʹai took her Egyptian servant Haʹgar and gave her to her husband Aʹbram as his wife.

genesis/16/4.text: So he had relations with Haʹgar, and she became pregnant. When she realized that she was pregnant, she began to despise her mistress.

genesis/16/5.text: At this Sarʹai said to Aʹbram: “The injury done to me is your fault. I was the one who put my servant in your arms, but when she realized that she was pregnant, she began to despise me. May Jehovah judge between me and you.”

genesis/16/6.text: So Aʹbram said to Sarʹai: “Look! Your servant is under your authority. Do to her whatever you think is best.” Then Sarʹai humiliated her, and she ran away from her.

genesis/16/7.text: Later Jehovah’s angel found her at a spring of waters in the wilderness, the spring on the way to Shur.

genesis/16/8.text: And he said: “Haʹgar, servant of Sarʹai, where have you come from and where are you going?” To this she said: “I am running away from my mistress Sarʹai.”

genesis/16/9.text: Jehovah’s angel then said to her: “Return to your mistress and humble yourself under her hand.”

genesis/16/10.text: Then Jehovah’s angel said: “I will greatly multiply your offspring, so that they will be too numerous to count.”

genesis/16/11.text: Jehovah’s angel added: “Here you are pregnant, and you will give birth to a son, and you must name him Ishʹma·el, for Jehovah has heard your affliction.

genesis/16/12.text: He will be a wild donkey of a man. His hand will be against everyone, and everyone’s hand will be against him, and he will dwell opposite all his brothers.”

genesis/16/13.text: Then she called on the name of Jehovah, who was speaking to her: “You are a God of sight, ” for she said: “Have I here actually looked upon the one who sees me?”

genesis/16/14.text: That is why the well was called Beʹer-laʹhai-roi. (It is between Kaʹdesh and Beʹred.)

genesis/16/15.text: So Haʹgar bore to Aʹbram a son, and Aʹbram named his son, whom Haʹgar bore, Ishʹma·el.

genesis/16/16.text: Aʹbram was 86 years old when Haʹgar bore Ishʹma·el to him.

genesis/19/1.text: 19 The two angels arrived at Sodʹom by evening, and Lot was sitting in the gate of Sodʹom. When Lot saw them, he got up to meet them and bowed down with his face to the earth.

genesis/19/2.text: And he said: “Please, my lords, turn aside, please, into the house of your servant and stay overnight and have your feet washed. Then you may get up early and travel on your way.” To this they said: “No, we will stay overnight in the public square.”

genesis/19/3.text: But he was so insistent with them that they went with him to his house. Then he made a feast for them, and he baked unleavened bread, and they ate.

genesis/19/4.text: Before they could lie down to sleep, the men of the city—the men of Sodʹom from boy to old man, all of them—surrounded the house in one mob.

genesis/19/5.text: And they kept calling out to Lot and saying to him: “Where are the men who came in to you tonight? Bring them out to us so that we may have sex with them.”

genesis/19/6.text: Then Lot went out to them to the doorway, and he shut the door behind him.

genesis/19/7.text: He said: “Please, my brothers, do not act wickedly.

genesis/19/8.text: Please, here I have two daughters who have never had sexual relations with a man. Please, let me bring them out to you for you to do to them whatever seems good to you. But do not do anything to these men, for they have come under the shelter of my roof.”

genesis/19/9.text: At this they said: “Stand back!” And they added: “This lone foreigner came to live here, and yet he dares to judge us! Now we are going to do worse to you than to them.” And they crowded in on Lot and moved forward to break down the door.

genesis/19/10.text: So the men reached out their hands and brought Lot into the house with them, and they shut the door.

genesis/19/11.text: But they struck the men who were at the entrance of the house with blindness, from the least to the greatest, so that they wore themselves out trying to find the doorway.

genesis/19/12.text: Then the men said to Lot: “Do you have anyone else here? Sons-in-law, your sons, your daughters, and all your people in the city, bring out of this place!

genesis/19/13.text: For we are going to destroy this place, because the outcry against them has indeed grown great before Jehovah, so that Jehovah sent us to destroy the city.”

genesis/19/14.text: So Lot went out and began to speak to his sons-in-law who were to marry his daughters, and he kept saying: “Get up! Get out of this place, because Jehovah will destroy the city!” But to his sons-in-law, he seemed to be joking.

genesis/19/15.text: As dawn was breaking, the angels became urgent with Lot, saying: “Get up! Take your wife and your two daughters who are here with you, so that you will not be swept away in the error of the city!”

genesis/19/16.text: When he kept lingering, then because of Jehovah’s compassion for him, the men seized hold of his hand and the hand of his wife and the hands of his two daughters, and they brought him out and stationed him outside the city.

genesis/19/17.text: As soon as they had brought them to the outskirts, he said: “Escape for your life! Do not look behind you and do not stand still in any part of the district! Escape to the mountainous region so that you may not be swept away!”

genesis/19/18.text: Then Lot said to them: “Not there, please, Jehovah!

genesis/19/19.text: Please, now, your servant has found favor in your eyes and you are showing great kindness to me by preserving me alive, but I am not able to flee to the mountainous region because I am afraid that disaster may overtake me and I will die.

genesis/19/20.text: Please, now, this town is nearby and I can flee there; it is only a small place. May I, please, escape there? It is only a small place. Then I will survive.”

genesis/19/21.text: So he said to him: “Very well, I will also show you consideration by not overthrowing the town you speak of.

genesis/19/22.text: Hurry! Escape there, because I cannot do anything until you arrive there!” That is why he named the town Zoʹar.

genesis/19/23.text: The sun had risen over the land when Lot arrived at Zoʹar.

genesis/19/24.text: Then Jehovah made it rain sulfur and fire on Sodʹom and Go·morʹrah—it came from Jehovah, from the heavens.

genesis/19/25.text: So he overthrew these cities, yes, the entire district, including all the inhabitants of the cities and the plants of the ground.

genesis/19/26.text: But Lot’s wife, who was behind him, began to look back, and she became a pillar of salt.

genesis/19/27.text: Now Abraham got up early in the morning and went to the place where he had stood before Jehovah.

genesis/19/28.text: When he looked down toward Sodʹom and Go·morʹrah and all the land of the district, he saw quite a sight. There was dense smoke rising from the land like the dense smoke of a kiln!

genesis/19/29.text: So when God destroyed the cities of the district, God kept Abraham in mind by sending Lot out from the cities he overthrew, the cities where Lot had been dwelling.

genesis/19/30.text: Later Lot went up from Zoʹar with his two daughters and began living in the mountainous region, because he was afraid to live in Zoʹar. So he began living in a cave with his two daughters.

genesis/19/31.text: And the firstborn said to the younger: “Our father is old, and there is not a man in the land to have relations with us according to the custom of the whole earth.

genesis/19/32.text: Come, let us give our father wine to drink, and let us lie down with him and preserve offspring from our father.”

genesis/19/33.text: So that night they kept giving their father wine to drink; then the firstborn went in and lay down with her father, but he did not know when she lay down and when she got up.

genesis/19/34.text: Then on the next day, the firstborn said to the younger: “Here I lay down with my father last night. Let us give him wine to drink tonight also. Then you go in and lie down with him, and let us preserve offspring from our father.”

genesis/19/35.text: So that night also, they repeatedly gave their father wine to drink; then the younger went and lay down with him, but he did not know when she lay down and when she got up.

genesis/19/36.text: So both daughters of Lot became pregnant by their father.

genesis/19/37.text: The firstborn gave birth to a son and named him Moʹab. He is the father of the Moʹab·ites of today.

genesis/19/38.text: The younger also gave birth to a son, and she named him Ben-amʹmi. He is the father of the Amʹmon·ites of today.

genesis/21/1.text: 21 Jehovah turned his attention to Sarah just as he had said, and Jehovah did for Sarah what he had promised.

genesis/21/2.text: So Sarah became pregnant and then bore a son to Abraham in his old age at the appointed time God had promised him.

genesis/21/3.text: Abraham named his newborn son, whom Sarah bore to him, Isaac.

genesis/21/4.text: And Abraham circumcised his son Isaac when he was eight days old, just as God had commanded him.

genesis/21/5.text: Abraham was 100 years old when his son Isaac was born to him.

genesis/21/6.text: Then Sarah said: “God has brought me laughter; everybody hearing of it will laugh with me.”

genesis/21/7.text: And she added: “Who would have said to Abraham, ‘Sarah will certainly nurse children’? Yet, I have given birth to a son for him in his old age.”

genesis/21/8.text: Now the child grew and was weaned, and Abraham prepared a big feast on the day that Isaac was weaned.

genesis/21/9.text: But Sarah kept noticing that the son of Haʹgar the Egyptian, whom she had borne to Abraham, was mocking Isaac.

genesis/21/10.text: So she said to Abraham: “Drive out this slave girl and her son, for the son of this slave girl is not going to be an heir along with my son, with Isaac!”

genesis/21/11.text: But what she said about his son was very displeasing to Abraham.

genesis/21/12.text: Then God said to Abraham: “Do not be displeased by what Sarah is saying to you about the boy and about your slave girl. Listen to her, for what will be called your offspring will be through Isaac.

genesis/21/13.text: As for the son of the slave girl, I will also make a nation out of him, because he is your offspring.”

genesis/21/14.text: So Abraham got up early in the morning and took bread and a skin bottle of water and gave it to Haʹgar. He set these on her shoulder and then sent her away along with the boy. So she departed and wandered about in the wilderness of Beʹer-sheʹba.

genesis/21/15.text: Finally the water in the skin bottle was used up, and she pushed the boy under one of the bushes.

genesis/21/16.text: Then she went on and sat down by herself, about the distance of a bowshot away, because she said: “I do not want to watch the boy die.” So she sat down at a distance and began to cry aloud and to weep.

genesis/21/17.text: At that God heard the voice of the boy, and God’s angel called to Haʹgar from the heavens and said to her: “What is the matter with you, Haʹgar? Do not be afraid, for God has heard the voice of the boy there where he is.

genesis/21/18.text: Get up, lift the boy and take hold of him with your hand, for I will make him a great nation.”

genesis/21/19.text: Then God opened her eyes and she saw a well of water, and she went and filled the skin bottle with water and gave the boy a drink.

genesis/21/20.text: And God was with the boy as he grew up. He lived in the wilderness and became an archer.

genesis/21/21.text: He took up dwelling in the wilderness of Paʹran, and his mother took a wife for him from the land of Egypt.

genesis/21/22.text: At that time A·bimʹe·lech together with Phiʹcol the chief of his army said to Abraham: “God is with you in everything you are doing.

genesis/21/23.text: So now swear to me here by God that you will not deal falsely with me and with my offspring and with my descendants, and that you will deal with me and with the land where you have been residing with the same loyal love that I have shown you.”

genesis/21/24.text: So Abraham said: “I swear to this.”

genesis/21/25.text: However, Abraham complained to A·bimʹe·lech about the well of water that the servants of A·bimʹe·lech had violently seized.

genesis/21/26.text: A·bimʹe·lech replied: “I do not know who did this; you did not tell me about it, and I heard nothing about it until today.”

genesis/21/27.text: At that Abraham took sheep and cattle and gave them to A·bimʹe·lech, and the two of them made a covenant.

genesis/21/28.text: When Abraham set seven female lambs apart from the flock by themselves,

genesis/21/29.text: A·bimʹe·lech said to Abraham: “Why have you set these seven female lambs here by themselves?”

genesis/21/30.text: Then he said: “You are to accept the seven female lambs from my hand as a witness that I dug this well.”

genesis/21/31.text: That is why he called that place Beʹer-sheʹba, because there both of them had taken an oath.

genesis/21/32.text: So they made a covenant at Beʹer-sheʹba, after which A·bimʹe·lech got up together with Phiʹcol the chief of his army, and they returned to the land of the Phi·lisʹtines.

genesis/21/33.text: After that he planted a tamarisk tree at Beʹer-sheʹba, and there he called on the name of Jehovah, the everlasting God.

genesis/21/34.text: And Abraham stayed in the land of the Phi·lisʹtines for a long time.

genesis/24/1.text: 24 Abraham was now old, advanced in years, and Jehovah had blessed Abraham in everything.

genesis/24/2.text: Abraham said to his servant, the oldest one of his household, who was managing all he had: “Please put your hand under my thigh,

genesis/24/3.text: and I will make you swear by Jehovah, the God of the heavens and the God of the earth, that you will not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Caʹnaan·ites, among whom I am dwelling.

genesis/24/4.text: You must go instead to my country and to my relatives and take a wife for my son, for Isaac.”

genesis/24/5.text: However, the servant said to him: “What if the woman is not willing to come with me to this land? Must I then return your son to the land from which you came?”

genesis/24/6.text: At this Abraham said to him: “See that you do not take my son there.

genesis/24/7.text: Jehovah the God of the heavens, who took me from my father’s house and from the land of my relatives and who spoke with me and swore to me: ‘To your offspring I am going to give this land, ’ he will send his angel ahead of you, and you will certainly take a wife for my son from there.

genesis/24/8.text: But if the woman is unwilling to come with you, you will be free from this oath. But you must not take my son there.”

genesis/24/9.text: With that the servant put his hand under the thigh of Abraham his master and swore to him concerning this matter.

genesis/24/10.text: So the servant took ten of his master’s camels and departed, taking along all sorts of good things from his master. Then he went on his way to Mes·o·po·taʹmi·a, to the city of Naʹhor.

genesis/24/11.text: He had the camels kneel down at a well of water outside the city. It was about evening, the time when the women would go out to draw water.

genesis/24/12.text: Then he said: “Jehovah the God of my master Abraham, please grant me success this day, and show your loyal love to my master Abraham.

genesis/24/13.text: Here I am standing at a spring of water, and the daughters of the men of the city are coming out to draw water.

genesis/24/14.text: May it happen that the young woman to whom I say, ‘Please let down your water jar so that I may take a drink, ’ and who replies, ‘Take a drink, and I will also water your camels, ’ let this be the one you choose for your servant Isaac; and by this let me know that you have shown your loyal love to my master.”

genesis/24/15.text: Even before he finished speaking, Re·bekʹah, who was the daughter of Be·thuʹel the son of Milʹcah the wife of Naʹhor, Abraham’s brother, came out with her water jar on her shoulder.

genesis/24/16.text: Now the young woman was very beautiful, a virgin; no man had had sexual relations with her. She went down to the spring, filled her water jar, and then came back up.

genesis/24/17.text: At once the servant ran to meet her and said: “Please give me a little sip of water from your jar.”

genesis/24/18.text: In turn she said: “Drink, my lord.” With that she quickly lowered her jar upon her hand and gave him a drink.

genesis/24/19.text: When she finished giving him a drink, she said: “I will also draw water for your camels until they are done drinking.”

genesis/24/20.text: So she quickly emptied her jar into the drinking trough and ran again and again to the well to draw water, and she kept drawing water for all his camels.

genesis/24/21.text: The whole time the man silently stared at her in amazement, wondering whether Jehovah had made his trip successful or not.

genesis/24/22.text: When the camels had finished drinking, the man took out for her a gold nose ring weighing a half shekel and two bracelets of gold weighing ten shekels,

genesis/24/23.text: and he said: “Please tell me, whose daughter are you? Is there any room at your father’s house for us to spend the night?”

genesis/24/24.text: At that she said to him: “I am the daughter of Be·thuʹel the son of Milʹcah, whom she bore to Naʹhor.”

genesis/24/25.text: And she added: “We have both straw and much fodder and also a place to spend the night.”

genesis/24/26.text: Then the man bowed down and prostrated himself before Jehovah

genesis/24/27.text: and said: “May Jehovah be praised, the God of my master Abraham, for he has not abandoned his loyal love and his faithfulness toward my master. Jehovah has guided me to the house of the brothers of my master.”

genesis/24/28.text: And the young woman ran to tell her mother’s household about these things.

genesis/24/29.text: Now Re·bekʹah had a brother whose name was Laʹban. So Laʹban ran to the man who was outside at the spring.

genesis/24/30.text: When he saw the nose ring and the bracelets on the hands of his sister and heard the words of his sister Re·bekʹah, who was saying, “This is the way the man spoke to me, ” he came to meet the man, who was still there standing by the camels at the spring.

genesis/24/31.text: At once he said: “Come, you who are blessed by Jehovah. Why do you keep standing out here? I have made the house ready and a place for the camels.”

genesis/24/32.text: With that the man came into the house, and he unharnessed the camels and gave straw and fodder to the camels and water to wash his feet and the feet of the men who were with him.

genesis/24/33.text: However, when something to eat was set before him, he said: “I will not eat until I have told you what I have to say.” So Laʹban said: “Speak!”

genesis/24/34.text: Then he said: “I am Abraham’s servant.

genesis/24/35.text: And Jehovah has blessed my master very much, and he has made him very wealthy by giving him sheep and cattle, silver and gold, male and female servants, and camels and donkeys.

genesis/24/36.text: Further, Sarah the wife of my master bore a son to my master after she grew old, and he will give him everything he has.

genesis/24/37.text: So my master made me swear, saying: ‘You must not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Caʹnaan·ites, in whose land I am dwelling.

genesis/24/38.text: No, but you will go to the house of my father and to my family, and you must take a wife for my son.’

genesis/24/39.text: But I said to my master: ‘What if the woman is unwilling to come with me?’

genesis/24/40.text: He said to me: ‘Jehovah, before whom I have walked, will send his angel with you and will certainly give success to your journey, and you must take a wife for my son from my family and from the house of my father.

genesis/24/41.text: You will be released from your oath to me if you go to my family and they will not give her to you. This will release you from your oath.’

genesis/24/42.text: “When I got to the spring today, I said: ‘Jehovah the God of my master Abraham, if you will make my journey successful,

genesis/24/43.text: here I am standing at a spring. What must take place is that when a young woman comes out to draw water, I will say, “Please, let me drink a little water from your jar, ”

genesis/24/44.text: and she will say to me, “You take a drink, and I will also draw water for your camels.” Let that woman be the one whom Jehovah has chosen for the son of my master.’

genesis/24/45.text: “Before I was finished speaking in my heart, there was Re·bekʹah coming out with her jar on her shoulder, and she made her way down to the spring and began to draw water. Then I said to her: ‘Give me a drink, please.’

genesis/24/46.text: So she quickly lowered her jar from her shoulder and said: ‘Take a drink, and I will also water your camels.’ Then I took a drink, and she also watered the camels.

genesis/24/47.text: After that I asked her, ‘Whose daughter are you?’ to which she replied, ‘The daughter of Be·thuʹel the son of Naʹhor, whom Milʹcah bore to him.’ So I put the ring on her nose and the bracelets on her hands.

genesis/24/48.text: And I bowed down and prostrated myself before Jehovah and praised Jehovah the God of my master Abraham, who had led me on the right path to take the daughter of the brother of my master for his son.

genesis/24/49.text: And now tell me if you wish to show loyal love and faithfulness toward my master; but if not, tell me, so that I may proceed one way or the other.”

genesis/24/50.text: Then Laʹban and Be·thuʹel answered: “This is from Jehovah. We are not able to say yes or no to you.

genesis/24/51.text: Here is Re·bekʹah before you. Take her and go, and let her become a wife to the son of your master, just as Jehovah has spoken.”

genesis/24/52.text: When Abraham’s servant heard their words, he at once bowed down on the ground before Jehovah.

genesis/24/53.text: And the servant began to bring out articles of silver and of gold and garments and to give them to Re·bekʹah, and he gave valuable things to her brother and to her mother.

genesis/24/54.text: After that he and the men with him ate and drank, and they spent the night there. When he got up in the morning, he said: “Send me off to my master.”

genesis/24/55.text: To this her brother and her mother said: “Let the young woman stay with us at least ten days. Then she can go.”

genesis/24/56.text: But he said to them: “Do not detain me, seeing that Jehovah has made my journey successful. Send me off, in order that I may go to my master.”

genesis/24/57.text: So they said: “Let us call the young woman and inquire of her.”

genesis/24/58.text: They called Re·bekʹah and said to her: “Will you go with this man?” She replied: “I am willing to go.”

genesis/24/59.text: So they sent off their sister Re·bekʹah and her nurse and Abraham’s servant and his men.

genesis/24/60.text: And they blessed Re·bekʹah and said to her: “Our sister, may you become thousands times ten thousand, and let your offspring take possession of the gate of those who hate them.”

genesis/24/61.text: Then Re·bekʹah and her female attendants rose, got on the camels, and followed the man. So the servant took Re·bekʹah and went on his way.

genesis/24/62.text: Now Isaac had come from the direction of Beʹer-laʹhai-roi, for he was dwelling in the land of the Negʹeb.

genesis/24/63.text: And Isaac was out walking in the field about nightfall to meditate. When he looked up, why, he saw that camels were coming!

genesis/24/64.text: When Re·bekʹah looked up, she caught sight of Isaac, and she quickly got down from the camel.

genesis/24/65.text: Then she asked the servant: “Who is that man there walking in the field to meet us?” And the servant said: “It is my master.” So she took her veil to cover herself.

genesis/24/66.text: And the servant told Isaac all the things he had done.

genesis/24/67.text: After that Isaac brought her into the tent of Sarah his mother. Thus he took Re·bekʹah as his wife; and he fell in love with her, and Isaac found comfort after the loss of his mother.

genesis/26/1.text: 26 Now there was a famine in the land, in addition to the first famine that occurred in the days of Abraham, so that Isaac went to A·bimʹe·lech king of the Phi·lisʹtines, in Geʹrar.

genesis/26/2.text: Then Jehovah appeared to him and said: “Do not go down to Egypt. Dwell in the land that I designate to you.

genesis/26/3.text: Reside as a foreigner in this land, and I will continue with you and bless you because to you and to your offspring I will give all these lands, and I will carry out the oath that I swore to your father Abraham:

genesis/26/4.text: ‘I will multiply your offspring like the stars of the heavens; and I will give to your offspring all these lands; and by means of your offspring, all nations of the earth will obtain a blessing for themselves, ’

genesis/26/5.text: on account of the fact that Abraham listened to my voice and continued to keep my requirements, my commands, my statutes, and my laws.”

genesis/26/6.text: So Isaac continued to dwell in Geʹrar.

genesis/26/7.text: When the men of the place kept asking about his wife, he would say: “She is my sister.” He was afraid to say, “She is my wife, ” for he said, “The men of the place might kill me because of Re·bekʹah, ” for she was beautiful in appearance.

genesis/26/8.text: After some time had passed, A·bimʹe·lech king of the Phi·lisʹtines was looking out of the window, and he saw Isaac displaying affection for Re·bekʹah his wife.

genesis/26/9.text: At once A·bimʹe·lech called Isaac and said: “She is actually your wife! Why did you say, ‘She is my sister’?” At this Isaac said to him: “I said it for fear I should die because of her.”

genesis/26/10.text: But A·bimʹe·lech continued: “What have you done to us? One of the people could easily have lain down with your wife, and you would have brought guilt upon us!”

genesis/26/11.text: Then A·bimʹe·lech commanded all the people, saying: “Anybody touching this man and his wife will surely be put to death!”

genesis/26/12.text: And Isaac began to sow seed in that land, and in that year he reaped 100 times what he sowed, for Jehovah was blessing him.

genesis/26/13.text: The man became wealthy, and he continued to prosper until he became very wealthy.

genesis/26/14.text: He acquired flocks of sheep and herds of cattle and a large body of servants, and the Phi·lisʹtines began to envy him.

genesis/26/15.text: So the Phi·lisʹtines took soil and stopped up all the wells that his father’s servants had dug in the days of Abraham.

genesis/26/16.text: A·bimʹe·lech then said to Isaac: “Move from our neighborhood, for you have grown far stronger than we are.”

genesis/26/17.text: So Isaac moved from there and encamped in the valley of Geʹrar and began dwelling there.

genesis/26/18.text: And Isaac again dug the wells that had been dug in the days of his father Abraham but that the Phi·lisʹtines had stopped up after Abraham’s death, and he called them by the names that his father had given them.

genesis/26/19.text: When the servants of Isaac were digging in the valley, they found a well of fresh water.

genesis/26/20.text: And the shepherds of Geʹrar began quarreling with the shepherds of Isaac, saying: “The water is ours!” So he named the well Eʹsek, because they had quarreled with him.

genesis/26/21.text: And they started digging another well, and they began quarreling over it also. So he named it Sitʹnah.

genesis/26/22.text: Later he moved away from there and dug another well, but they did not quarrel over it. So he named it Re·hoʹboth and said: “It is because now Jehovah has given us ample room and has made us fruitful in the land.”

genesis/26/23.text: Then he went up from there to Beʹer-sheʹba.

genesis/26/24.text: That night Jehovah appeared to him and said: “I am the God of your father Abraham. Do not be afraid, for I am with you, and I will bless you and multiply your offspring on account of Abraham my servant.”

genesis/26/25.text: So he built an altar there and called on the name of Jehovah. And Isaac pitched his tent there, and his servants dug a well there.

genesis/26/26.text: Later A·bimʹe·lech came to him from Geʹrar with A·huzʹzath his personal adviser and Phiʹcol the chief of his army.

genesis/26/27.text: At this Isaac said to them: “Why have you come to me, seeing that you hated me and sent me away from your neighborhood?”

genesis/26/28.text: To this they said: “We have clearly seen that Jehovah has been with you. So we said, ‘Let there, please, be an oath of obligation between us and you, and let us make a covenant with you

genesis/26/29.text: that you will do nothing bad to us just as we have not harmed you, seeing that we have done only good to you in that we sent you away in peace. You now are the blessed of Jehovah.’”

genesis/26/30.text: Then he made a feast for them, and they ate and drank.

genesis/26/31.text: In the morning they got up early and swore an oath to each other. After that Isaac sent them away, and they went from him in peace.

genesis/26/32.text: On that day the servants of Isaac came and reported to him about the well that they had dug, and they told him: “We have found water!”

genesis/26/33.text: So he named it Shiʹbah. That is why the name of the city is Beʹer-sheʹba to this day.

genesis/26/34.text: When Eʹsau was 40 years old, he took as wife Juʹdith the daughter of Be·eʹri the Hitʹtite and also Basʹe·math the daughter of Eʹlon the Hitʹtite.

genesis/26/35.text: They were a source of great grief to Isaac and Re·bekʹah.

genesis/28/1.text: 28 So Isaac called Jacob and blessed him and commanded him, saying: “You must not take a wife from the daughters of Caʹnaan.

genesis/28/2.text: Go away to Padʹdan-aʹram to the house of Be·thuʹel, your mother’s father, and from there take for yourself a wife from the daughters of Laʹban, your mother’s brother.

genesis/28/3.text: God Almighty will bless you and make you fruitful and multiply you, and you will certainly become a congregation of peoples.

genesis/28/4.text: And he will give to you the blessing of Abraham, to you and to your offspring with you, so that you may take possession of the land where you have been living as a foreigner, which God has given to Abraham.”

genesis/28/5.text: So Isaac sent Jacob away, and he departed for Padʹdan-aʹram, to Laʹban the son of Be·thuʹel the A·ra·maeʹan, the brother of Re·bekʹah, the mother of Jacob and Eʹsau.

genesis/28/6.text: Eʹsau saw that Isaac had blessed Jacob and had sent him away to Padʹdan-aʹram to take a wife from there and that when he blessed him, he commanded him, “Do not take a wife from the daughters of Caʹnaan, ”

genesis/28/7.text: and that Jacob obeyed his father and his mother and departed for Padʹdan-aʹram.

genesis/28/8.text: Eʹsau then realized that the daughters of Caʹnaan were displeasing to his father Isaac,

genesis/28/9.text: so Eʹsau went to Ishʹma·el and took as wife Maʹha·lath the daughter of Abraham’s son Ishʹma·el, the sister of Ne·baʹioth, in addition to the other wives he already had.

genesis/28/10.text: Jacob departed from Beʹer-sheʹba and kept going toward Haʹran.

genesis/28/11.text: In time he came to a place and prepared to spend the night there because the sun had set. So he took one of the stones of that place and set it to rest his head on and lay down there.

genesis/28/12.text: Then he had a dream, and look! there was a stairway set on the earth, and its top reached up to the heavens; and there were God’s angels ascending and descending on it.

genesis/28/13.text: And look! there was Jehovah stationed above it, and he said: “I am Jehovah the God of Abraham your father and the God of Isaac. The land on which you are lying, to you I am going to give it and to your offspring.

genesis/28/14.text: And your offspring will certainly become like the dust particles of the earth, and you will spread abroad to the west and to the east and to the north and to the south, and by means of you and by means of your offspring all the families of the ground will certainly be blessed.

genesis/28/15.text: I am with you, and I will safeguard you wherever you go, and I will return you to this land. I will not leave you until I have done what I have promised you.”

genesis/28/16.text: Then Jacob awoke from his sleep and said: “Truly Jehovah is in this place, and I did not know it.”

genesis/28/17.text: And he grew fearful and added: “How awe-inspiring this place is! This can only be the house of God, and this is the gate of the heavens.”

genesis/28/18.text: So Jacob got up early in the morning and took the stone on which he had rested his head and set it up as a pillar and poured oil on top of it.

genesis/28/19.text: So he named that place Bethʹel, but previously the city’s name was Luz.

genesis/28/20.text: Jacob then made a vow, saying: “If God will continue with me and will protect me on my journey and will give me bread to eat and garments to wear

genesis/28/21.text: and I return in peace to the house of my father, then Jehovah will certainly have proved to be my God.

genesis/28/22.text: And this stone that I have set up as a pillar will become a house of God, and without fail I will give you a tenth of everything you give to me.”

genesis/34/1.text: 34 Now Diʹnah, Jacob’s daughter by Leʹah, used to go out to spend time with the young women of the land.

genesis/34/2.text: When Sheʹchem, the son of Haʹmor the Hiʹvite, a chieftain of the land, saw her, he took her and lay down with her and violated her.

genesis/34/3.text: And he became very attached to Diʹnah, the daughter of Jacob, and he fell in love with the young woman and spoke persuasively to her.

genesis/34/4.text: Finally Sheʹchem said to Haʹmor his father: “Get me this young woman to be my wife.”

genesis/34/5.text: When Jacob heard that he had defiled Diʹnah his daughter, his sons were with his herd in the field. So Jacob kept silent until they returned.

genesis/34/6.text: Later Haʹmor, Sheʹchem’s father, went out to speak with Jacob.

genesis/34/7.text: But the sons of Jacob heard about it and returned from the field right away. They were offended and very angry because he had disgraced Israel by lying down with Jacob’s daughter, something that should not be done.

genesis/34/8.text: Haʹmor spoke with them, saying: “My son Sheʹchem longs for your daughter. Please give her to him as his wife,

genesis/34/9.text: and form marriage alliances with us. Give us your daughters, and take our daughters for yourselves.

genesis/34/10.text: You may dwell with us, and the land will become available for you. Dwell and carry on trade in it and settle in it.”

genesis/34/11.text: Then Sheʹchem said to her father and to her brothers: “Let me find favor in your eyes, and I will give you whatever you ask me.

genesis/34/12.text: You can demand from me a very high bride price and gift. I am willing to give whatever you may say to me. Just give me the young woman as a wife.”

genesis/34/13.text: And Jacob’s sons answered Sheʹchem and Haʹmor his father deceitfully because he had defiled Diʹnah their sister.

genesis/34/14.text: They said to them: “We cannot possibly do such a thing, to give our sister to a man who is not circumcised, for that is a disgrace to us.

genesis/34/15.text: We can only consent on this condition: that you become like us and circumcise all your males.

genesis/34/16.text: Then we will give our daughters to you, and we will take your daughters for ourselves, and we will dwell with you and become one people.

genesis/34/17.text: But if you do not listen to us and get circumcised, then we will take our daughter and go.”

genesis/34/18.text: Their words pleased Haʹmor and Sheʹchem, Haʹmor’s son.

genesis/34/19.text: The young man did not delay in doing what they asked, because he found delight in Jacob’s daughter, and he was the most honorable of the whole house of his father.

genesis/34/20.text: So Haʹmor and his son Sheʹchem went to the city gate and spoke to the men of their city, saying:

genesis/34/21.text: “These men wish to be at peace with us. Let them dwell in the land and carry on trade in it, for the land is large enough to accommodate them. We can take their daughters as wives, and our daughters we can give to them.

genesis/34/22.text: Only on this one condition will the men consent to dwell with us in order to become one people: that every male among us be circumcised just the way they are circumcised.

genesis/34/23.text: Then, will not their possessions, their wealth, and all their livestock be ours? So let us give them our consent that they may dwell with us.”

genesis/34/24.text: All those going out by the gate of his city listened to Haʹmor and to his son Sheʹchem, and all the males got circumcised, all those going out of the city gate.

genesis/34/25.text: However, on the third day, when they were still in pain, two sons of Jacob, Simʹe·on and Leʹvi, Diʹnah’s brothers, each took his sword and went into the unsuspecting city and killed every male.

genesis/34/26.text: They killed Haʹmor and his son Sheʹchem with the sword and then took Diʹnah from Sheʹchem’s house and left.

genesis/34/27.text: Jacob’s other sons came upon the slain men and plundered the city because they had defiled their sister.

genesis/34/28.text: They took their flocks, their herds, their donkeys, and whatever was in the city and in the field.

genesis/34/29.text: They also took all their possessions, captured all their little children and their wives, and plundered everything in the houses.

genesis/34/30.text: At this Jacob said to Simʹe·on and to Leʹvi: “You have brought great trouble on me in making me a stench to the inhabitants of the land, to the Caʹnaan·ites and the Perʹiz·zites. I am few in number, and they will certainly gather together to attack me and I will be annihilated, I and my house.”

genesis/34/31.text: But they said: “Should anyone treat our sister like a prostitute?”

genesis/37/1.text: 37 Jacob continued to dwell in the land of Caʹnaan, where his father had lived as a foreigner.

genesis/37/2.text: This is the history of Jacob. When Joseph was 17 years old, the young man was tending the flock with the sons of Bilʹhah and the sons of Zilʹpah, the wives of his father. And Joseph brought a bad report about them to their father.

genesis/37/3.text: Now Israel loved Joseph more than all his other sons because he was the son of his old age, and he had a special robe made for him.

genesis/37/4.text: When his brothers saw that their father loved him more than all his brothers, they began to hate him, and they could not speak peaceably to him.

genesis/37/5.text: Later Joseph had a dream and told it to his brothers, and they found further reason to hate him.

genesis/37/6.text: He said to them: “Please listen to this dream that I had.

genesis/37/7.text: There we were binding sheaves in the middle of the field when my sheaf got up and stood erect and your sheaves encircled and bowed down to my sheaf.”

genesis/37/8.text: His brothers said to him: “Are you really going to make yourself king over us and dominate us?” So they found another reason to hate him, because of his dreams and what he said.

genesis/37/9.text: After that he had still another dream, and he related it to his brothers: “I have had another dream. This time the sun and the moon and 11 stars were bowing down to me.”

genesis/37/10.text: Then he related it to his father as well as his brothers, and his father rebuked him and said to him: “What is the meaning of this dream of yours? Am I as well as your mother and your brothers really going to come and bow down to the earth to you?”

genesis/37/11.text: And his brothers grew jealous of him, but his father kept the saying in mind.

genesis/37/12.text: His brothers now went to pasture their father’s flock near Sheʹchem.

genesis/37/13.text: Israel later said to Joseph: “Your brothers are tending flocks near Sheʹchem, are they not? Come, and let me send you to them.” At this he said to him: “I am ready!”

genesis/37/14.text: So he said to him: “Go, please, and see whether your brothers are well. See how the flock is, and bring word back to me.” With that he sent him away from the valley of Hebʹron, and he went on toward Sheʹchem.

genesis/37/15.text: Later a man found him as he was wandering in a field. The man asked him: “What are you looking for?”

genesis/37/16.text: To this he said: “I am looking for my brothers. Please tell me, where are they tending flocks?”

genesis/37/17.text: The man continued: “They have pulled away from here, for I heard them saying, ‘Let us go to Doʹthan.’” So Joseph went after his brothers and found them at Doʹthan.

genesis/37/18.text: Now they caught sight of him from a distance, and before he reached them, they began plotting against him to put him to death.

genesis/37/19.text: So they said to one another: “Look! Here comes that dreamer.

genesis/37/20.text: Come, now, let us kill him and pitch him into one of the waterpits, and we will say that a vicious wild animal devoured him. Then let us see what will become of his dreams.”

genesis/37/21.text: When Reuʹben heard this, he tried to rescue him from them. So he said: “Let us not take his life.”

genesis/37/22.text: Reuʹben said to them: “Do not shed blood. Throw him into this waterpit in the wilderness, but do not harm him.” His purpose was to rescue him from them in order to return him to his father.

genesis/37/23.text: So as soon as Joseph came to his brothers, they stripped Joseph of his robe, the special robe that he wore,
