genesis/37/24.text: and they took him and threw him into the waterpit. At the time the pit was empty; there was no water in it.

genesis/37/25.text: Then they sat down to eat. When they looked up, there was a caravan of Ishʹma·el·ites coming from Gilʹe·ad. Their camels were carrying labdanum gum, balsam, and resinous bark, and they were on their way down to Egypt.

genesis/37/26.text: At this Judah said to his brothers: “What profit would there be if we killed our brother and covered over his blood?

genesis/37/27.text: Come, now, let us sell him to the Ishʹma·el·ites, and do not let our hand be upon him. After all, he is our brother, our flesh.” So they listened to their brother.

genesis/37/28.text: And when the Midʹi·an·ite merchants were passing by, they lifted Joseph up out of the waterpit and sold him to the Ishʹma·el·ites for 20 pieces of silver. These men took Joseph into Egypt.

genesis/37/29.text: Later when Reuʹben returned to the waterpit and saw that Joseph was not in the waterpit, he ripped his garments apart.

genesis/37/30.text: When he returned to his brothers, he exclaimed: “The child is gone! And I—what am I going to do?”

genesis/37/31.text: So they took Joseph’s robe and slaughtered a male goat and dipped the robe in the blood.

genesis/37/32.text: After that they sent the special robe to their father and said: “This is what we found. Please examine whether this is your son’s robe or not.”

genesis/37/33.text: Then he examined it and exclaimed: “It is my son’s robe! A vicious wild animal must have devoured him! Joseph is surely torn to pieces!”

genesis/37/34.text: With that Jacob ripped his garments apart and put sackcloth around his waist and mourned his son for many days.

genesis/37/35.text: And all his sons and all his daughters kept trying to comfort him, but he kept refusing to take comfort, saying: “I will go down into the Grave mourning my son!” And his father continued weeping for him.

genesis/37/36.text: Now the Midʹi·an·ites sold him in Egypt to Potʹi·phar, a court official of Pharʹaoh and the chief of the guard.

genesis/41/1.text: 41 At the end of two full years, Pharʹaoh dreamed that he was standing by the Nile River.

genesis/41/2.text: And there, coming up from the river, were seven fine-looking, fat cows, and they were feeding on the Nile grass.

genesis/41/3.text: There were seven other cows that looked ugly and thin coming up after them from the Nile, and they stood alongside the fat cows by the bank of the Nile.

genesis/41/4.text: Then the ugly, thin cows began to eat up the seven fine-looking, fat cows. At this Pharʹaoh woke up.

genesis/41/5.text: Then he went back to sleep and had a second dream. There were seven ears of grain coming up on one stalk, full and choice.

genesis/41/6.text: And growing up after them were seven ears of grain that were thin and scorched by the east wind.

genesis/41/7.text: And the thin ears of grain began to swallow up the seven full and choice ears of grain. At this Pharʹaoh woke up and realized that it was a dream.

genesis/41/8.text: But in the morning, his spirit became agitated. So he sent for all the magic-practicing priests of Egypt and all her wise men. Pharʹaoh related his dreams to them, but there was no one who could interpret them for Pharʹaoh.

genesis/41/9.text: At that the chief cupbearer spoke with Pharʹaoh, saying: “I am confessing my sins today.

genesis/41/10.text: Pharʹaoh was indignant at his servants. So he committed me to the jail of the house of the chief of the guard, both me and the chief baker.

genesis/41/11.text: After that we each had a dream on the same night. He and I each had a dream with its own interpretation.

genesis/41/12.text: And there with us was a young Hebrew man, a servant of the chief of the guard. When we related them to him, he interpreted for us the meaning of each dream.

genesis/41/13.text: It happened exactly as he had interpreted to us. I was restored to my office, but the other man was hanged.”

genesis/41/14.text: So Pharʹaoh sent for Joseph, and they brought him quickly from the prison. He shaved and changed his clothes and went in to Pharʹaoh.

genesis/41/15.text: Then Pharʹaoh said to Joseph: “I had a dream, but there is no one to interpret it. Now I have heard it said about you that you can hear a dream and interpret it.”

genesis/41/16.text: At this Joseph answered Pharʹaoh: “I need not be considered! God will speak concerning Pharʹaoh’s welfare.”

genesis/41/17.text: Pharʹaoh went on to say to Joseph: “In my dream I was standing on the bank of the Nile River.

genesis/41/18.text: And there, coming up from the Nile, were seven fine-looking, fat cows, and they began to feed on the Nile grass.

genesis/41/19.text: And there were seven other cows coming up after them, poor and very bad-looking and thin. I have never seen such bad-looking cows in all the land of Egypt.

genesis/41/20.text: And the skinny, bad cows began to eat up the first seven fat cows.

genesis/41/21.text: But when they had consumed them, no one could have known that they had done so, since their appearance was just as bad as at the start. At that I woke up.

genesis/41/22.text: “After that I saw in my dream seven ears of grain coming up on one stalk, full and choice.

genesis/41/23.text: Growing up after them were seven ears of shriveled grain, thin and scorched by the east wind.

genesis/41/24.text: Then the thin ears of grain began to swallow up the seven choice ears of grain. So I told it to the magic-practicing priests, but there was no one who could explain it to me.”

genesis/41/25.text: Then Joseph said to Pharʹaoh: “The dreams of Pharʹaoh are one and the same. The true God has told to Pharʹaoh what He will do.

genesis/41/26.text: The seven good cows are seven years. Likewise, the seven good ears of grain are seven years. The dreams are one and the same.

genesis/41/27.text: The seven skinny and bad cows that came up after them are seven years, and the seven empty ears of grain, scorched by the east wind, will prove to be seven years of famine.

genesis/41/28.text: This is just as I told to Pharʹaoh: The true God has caused Pharʹaoh to see what He will do.

genesis/41/29.text: “There are to be seven years of great abundance in all the land of Egypt.

genesis/41/30.text: But seven years of famine will certainly arise after them, and all the abundance in the land of Egypt will certainly be forgotten, and the famine will exhaust the land.

genesis/41/31.text: And the previous abundance in the land will not be remembered because of the famine afterward, for it will be very severe.

genesis/41/32.text: The dream was given twice to Pharʹaoh because the matter has been firmly established by the true God, and the true God will soon carry it out.

genesis/41/33.text: “So now let Pharʹaoh look for a man who is discreet and wise and place him over the land of Egypt.

genesis/41/34.text: Let Pharʹaoh take action and appoint overseers in the land, and he should collect one fifth of the produce of Egypt during the seven years of abundance.

genesis/41/35.text: And let them collect all the food during these coming good years, and let them stockpile grain under Pharʹaoh’s authority as food to be stored in the cities and safeguarded there.

genesis/41/36.text: The food should serve as a supply for the land for the seven years of famine that will occur in the land of Egypt, so that the land may not perish in the famine.”

genesis/41/37.text: This proposal seemed good to Pharʹaoh and all his servants.

genesis/41/38.text: So Pharʹaoh said to his servants: “Can another man be found like this one in whom there is the spirit of God?”

genesis/41/39.text: Pharʹaoh then said to Joseph: “Since God has caused you to know all of this, there is no one as discreet and wise as you.

genesis/41/40.text: You will personally be over my house, and all my people will obey you implicitly. Only in my role as king will I be greater than you.”

genesis/41/41.text: And Pharʹaoh added to Joseph: “See, I am putting you over all the land of Egypt.”

genesis/41/42.text: Then Pharʹaoh removed his signet ring from his own hand and put it on Joseph’s hand and clothed him with garments of fine linen and placed a necklace of gold around his neck.

genesis/41/43.text: Moreover, he had him ride in the second chariot of honor that he had, and they would call out ahead of him, “A·vrékh!” Thus he put him over all the land of Egypt.

genesis/41/44.text: Pharʹaoh further said to Joseph: “I am Pharʹaoh, but without your authorization, no man may do a single thing in all the land of Egypt.”

genesis/41/45.text: After that Pharʹaoh gave Joseph the name Zaphʹe·nath-pa·neʹah and gave him Asʹe·nath the daughter of Pot·iʹphe·ra the priest of On as a wife. And Joseph began to oversee the land of Egypt.

genesis/41/46.text: Joseph was 30 years old when he stood before Pharʹaoh king of Egypt. Then Joseph went out from before Pharʹaoh and traveled throughout all the land of Egypt.

genesis/41/47.text: And during the seven years of abundance, the land went on producing plentifully.

genesis/41/48.text: And he kept collecting all the food of the seven years from the land of Egypt, and he would stockpile the food in the cities. In each city he would store the food from the fields around it.

genesis/41/49.text: Joseph continued stockpiling grain in very great quantity, like the sand of the sea, until finally they gave up measuring it because it could not be measured.

genesis/41/50.text: Before the year of the famine arrived, two sons were born to Joseph, whom Asʹe·nath the daughter of Pot·iʹphe·ra the priest of On bore to him.

genesis/41/51.text: Joseph named the firstborn Ma·nasʹseh, for he said, “God has made me forget all my trouble and all the house of my father.”

genesis/41/52.text: And he named the second one Eʹphra·im, for he said, “God has made me fruitful in the land of my affliction.”

genesis/41/53.text: Then the seven years of abundance in the land of Egypt ended,

genesis/41/54.text: and the seven years of famine began, just as Joseph had said. The famine developed in all the lands, but in all the land of Egypt there was bread.

genesis/41/55.text: Eventually, all the land of Egypt suffered from the famine, and the people began to cry to Pharʹaoh for bread. Then Pharʹaoh said to all the Egyptians: “Go to Joseph, and do whatever he tells you.”

genesis/41/56.text: The famine continued over all the surface of the earth. Then Joseph began to open up all the granaries that were among them and to sell to the Egyptians, as the famine had a strong grip on the land of Egypt.

genesis/41/57.text: Moreover, people of all the earth came to Egypt to buy from Joseph, because the famine had a strong grip on all the earth.

exodus/2/1.text: 2 About that time, a certain man of the house of Leʹvi married a daughter of Leʹvi.

exodus/2/2.text: And the woman became pregnant and gave birth to a son. When she saw how beautiful he was, she kept him concealed for three months.

exodus/2/3.text: When she was no longer able to conceal him, she took a papyrus basket and coated it with bitumen and pitch and put the child in it and placed it among the reeds by the bank of the Nile River.

exodus/2/4.text: But his sister stood at a distance to see what would happen to him.

exodus/2/5.text: When Pharʹaoh’s daughter came down to bathe in the Nile, her female attendants were walking by the side of the Nile. And she caught sight of the basket in the middle of the reeds. She immediately sent her slave girl to get it.

exodus/2/6.text: When she opened it, she saw the child, and the boy was crying. She felt compassion for him, but she said: “This is one of the children of the Hebrews.”

exodus/2/7.text: Then his sister said to Pharʹaoh’s daughter: “Shall I go and call a nursing woman from the Hebrews to nurse the child for you?”

exodus/2/8.text: Pharʹaoh’s daughter said to her: “Go!” At once the girl went and called the child’s mother.

exodus/2/9.text: Pharʹaoh’s daughter then said to her: “Take this child with you and nurse him for me, and I will pay you.” So the woman took the child and nursed him.

exodus/2/10.text: When the child grew older, she brought him to Pharʹaoh’s daughter, and he became a son to her. She named him Moses and said: “It is because I have drawn him out of the water.”

exodus/2/11.text: Now in those days, after Moses had become an adult, he went out to his brothers to look at the burdens they were bearing, and he caught sight of an Egyptian beating a Hebrew, one of his brothers.

exodus/2/12.text: So he looked this way and that, and seeing no one, he killed the Egyptian and hid him in the sand.

exodus/2/13.text: But he went out on the following day, and there were two Hebrew men fighting with each other. So he said to the one in the wrong: “Why do you strike your companion?”

exodus/2/14.text: At this he said: “Who appointed you as a prince and a judge over us? Are you planning to kill me just as you killed the Egyptian?” Moses now was afraid and said: “Surely the matter has become known!”

exodus/2/15.text: Then Pharʹaoh heard about it, and he attempted to kill Moses; but Moses ran away from Pharʹaoh and went to dwell in the land of Midʹi·an, and he sat down by a well.

exodus/2/16.text: Now the priest of Midʹi·an had seven daughters, and these came to draw water and to fill the troughs to water their father’s flock.

exodus/2/17.text: But as usual, the shepherds came and drove them away. At this Moses got up and helped the women and watered their flock.

exodus/2/18.text: When they came home to their father Reuʹel, he exclaimed: “How is it that you have come home so quickly today?”

exodus/2/19.text: They replied: “A certain Egyptian rescued us from the shepherds, and he even drew water for us and watered the flock.”

exodus/2/20.text: He said to his daughters: “But where is he? Why did you leave the man behind? Call him, so that he may eat with us.”

exodus/2/21.text: After that Moses consented to stay with the man, and he gave his daughter Zip·poʹrah to Moses in marriage.

exodus/2/22.text: Later she bore a son, and he named him Gerʹshom, for he said, “I have become a foreign resident in a foreign land.”

exodus/2/23.text: After a long time, the king of Egypt died, but the Israelites continued to groan because of the slavery and to cry out in complaint, and their cry for help because of the slavery kept going up to the true God.

exodus/2/24.text: In time God heard their groaning, and God remembered his covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

exodus/2/25.text: So God looked on the Israelites; and God took notice.

exodus/17/1.text: 17 The entire assembly of the Israelites departed from the wilderness of Sin by stages according to the order of Jehovah, and they camped at Rephʹi·dim. But there was no water for the people to drink.

exodus/17/2.text: So the people began quarreling with Moses and saying: “Give us water to drink.” But Moses said to them: “Why are you quarreling with me? Why do you keep putting Jehovah to the test?”

exodus/17/3.text: But the people were very thirsty for water there, and they kept murmuring against Moses and saying: “Why have you brought us up out of Egypt to kill us and our sons and our livestock with thirst?”

exodus/17/4.text: Finally Moses cried out to Jehovah: “What should I do with this people? A little longer and they will stone me!”

exodus/17/5.text: Then Jehovah said to Moses: “Go ahead of the people, and take with you some of the elders of Israel and your rod with which you struck the Nile River. Take it in your hand and walk on.

exodus/17/6.text: Look! I will be standing before you there on the rock in Horʹeb. You must strike the rock, and water will come out of it, and the people will drink it.” Moses did so before the eyes of the elders of Israel.

exodus/17/7.text: So he named the place Masʹsah and Merʹi·bah because of the quarreling of the Israelites and because they put Jehovah to the test by saying: “Is Jehovah in our midst or not?”

exodus/17/8.text: Then the A·malʹek·ites came and fought against Israel in Rephʹi·dim.

exodus/17/9.text: At this Moses said to Joshua: “Choose men for us and go out to fight against the A·malʹek·ites. Tomorrow I will stand on top of the hill, with the rod of the true God in my hand.”

exodus/17/10.text: Then Joshua did just as Moses told him, and he fought against the A·malʹek·ites. And Moses, Aaron, and Hur went up to the top of the hill.

exodus/17/11.text: As long as Moses kept his hands lifted up, the Israelites prevailed, but as soon as he would let down his hands, the A·malʹek·ites prevailed.

exodus/17/12.text: When the hands of Moses were heavy, they took a stone and put it under him, and he sat on it. Then Aaron and Hur, one on each side, supported his hands, so that his hands remained steady until the sun set.

exodus/17/13.text: Thus Joshua defeated Amʹa·lek and his people with the sword.

exodus/17/14.text: Jehovah now said to Moses: “Write this as a memorial in the book and repeat it to Joshua, ‘I will completely wipe out the memory of Amʹa·lek from under the heavens.’”

exodus/17/15.text: Then Moses built an altar and named it Je·hoʹvah-nisʹsi,

exodus/17/16.text: saying: “Because his hand is against the throne of Jah, Jehovah will have war with Amʹa·lek from generation to generation.”

numbers/13/1.text: 13 Jehovah now spoke to Moses, saying:

numbers/13/2.text: “Send out men to spy out the land of Caʹnaan, which I am giving to the Israelites. You are to send out one man from each ancestral tribe, each one a chieftain among them.”

numbers/13/3.text: So Moses sent them out from the wilderness of Paʹran at the order of Jehovah. All the men were heads of the Israelites.

numbers/13/4.text: These are their names: of the tribe of Reuʹben, Sham·muʹa the son of Zacʹcur;

numbers/13/5.text: of the tribe of Simʹe·on, Shaʹphat the son of Hoʹri;

numbers/13/6.text: of the tribe of Judah, Caʹleb the son of Je·phunʹneh;

numbers/13/7.text: of the tribe of Isʹsa·char, Iʹgal the son of Joseph;

numbers/13/8.text: of the tribe of Eʹphra·im, Ho·sheʹa the son of Nun;

numbers/13/9.text: of the tribe of Benjamin, Palʹti the son of Raʹphu;

numbers/13/10.text: of the tribe of Zebʹu·lun, Gadʹdi·el the son of Soʹdi;

numbers/13/11.text: of the tribe of Joseph, for the tribe of Ma·nasʹseh, Gadʹdi the son of Suʹsi;

numbers/13/12.text: of the tribe of Dan, Amʹmi·el the son of Ge·malʹli;

numbers/13/13.text: of the tribe of Ashʹer, Seʹthur the son of Miʹcha·el;

numbers/13/14.text: of the tribe of Naphʹta·li, Nahʹbi the son of Vophʹsi;

numbers/13/15.text: of the tribe of Gad, Geuʹel the son of Maʹchi.

numbers/13/16.text: These are the names of the men whom Moses sent to spy out the land. And Moses gave the name Joshua to Ho·sheʹa the son of Nun.

numbers/13/17.text: When Moses was sending them to spy out the land of Caʹnaan, he said to them: “Go up there into the Negʹeb, and then go up into the mountainous region.

numbers/13/18.text: You must see what kind of land it is and whether the people who are dwelling in it are strong or weak, few or many,

numbers/13/19.text: and whether the land is good or bad and whether the cities they are dwelling in are encampments or fortifications.

numbers/13/20.text: And find out whether the land is rich or poor and whether there are trees in it or not. You must be courageous and take some of the fruitage of the land.” Now it was the season of the first ripe grapes.

numbers/13/21.text: So they went up and spied out the land from the wilderness of Zin to Reʹhob, near Leʹbo-haʹmath.

numbers/13/22.text: When they went up into the Negʹeb, they came to Hebʹron, where A·hiʹman, Sheʹshai, and Talʹmai, the Anʹa·kim, were living. Incidentally, Hebʹron had been built seven years before Zoʹan of Egypt.

numbers/13/23.text: When they came to the Valley of Eshʹcol, there they cut down a branch with one cluster of grapes, which two of the men had to carry on a bar, as well as some of the pomegranates and figs.

numbers/13/24.text: They called that place the Valley of Eshʹcol because of the cluster that the Israelites cut down from there.

numbers/13/25.text: At the end of 40 days, they returned from spying out the land.

numbers/13/26.text: So they came back to Moses and Aaron and all the assembly of the Israelites in the wilderness of Paʹran, at Kaʹdesh. They brought back a report to all the assembly and showed them the fruitage of the land.

numbers/13/27.text: This is what they reported to Moses: “We entered the land into which you sent us, and it is indeed flowing with milk and honey, and this is its fruitage.

numbers/13/28.text: Nevertheless, the people who dwell in the land are strong, and the fortified cities are very great. We also saw the Anʹa·kim there.

numbers/13/29.text: The A·malʹek·ites are dwelling in the land of the Negʹeb, and the Hitʹtites, the Jebʹu·sites, and the Amʹor·ites are dwelling in the mountainous region, and the Caʹnaan·ites are dwelling by the sea and along the Jordan.”

numbers/13/30.text: Then Caʹleb tried to calm the people as they stood before Moses by saying: “Let us go up immediately, and we are sure to take possession of it, because we can surely conquer it.”

numbers/13/31.text: But the men who went up with him said: “We are not able to go up against the people, because they are stronger than we are.”

numbers/13/32.text: And they kept on giving the Israelites a bad report about the land that they had spied out, saying: “The land that we passed through to spy out is a land that devours its inhabitants, and all the people whom we saw in it are men of extraordinary size.

numbers/13/33.text: And there we saw the Nephʹi·lim, the sons of Aʹnak, who are from the Nephʹi·lim, and in comparison we seemed like grasshoppers, both to us and to them.”

judges/3/1.text: 3 These are the nations that Jehovah allowed to remain so that they could test all those of Israel who had not experienced any of the wars of Caʹnaan

judges/3/2.text: (this was so that succeeding generations of Israelites would experience war, those who had not experienced such things before):

judges/3/3.text: the five lords of the Phi·lisʹtines, and all the Caʹnaan·ites, the Si·doʹni·ans, and the Hiʹvites inhabiting Mount Lebʹa·non from Mount Baʹal-herʹmon as far as Leʹbo-haʹmath.

judges/3/4.text: They served as a means of testing Israel to determine whether Israel would obey Jehovah’s commandments that he had given their fathers through Moses.

judges/3/5.text: So the Israelites lived among the Caʹnaan·ites, the Hitʹtites, the Amʹor·ites, the Perʹiz·zites, the Hiʹvites, and the Jebʹu·sites.

judges/3/6.text: They would take their daughters as wives, and their own daughters they gave to their sons, and they began serving their gods.

judges/3/7.text: So the Israelites did what was bad in Jehovah’s eyes, and they forgot Jehovah their God and were serving the Baʹals and the sacred poles.

judges/3/8.text: At this Jehovah’s anger blazed against Israel, and he sold them into the hand of Cuʹshan-rish·a·thaʹim the king of Mes·o·po·taʹmi·a. The Israelites served Cuʹshan-rish·a·thaʹim for eight years.

judges/3/9.text: When the Israelites called to Jehovah for help, Jehovah raised up a savior to rescue the Israelites, Othʹni·el the son of Keʹnaz, the younger brother of Caʹleb.

judges/3/10.text: The spirit of Jehovah came upon him, and he became the judge of Israel. When he went out to battle, Jehovah gave Cuʹshan-rish·a·thaʹim the king of Mes·o·po·taʹmi·a into his hand so that he prevailed over Cuʹshan-rish·a·thaʹim.

judges/3/11.text: After that the land had rest for 40 years. Then Othʹni·el the son of Keʹnaz died.

judges/3/12.text: And once again the Israelites began doing what was bad in Jehovah’s eyes. So Jehovah let Egʹlon the king of Moʹab prevail over Israel, because they did what was bad in Jehovah’s eyes.

judges/3/13.text: Furthermore, he brought against them the Amʹmon·ites and the A·malʹek·ites. They attacked Israel and captured the city of palm trees.

judges/3/14.text: The Israelites served Egʹlon the king of Moʹab for 18 years.

judges/3/15.text: Then the Israelites called to Jehovah for help, so Jehovah raised up for them a savior, Eʹhud the son of Geʹra, a Benʹja·min·ite who was left-handed. In time the Israelites sent tribute through him to Egʹlon the king of Moʹab.

judges/3/16.text: Meanwhile, Eʹhud made for himself a two-edged sword, a cubit long, and he strapped it underneath his garment on his right thigh.

judges/3/17.text: He then presented the tribute to Egʹlon the king of Moʹab. Now Egʹlon was a very fat man.

judges/3/18.text: When Eʹhud finished presenting the tribute, he sent away the people who had carried the tribute.

judges/3/19.text: But after reaching the carved images at Gilʹgal, he himself went back and said: “I have a secret message for you, O king.” So the king said: “Silence!” With that all his attendants left him.

judges/3/20.text: So Eʹhud came to him as he was sitting alone in his cool roof chamber. Then Eʹhud said: “I have a message from God for you.” So he rose up from his throne.

judges/3/21.text: Then Eʹhud drew the sword from his right thigh with his left hand and plunged it into his belly.

judges/3/22.text: The handle went in after the blade, and the fat closed in over the blade, for he did not draw the sword out of his belly, and the fecal matter came out.

judges/3/23.text: Eʹhud went out through the porch, closing the doors of the roof chamber behind him and locking them.

judges/3/24.text: After he left, the servants returned and saw that the doors of the roof chamber were locked. So they said: “He must be relieving himself in the cool interior room.”

judges/3/25.text: They kept waiting until they were embarrassed, but when they saw that he was still not opening the doors of the roof chamber, they took the key and opened them and saw their lord fallen to the floor dead!

judges/3/26.text: Eʹhud escaped while they were lingering, and he passed by the carved images and made it safely to Se·iʹrah.

judges/3/27.text: When he arrived, he sounded the horn in the mountainous region of Eʹphra·im; and the Israelites went down out of the mountainous region, with him at their head.

judges/3/28.text: Then he said to them: “Follow me, because Jehovah has given your enemies, the Moʹab·ites, into your hand.” So they followed him and captured the fords of the Jordan against the Moʹab·ites, and they did not allow anyone to cross.

judges/3/29.text: At that time they struck down about 10, 000 Moʹab·ites, all strong and valiant men; not a single one escaped.

judges/3/30.text: So Moʹab was subdued on that day under Israel’s hand; and the land had rest for 80 years.

judges/3/31.text: After him was Shamʹgar the son of Aʹnath, who struck down 600 Phi·lisʹtine men with a cattle goad; he too saved Israel.

judges/4/1.text: 4 But after Eʹhud died, the Israelites again did what was bad in Jehovah’s eyes.

judges/4/2.text: So Jehovah sold them into the hand of Jaʹbin the king of Caʹnaan, who reigned in Haʹzor. The chief of his army was Sisʹe·ra, who lived in Ha·roʹsheth of the nations.

judges/4/3.text: The Israelites cried out to Jehovah, because Jaʹbin had 900 war chariots with iron scythes, and he harshly oppressed the Israelites for 20 years.

judges/4/4.text: Now Debʹo·rah, a prophetess, the wife of Lapʹpi·doth, was judging Israel at that time.

judges/4/5.text: She used to sit under Debʹo·rah’s palm tree between Raʹmah and Bethʹel in the mountainous region of Eʹphra·im; the Israelites would go up to her for judgment.

judges/4/6.text: She sent for Baʹrak the son of A·binʹo·am out of Keʹdesh-naphʹta·li and said to him: “Has not Jehovah the God of Israel given the command? ‘Go and march to Mount Taʹbor, and take 10, 000 men of Naphʹta·li and Zebʹu·lun with you.

judges/4/7.text: I will bring to you Sisʹe·ra, the chief of Jaʹbin’s army, along with his war chariots and his troops to the stream of Kiʹshon, and I will give him into your hand.’”

judges/4/8.text: At this Baʹrak said to her: “If you go with me, I will go, but if you do not go with me, I will not go.”

judges/4/9.text: To this she said: “I will certainly go with you. However, the campaign you are going on will not bring you glory, for it will be into the hand of a woman that Jehovah will give Sisʹe·ra.” Then Debʹo·rah got up and went with Baʹrak to Keʹdesh.

judges/4/10.text: Baʹrak summoned Zebʹu·lun and Naphʹta·li to Keʹdesh, and 10, 000 men followed his steps. Debʹo·rah also went up with him.

judges/4/11.text: Incidentally, Heʹber the Kenʹite had separated from the Kenʹites, the descendants of Hoʹbab, Moses’ father-in-law, and his tent was pitched near the big tree in Za·a·nanʹnim, which is at Keʹdesh.

judges/4/12.text: They reported to Sisʹe·ra that Baʹrak the son of A·binʹo·am had gone up to Mount Taʹbor.

judges/4/13.text: At once Sisʹe·ra assembled all his war chariots—900 chariots with iron scythes—and all the troops that were with him from Ha·roʹsheth of the nations to go to the stream of Kiʹshon.

judges/4/14.text: Debʹo·rah now said to Baʹrak: “Rise up, for this is the day that Jehovah will give Sisʹe·ra into your hand. Is Jehovah not going out before you?” And Baʹrak descended from Mount Taʹbor with 10, 000 men following him.

judges/4/15.text: Then Jehovah threw Sisʹe·ra and all his war chariots and all the army into confusion before the sword of Baʹrak. Finally Sisʹe·ra got down from his chariot and fled on foot.

judges/4/16.text: Baʹrak chased after the war chariots and the army as far as Ha·roʹsheth of the nations. So Sisʹe·ra’s whole army fell by the sword; not even one remained.

judges/4/17.text: But Sisʹe·ra fled on foot to the tent of Jaʹel the wife of Heʹber the Kenʹite, for there was peace between Jaʹbin the king of Haʹzor and the house of Heʹber the Kenʹite.

judges/4/18.text: Then Jaʹel came out to meet Sisʹe·ra and said to him: “Come in, my lord, come in here. Do not be afraid.” So he went into her tent, and she covered him with a blanket.

judges/4/19.text: Then he said to her: “Give me, please, a little water to drink, for I am thirsty.” So she opened a skin bottle of milk and gave him a drink, after which she again covered him.

judges/4/20.text: He told her: “Stand at the entrance of the tent, and if anybody comes and asks you, ‘Is there a man here?’ say, ‘No!’”

judges/4/21.text: But Jaʹel the wife of Heʹber took a tent pin and a hammer in her hand. Then while he was fast asleep and exhausted, she stealthily approached him and drove the pin through his temples and beat it into the ground, and he died.

judges/4/22.text: Baʹrak went there in pursuit of Sisʹe·ra, and Jaʹel now came out to meet him and said: “Come and I will show you the man you are looking for.” He went in with her and saw Sisʹe·ra lying dead, with the tent pin through his temples.

judges/4/23.text: So on that day, God subdued Jaʹbin the king of Caʹnaan before the Israelites.

judges/4/24.text: The hand of the Israelites came down harder and harder against Jaʹbin the king of Caʹnaan, until they destroyed Jaʹbin the king of Caʹnaan.

judges/7/1.text: 7 Then Jer·ub·baʹal, that is, Gidʹe·on, and all the people with him rose early and encamped at the Spring of Haʹrod, while the camp of Midʹi·an was north of him at the hill of Moʹreh in the valley plain.

judges/7/2.text: Jehovah now said to Gidʹe·on: “There are too many people with you for me to give Midʹi·an into their hand. Otherwise, Israel might brag about itself against me and say, ‘My own hand saved me.’

judges/7/3.text: Now, please, announce in the presence of the people: ‘Whoever is afraid and trembling, let him return home.’” So Gidʹe·on put them to the test. With that, 22, 000 of the people returned home, and 10, 000 remained.

judges/7/4.text: Still Jehovah said to Gidʹe·on: “There are yet too many people. Have them go down to the water so that I may test them for you there. When I say to you, ‘This one will go with you, ’ he will go with you, but when I say to you, ‘This one will not go along with you, ’ he will not go along.”

judges/7/5.text: So he took the people down to the water. Then Jehovah said to Gidʹe·on: “Separate everyone who laps up the water with his tongue just as a dog laps, from those who bend down on their knees to drink.”

judges/7/6.text: The number of those lapping up the water, putting their hand to their mouth, was 300 men. The rest of the people bent down on their knees to drink.

judges/7/7.text: Jehovah now said to Gidʹe·on: “I will save you with the 300 men who lapped the water, and I will give Midʹi·an into your hand. But let all the other people go back home.”

judges/7/8.text: So after they took the provisions and the horns from the people, he sent all the other men of Israel back home, and he kept only the 300 men. The camp of Midʹi·an was below him in the valley plain.

judges/7/9.text: During that night, Jehovah said to him: “Get up, attack the camp, for I have given it into your hand.

judges/7/10.text: But if you are afraid to attack, go down to the camp with Puʹrah your attendant.

judges/7/11.text: Listen to what they say, and afterward you will have the courage to attack the camp.” At that he and Puʹrah his attendant went down to the edge of the encamped army.

judges/7/12.text: Now Midʹi·an and Amʹa·lek and all the Easterners covered the valley plain like a swarm of locusts, and their camels were without number, as many as the grains of sand on the seashore.

judges/7/13.text: Gidʹe·on now came, and there was a man relating a dream to his companion, and he said: “This is the dream I had. There was a round loaf of barley bread rolling into the camp of Midʹi·an. It came to a tent and struck it so hard that it collapsed. Yes, it turned the tent upside down, and the tent fell flat.”

judges/7/14.text: At this his companion said: “This can only be the sword of Gidʹe·on the son of Joʹash, a man of Israel. God has given Midʹi·an and all the camp into his hand.”

judges/7/15.text: As soon as Gidʹe·on heard him relate the dream and its interpretation, he bowed down to worship. After that he returned to the camp of Israel and said: “Get up, for Jehovah has given the camp of Midʹi·an into your hand.”

judges/7/16.text: Then he divided the 300 men into three bands and gave all of them horns and large empty jars with torches inside the jars.

judges/7/17.text: Then he said to them: “Watch me and do exactly what I do. When I come to the edge of the camp, you should do just as I do.

judges/7/18.text: When I blow the horn, I and all who are with me, you also must blow the horns all around the camp and shout, ‘For Jehovah and for Gidʹe·on!’”

judges/7/19.text: Gidʹe·on and the 100 men who were with him came to the edge of the camp at the start of the middle night watch, just after the sentries were posted. They blew the horns and smashed the large water jars that were in their hands.

judges/7/20.text: So the three bands blew the horns and shattered the large jars. They held the torches in their left hands and blew the horns in their right hands and they called out: “The sword of Jehovah and of Gidʹe·on!”

judges/7/21.text: All the while each man stood in his place all around the camp, and the whole army ran away, shouting as they fled.

judges/7/22.text: The 300 continued to blow the horns, and Jehovah turned the sword of each one against the other throughout the camp; and the army fled as far as Beth-shitʹtah, on to Zerʹe·rah, as far as the outskirts of Aʹbel-me·hoʹlah by Tabʹbath.

judges/7/23.text: And the men of Israel were called together from Naphʹta·li, Ashʹer, and all of Ma·nasʹseh, and they chased after Midʹi·an.

judges/7/24.text: Gidʹe·on sent messengers into all the mountainous region of Eʹphra·im, saying: “Go down to attack Midʹi·an, and capture the access to the waters as far as Beth-barʹah and the Jordan.” So all the men of Eʹphra·im were gathered together, and they captured the waters as far as Beth-barʹah and the Jordan.

judges/7/25.text: They also captured the two princes of Midʹi·an, Oʹreb and Zeʹeb; they killed Oʹreb on the rock of Oʹreb, and they killed Zeʹeb at the winepress of Zeʹeb. They kept on pursuing Midʹi·an, and they brought the heads of Oʹreb and Zeʹeb to Gidʹe·on in the region of the Jordan.

judges/10/1.text: 10 After A·bimʹe·lech, Toʹla the son of Puʹah, the son of Doʹdo, a man of Isʹsa·char, rose up to save Israel. He lived in Shaʹmir in the mountainous region of Eʹphra·im.

judges/10/2.text: He judged Israel for 23 years. Then he died and was buried in Shaʹmir.

judges/10/3.text: After him Jaʹir the Gilʹe·ad·ite rose up and judged Israel for 22 years.

judges/10/4.text: He had 30 sons who rode on 30 donkeys, and they had 30 cities, which to this day are called Havʹvoth-jaʹir; they are in the land of Gilʹe·ad.

judges/10/5.text: After that Jaʹir died and was buried in Kaʹmon.

judges/10/6.text: Again the Israelites did what was bad in the eyes of Jehovah, and they began to serve the Baʹals, the Ashʹto·reth images, the gods of Aʹram, the gods of Siʹdon, the gods of Moʹab, the gods of the Amʹmon·ites, and the gods of the Phi·lisʹtines. They abandoned Jehovah and did not serve him.

judges/10/7.text: Then Jehovah’s anger blazed against Israel, and he sold them into the hands of the Phi·lisʹtines and the Amʹmon·ites.

judges/10/8.text: So they crushed and greatly oppressed the Israelites in that year—for 18 years they oppressed all the Israelites on the side of the Jordan that had been the land of the Amʹor·ites in Gilʹe·ad.

judges/10/9.text: The Amʹmon·ites would also cross the Jordan to fight against Judah and Benjamin and the house of Eʹphra·im; and Israel was greatly distressed.

judges/10/10.text: Then the Israelites called to Jehovah for help, saying: “We have sinned against you, for we abandoned our God and served the Baʹals.”

judges/10/11.text: But Jehovah said to the Israelites: “Did I not save you from Egypt and from the Amʹor·ites, the Amʹmon·ites, the Phi·lisʹtines,

judges/10/12.text: the Si·doʹni·ans, Amʹa·lek, and Midʹi·an when they oppressed you? When you cried out to me, I saved you out of their hand.

judges/10/13.text: But you abandoned me and served other gods. That is why I will not save you again.

judges/10/14.text: Go to the gods whom you have chosen and call for help. Let them save you in your time of distress.”

judges/10/15.text: But the Israelites said to Jehovah: “We have sinned. Do to us whatever is good in your eyes. Only save us, please, this day.”

judges/10/16.text: And they removed the foreign gods from their midst and served Jehovah, so that he could no longer tolerate Israel’s suffering.

judges/10/17.text: In time the Amʹmon·ites were called together, and they pitched camp in Gilʹe·ad. So the Israelites gathered together and pitched camp in Mizʹpah.

judges/10/18.text: The people and the princes of Gilʹe·ad said to one another: “Who will take the lead in fighting against the Amʹmon·ites? Let him become the chief over all the inhabitants of Gilʹe·ad.”

judges/11/1.text: 11 Now Jephʹthah the Gilʹe·ad·ite was a mighty warrior; he was the son of a prostitute, and Gilʹe·ad was Jephʹthah’s father.

judges/11/2.text: But Gilʹe·ad’s wife also bore him sons. When the sons of his wife grew up, they drove Jephʹthah out and said to him: “You will have no inheritance in our father’s household, for you are the son of another woman.”

judges/11/3.text: So Jephʹthah fled from his brothers and settled in the land of Tob. And idle men joined company with Jephʹthah, and they followed him.

judges/11/4.text: After a while, the Amʹmon·ites fought against Israel.

judges/11/5.text: And when the Amʹmon·ites fought against Israel, the elders of Gilʹe·ad immediately went to bring Jephʹthah back from the land of Tob.

judges/11/6.text: They said to Jephʹthah: “Come and serve as our commander, so that we can fight against the Amʹmon·ites.”

judges/11/7.text: But Jephʹthah said to the elders of Gilʹe·ad: “Was it not you who hated me so much that you drove me out of my father’s house? Why have you come to me now when you are in distress?”

judges/11/8.text: At this the elders of Gilʹe·ad said to Jephʹthah: “That is why now we have returned to you. If you go with us and fight against the Amʹmon·ites, you will become our leader over all the inhabitants of Gilʹe·ad.”

judges/11/9.text: So Jephʹthah said to the elders of Gilʹe·ad: “If you bring me back to fight against the Amʹmon·ites and Jehovah defeats them for me, then I will indeed become your leader!”

judges/11/10.text: The elders of Gilʹe·ad said to Jephʹthah: “Let Jehovah be the witness between us if we do not do as you say.”

judges/11/11.text: So Jephʹthah went with the elders of Gilʹe·ad, and the people made him their leader and commander. And Jephʹthah repeated all his words before Jehovah in Mizʹpah.

judges/11/12.text: Jephʹthah then sent messengers to the king of the Amʹmon·ites, saying: “What do you have against me that you have come to attack my land?”

judges/11/13.text: So the king of the Amʹmon·ites said to the messengers of Jephʹthah: “It is because Israel took my land when they came up out of Egypt, from the Arʹnon to the Jabʹbok and as far as the Jordan. Now return it peaceably.”

judges/11/14.text: But Jephʹthah sent messengers back to the king of the Amʹmon·ites

judges/11/15.text: to say to him: “This is what Jephʹthah says: ‘Israel did not take the land of the Moʹab·ites and the land of the Amʹmon·ites,

judges/11/16.text: for when they came up out of Egypt, Israel walked through the wilderness as far as the Red Sea and came to Kaʹdesh.

judges/11/17.text: Then Israel sent messengers to the king of Eʹdom, saying: “Please let us pass through your land, ” but the king of Eʹdom did not listen. Also to the king of Moʹab they sent word, but he did not consent. So Israel kept dwelling in Kaʹdesh.

judges/11/18.text: When they walked through the wilderness, they bypassed the land of Eʹdom and the land of Moʹab. They traveled east of the land of Moʹab and camped in the region of the Arʹnon; they did not come within the boundary of Moʹab, for the Arʹnon was the boundary of Moʹab.

judges/11/19.text: “‘After that Israel sent messengers to Siʹhon king of the Amʹor·ites, king of Heshʹbon, and Israel said to him: “Please let us pass through your land to our own place.”

judges/11/20.text: But Siʹhon did not trust Israel to cross through his territory, so Siʹhon gathered all his people together and encamped in Jaʹhaz and fought against Israel.

judges/11/21.text: At this Jehovah the God of Israel gave Siʹhon and all his people into Israel’s hand, so that they defeated them and Israel took possession of all the land of the Amʹor·ites, the inhabitants of that land.

judges/11/22.text: Thus they took possession of all the territory of the Amʹor·ites from the Arʹnon to the Jabʹbok and from the wilderness to the Jordan.

judges/11/23.text: “‘It was Jehovah the God of Israel who drove out the Amʹor·ites from before his people Israel, and now would you drive them out?

judges/11/24.text: Do you not possess whatever your god Cheʹmosh gives you to possess? So everyone whom Jehovah our God has driven out from before us is the one we will drive out.

judges/11/25.text: Now are you any better than Baʹlak the son of Zipʹpor, the king of Moʹab? Did he ever contend with Israel, or did he ever fight against them?

judges/11/26.text: While Israel was dwelling in Heshʹbon and its dependent towns and in A·roʹer and its dependent towns and in all the cities that are by the banks of the Arʹnon for 300 years, why did you never try to take them back during that time?

judges/11/27.text: I have not sinned against you, but you are wrong to attack me. Let Jehovah the Judge be judge today between the people of Israel and the people of Amʹmon.’”

judges/11/28.text: But the king of the Amʹmon·ites would not listen to the message that Jephʹthah sent to him.

judges/11/29.text: Jehovah’s spirit came upon Jephʹthah, and he passed through Gilʹe·ad and Ma·nasʹseh to go to Mizʹpeh of Gilʹe·ad, and from Mizʹpeh of Gilʹe·ad he continued on to the Amʹmon·ites.

judges/11/30.text: Then Jephʹthah made a vow to Jehovah and said: “If you give the Amʹmon·ites into my hand,

judges/11/31.text: then whoever comes out of the door of my house to meet me when I return in peace from the Amʹmon·ites will become Jehovah’s, and I will offer that one up as a burnt offering.”

judges/11/32.text: So Jephʹthah went to fight against the Amʹmon·ites, and Jehovah gave them into his hand.

judges/11/33.text: He struck them down with a very great slaughter from A·roʹer all the way to Minʹnith—20 cities—and as far as Aʹbel-kerʹa·mim. Thus the Amʹmon·ites were subdued before the Israelites.

judges/11/34.text: Finally Jephʹthah came to his home in Mizʹpah, and look! his daughter was coming out to meet him, playing the tambourine and dancing! Now she was his one and only child. Besides her, he had neither son nor daughter.

judges/11/35.text: When he saw her, he ripped his garments and said: “Oh no, my daughter! You have broken my heart, for you have become the one I have banished. Now I have opened my mouth to Jehovah, and I am unable to turn back.”

judges/11/36.text: But she said to him: “My father, if you have opened your mouth to Jehovah, do to me as you have promised, since Jehovah has executed vengeance for you upon your enemies, the Amʹmon·ites.”

judges/11/37.text: She then said to her father: “Let this be done for me: Let me be alone for two months, and let me go away into the mountains, and let me weep over my virginity with my female companions.”

judges/11/38.text: At this he said: “Go!” So he sent her away for two months, and she went to the mountains with her companions to weep over her virginity.

judges/11/39.text: At the end of two months, she returned to her father, after which he carried out the vow he had made regarding her. She never had relations with a man. And it became a custom in Israel:

judges/11/40.text: From year to year, the young women of Israel would go to give commendation to the daughter of Jephʹthah the Gilʹe·ad·ite four days in the year.

judges/12/1.text: 12 Then the men of Eʹphra·im were summoned, and they crossed over to Zaʹphon and said to Jephʹthah: “Why did you not call us to go with you when you crossed over to fight against the Amʹmon·ites? We will burn your house down with you in it.”

judges/12/2.text: But Jephʹthah said to them: “Along with my people, I was engaged in a great conflict with the Amʹmon·ites. I did call to you for help, but you did not save me from their hand.

judges/12/3.text: When I saw that you would not save me, then I decided to risk my life and go against the Amʹmon·ites, and Jehovah handed them over to me. So why have you come today to fight against me?”

judges/12/4.text: Jephʹthah then gathered all the men of Gilʹe·ad, and they fought Eʹphra·im; the men of Gilʹe·ad defeated Eʹphra·im, who had said: “You are only fugitives from Eʹphra·im, you Gilʹe·ad·ites in Eʹphra·im and Ma·nasʹseh.”

judges/12/5.text: Gilʹe·ad captured the fords of the Jordan ahead of Eʹphra·im; and when the men of Eʹphra·im were trying to escape, they would say, “Let me cross over”; then the men of Gilʹe·ad would ask each one, “Are you an Eʹphra·im·ite?” When he would reply, “No!”

judges/12/6.text: they would say to him, “Please say Shibʹbo·leth.” But he would say, “Sibʹbo·leth, ” as he was unable to say the word correctly. Then they would seize him and slay him at the fords of the Jordan. So 42, 000 Eʹphra·im·ites fell at that time.

judges/12/7.text: Jephʹthah judged Israel for six years, after which Jephʹthah the Gilʹe·ad·ite died and was buried in his city in Gilʹe·ad.

judges/12/8.text: Ibʹzan from Bethʹle·hem judged Israel after him.

judges/12/9.text: He had 30 sons and 30 daughters. He sent his daughters to marry men outside his clan, and he brought in 30 women to marry his sons. He judged Israel for seven years.

judges/12/10.text: Then Ibʹzan died and was buried in Bethʹle·hem.

judges/12/11.text: After him Eʹlon the Zebʹu·lun·ite judged Israel; he judged Israel for ten years.

judges/12/12.text: Then Eʹlon the Zebʹu·lun·ite died and was buried in Aiʹja·lon in the land of Zebʹu·lun.

judges/12/13.text: After him Abʹdon the son of Hilʹlel the Pirʹa·thon·ite judged Israel.

judges/12/14.text: He had 40 sons and 30 grandsons who rode on 70 donkeys. He judged Israel for eight years.

judges/12/15.text: Then Abʹdon the son of Hilʹlel the Pirʹa·thon·ite died and was buried in Pirʹa·thon in the land of Eʹphra·im in the mountain of the A·malʹek·ite.

judges/13/1.text: 13 Again the Israelites did what was bad in Jehovah’s eyes, and Jehovah gave them into the hand of the Phi·lisʹtines for 40 years.

judges/13/2.text: Meanwhile, there was a man of Zorʹah of the family of the Danʹites, whose name was Ma·noʹah. His wife was barren and childless.

judges/13/3.text: In time Jehovah’s angel appeared to the woman and said to her: “Look, you are barren and childless. But you will conceive and give birth to a son.

judges/13/4.text: Now be careful not to drink wine or anything alcoholic, and do not eat anything unclean.

judges/13/5.text: Look! You will conceive and give birth to a son, and no razor should touch his head, because the child will be a Nazʹi·rite of God from birth, and he will take the lead in saving Israel out of the hand of the Phi·lisʹtines.”

judges/13/6.text: Then the woman went and told her husband: “A man of the true God came to me, and his appearance was like an angel of the true God, very awe-inspiring. I did not ask him where he was from, nor did he tell me his name.

judges/13/7.text: But he said to me, ‘Look! You will conceive and give birth to a son. Now do not drink wine or anything alcoholic, and do not eat anything unclean, because the child will be a Nazʹi·rite of God from birth until the day of his death.’”

judges/13/8.text: Ma·noʹah pleaded with Jehovah and said: “Pardon me, Jehovah. Please let the man of the true God whom you just sent come again to instruct us about what we should do with the child who will be born.”

judges/13/9.text: So the true God listened to Ma·noʹah, and the angel of the true God came again to the woman while she was sitting in the field; her husband Ma·noʹah was not with her.

judges/13/10.text: The woman quickly ran and told her husband: “Look! The man who came to me the other day has appeared to me.”

judges/13/11.text: Then Ma·noʹah got up and went with his wife. He came to the man and said to him: “Are you the man who spoke to my wife?” He said: “I am.”

judges/13/12.text: Then Ma·noʹah said: “May your words come true! What will be the child’s manner of life, and what will be his work?”

judges/13/13.text: So Jehovah’s angel said to Ma·noʹah: “Your wife should keep herself from everything that I mentioned to her.

judges/13/14.text: She should not eat anything that the grapevine produces, she should not drink wine or anything alcoholic, and she should not eat anything unclean. Everything that I commanded her, let her observe.”

judges/13/15.text: Ma·noʹah now said to Jehovah’s angel: “Please stay, and let us prepare a young goat for you.”

judges/13/16.text: But Jehovah’s angel said to Ma·noʹah: “If I stay, I will not eat your food; but if you wish to present a burnt offering to Jehovah, you may offer it up.” Ma·noʹah did not know that he was Jehovah’s angel.

judges/13/17.text: Then Ma·noʹah said to Jehovah’s angel: “What is your name, so that we may honor you when your word comes true?”

judges/13/18.text: However, Jehovah’s angel said to him: “Why are you asking about my name, seeing that it is a wonderful one?”

judges/13/19.text: Then Ma·noʹah took the young goat and the grain offering and offered them on the rock to Jehovah. And He was doing something amazing while Ma·noʹah and his wife were looking on.

judges/13/20.text: As the flame ascended from the altar heavenward, Jehovah’s angel ascended in the flame from the altar while Ma·noʹah and his wife were looking on. At once they fell with their faces to the ground.

judges/13/21.text: Jehovah’s angel did not appear again to Ma·noʹah and his wife. Then Ma·noʹah realized that he was Jehovah’s angel.

judges/13/22.text: Ma·noʹah then said to his wife: “We are sure to die, because it is God whom we have seen.”

judges/13/23.text: But his wife said to him: “If Jehovah wanted to put us to death, he would not have accepted a burnt offering and a grain offering from our hand, he would not have shown us all these things, and he would not have told us any of these things.”

judges/13/24.text: The woman later gave birth to a son and named him Samson; and as the boy grew, Jehovah continued to bless him.

judges/13/25.text: In time Jehovah’s spirit started to impel him in Maʹha·neh-dan, between Zorʹah and Eshʹta·ol.

1-samuel/1/1.text: 1 Now there was a man of Ra·math·aʹim-zoʹphim of the mountainous region of Eʹphra·im whose name was El·kaʹnah, the son of Je·roʹham, the son of E·liʹhu, the son of Toʹhu, the son of Zuph, an Eʹphra·im·ite.

1-samuel/1/2.text: He had two wives; one was named Hanʹnah, and the other was named Pe·ninʹnah. Pe·ninʹnah had children, but Hanʹnah had no children.

1-samuel/1/3.text: That man went up from his city year after year to worship and to sacrifice to Jehovah of armies in Shiʹloh. That is where the two sons of Eʹli, Hophʹni and Phinʹe·has, served as priests to Jehovah.

1-samuel/1/4.text: One day when El·kaʹnah offered a sacrifice, he gave portions to his wife Pe·ninʹnah as well as to all her sons and her daughters,

1-samuel/1/5.text: but to Hanʹnah he gave a special portion, because Hanʹnah was the one he loved; but Jehovah had not given her children.

1-samuel/1/6.text: Moreover, her rival wife taunted her relentlessly in order to upset her because Jehovah had not given her children.

1-samuel/1/7.text: That is what she would do year after year; whenever Hanʹnah went up to the house of Jehovah, her rival would taunt her so much that she would weep and not eat.

1-samuel/1/8.text: But her husband El·kaʹnah said to her: “Hanʹnah, why do you weep, and why do you not eat, and why are you so sad? Am I not better to you than ten sons?”

1-samuel/1/9.text: Then Hanʹnah got up after they had finished eating and drinking in Shiʹloh. At the time, Eʹli the priest was sitting on the seat by the doorpost of the temple of Jehovah.

1-samuel/1/10.text: Hanʹnah was extremely bitter, and she began to pray to Jehovah and to weep uncontrollably.

1-samuel/1/11.text: And she made this vow: “O Jehovah of armies, if you look upon the affliction of your servant and remember me and you do not forget your servant and give to your servant a male child, I will give him to Jehovah all the days of his life, and no razor will touch his head.”

1-samuel/1/12.text: While she prayed for a long time before Jehovah, Eʹli was watching her mouth.

1-samuel/1/13.text: Hanʹnah was speaking in her heart, only her lips were trembling, but her voice was not heard. So Eʹli thought she was drunk.

1-samuel/1/14.text: Eʹli said to her: “How long will you stay drunk? Stop drinking your wine.”

1-samuel/1/15.text: At this Hanʹnah answered: “No, my lord! I am a woman under great stress; I have not drunk wine or anything alcoholic, but I am pouring out my soul before Jehovah.

1-samuel/1/16.text: Do not take your servant for a worthless woman, for I have been speaking until now out of my great anguish and distress.”

1-samuel/1/17.text: Then Eʹli answered: “Go in peace, and may the God of Israel grant your petition that you have asked of him.”

1-samuel/1/18.text: To this she said: “Let your servant find favor in your eyes.” And the woman went on her way and ate, and her face was no longer downcast.

1-samuel/1/19.text: Then they got up early in the morning and bowed before Jehovah, after which they returned to their house in Raʹmah. El·kaʹnah had sexual relations with his wife Hanʹnah, and Jehovah gave attention to her.

1-samuel/1/20.text: Within a year Hanʹnah became pregnant and gave birth to a son and named him Samuel, because, as she said, “it is from Jehovah that I have asked him.”

1-samuel/1/21.text: In time El·kaʹnah went up with all his household to offer the yearly sacrifice to Jehovah and to present his vow offering.

1-samuel/1/22.text: But Hanʹnah did not go up, for she said to her husband: “As soon as the boy is weaned, I will bring him; then he will appear before Jehovah and remain there from then on.”

1-samuel/1/23.text: El·kaʹnah her husband then said to her: “Do what you think is best. Stay at home until you wean him. May Jehovah carry out what you have said.” So the woman stayed at home and nursed her son until she weaned him.

1-samuel/1/24.text: As soon as she had weaned him, she took him up to Shiʹloh, along with a three-year-old bull, one eʹphah of flour, and a large jar of wine, and she came to the house of Jehovah in Shiʹloh and brought the young boy with her.

1-samuel/1/25.text: Then they slaughtered the bull and brought the boy to Eʹli.

1-samuel/1/26.text: With that she said: “Pardon me, my lord! As surely as you live, my lord, I am the woman who was standing with you in this place to pray to Jehovah.

1-samuel/1/27.text: It was for this boy that I prayed, and Jehovah granted my petition that I asked of him.

1-samuel/1/28.text: I, in turn, now lend him to Jehovah. For all his days, he is lent to Jehovah.” And he bowed down there to Jehovah.

1-samuel/9/1.text: 9 There was a man of Benjamin named Kish, the son of A·biʹel, the son of Zeʹror son of Be·coʹrath son of A·phiʹah, a Benʹja·min·ite and a very wealthy man.

1-samuel/9/2.text: He had a son named Saul, who was young and handsome—there was no man among the Israelites more handsome than he—and he stood head and shoulders taller than all the people.

1-samuel/9/3.text: When the donkeys belonging to Saul’s father Kish got lost, Kish said to his son Saul: “Please take with you one of the attendants and go look for the donkeys.”

1-samuel/9/4.text: They passed through the mountainous region of Eʹphra·im and through the land of Shalʹi·shah, and they did not find them. They traveled through the land of Shaʹa·lim, but the donkeys were not there. They passed through the entire land of the Benʹja·min·ites, and they did not find them.

1-samuel/9/5.text: They came into the land of Zuph, and Saul said to his attendant who was with him: “Come, let us return, so that my father does not start worrying about us rather than the donkeys.”

1-samuel/9/6.text: But the attendant replied: “Look, there is a man of God in this city, a man who is held in honor. All that he says is sure to come true. Let us go there now. Perhaps he can tell us which way to go.”

1-samuel/9/7.text: At this Saul said to his attendant: “If we go, what can we take to the man? There is no bread in our bags; there is nothing to take as a gift to the man of the true God. What do we have?”

1-samuel/9/8.text: So the attendant answered Saul again: “Look! There is a quarter of a shekel of silver in my hand. I will give it to the man of the true God, and he will tell us which way to go.”

1-samuel/9/9.text: (In former times in Israel, this was what a man would say when going to seek God: “Come, and let us go to the seer.” For the prophet of today used to be called a seer in former times.)

1-samuel/9/10.text: Then Saul said to his attendant: “What you said is good. Let us go.” So they went to the city where the man of the true God was.

1-samuel/9/11.text: While they were going up the ascent to the city, they met girls going out to draw water. So they said to them: “Is the seer in this place?”

1-samuel/9/12.text: They answered: “He is. Look, he is just ahead of you. Hurry now, for today he has come to the city, because the people are making a sacrifice today on the high place.

1-samuel/9/13.text: As soon as you come into the city, you will find him before he goes up to the high place to eat. The people will not eat until he comes, for he is the one who blesses the sacrifice. Once that is done, those who are invited may eat. So now go up right away, and you will find him.”

1-samuel/9/14.text: So they went up to the city. As they were coming into the middle of the city, there was Samuel coming out to meet them to go up to the high place.

1-samuel/9/15.text: The day before Saul came, Jehovah had told Samuel:

1-samuel/9/16.text: “Tomorrow about this time, I will send to you a man from the land of Benjamin. You must anoint him as leader over my people Israel, and he will save my people from the hand of the Phi·lisʹtines. For I have seen the affliction of my people, and their outcry has reached me.”

1-samuel/9/17.text: When Samuel saw Saul, Jehovah told him: “Here is the man of whom I said to you, ‘This is the one who will govern my people.’”

1-samuel/9/18.text: Then Saul approached Samuel in the middle of the gate and said: “Tell me, please, where is the house of the seer?”

1-samuel/9/19.text: Samuel answered Saul: “I am the seer. Go up ahead of me to the high place, and you will eat with me today. I will send you away in the morning, and I will tell you all that you want to know.

1-samuel/9/20.text: As for the donkeys that were lost three days ago, do not worry about them, for they have been found. And to whom does all that is desirable of Israel belong? Is it not to you and to the whole house of your father?”

1-samuel/9/21.text: At this Saul answered: “Am I not a Benʹja·min·ite of the smallest of the tribes of Israel, and my family the most insignificant of all the families of the tribe of Benjamin? So why have you spoken to me in this way?”

1-samuel/9/22.text: Then Samuel took Saul and his attendant and brought them to the dining hall and gave them a place at the head of those invited; there were about 30 men.

1-samuel/9/23.text: Samuel said to the cook: “Bring the portion that I gave you and told you, ‘Set it aside.’”

1-samuel/9/24.text: At that the cook lifted up the leg and what was on it, and set it before Saul. And Samuel said: “What has been reserved has been set before you. Eat, because they have reserved it for you for this occasion. For I told them, ‘I invited guests.’” So Saul ate with Samuel on that day.

1-samuel/9/25.text: Then they went down from the high place to the city, and he continued to speak with Saul on the housetop.

1-samuel/9/26.text: They rose early, and at daybreak Samuel called to Saul on the housetop, saying: “Get ready, so that I may send you away.” So Saul got ready and both he and Samuel went outside.

1-samuel/9/27.text: While they were descending toward the outskirts of the city, Samuel said to Saul: “Tell the attendant to go on ahead of us, ” so he went on ahead. “But you, stand still now, so that I may let you hear the word of God.”

1-samuel/16/1.text: 16 Jehovah eventually said to Samuel: “How long will you mourn for Saul now that I have rejected him from ruling as king over Israel? Fill your horn with oil and go. I will send you to Jesʹse the Bethʹle·hem·ite, because I have selected from among his sons a king for myself.”

1-samuel/16/2.text: But Samuel said: “How can I go? When Saul hears about it, he will kill me.” Jehovah replied: “Take a young cow with you and say, ‘I have come to sacrifice to Jehovah.’

1-samuel/16/3.text: Invite Jesʹse to the sacrifice; then I will make known to you what to do. You must anoint for me the one whom I designate to you.”

1-samuel/16/4.text: Samuel did what Jehovah said. When he came to Bethʹle·hem, the elders of the city were trembling at meeting him, and they said: “Does your coming mean peace?”

1-samuel/16/5.text: To this he said: “It means peace. I have come to sacrifice to Jehovah. Sanctify yourselves, and come with me to the sacrifice.” Then he sanctified Jesʹse and his sons, after which he summoned them to the sacrifice.

1-samuel/16/6.text: As they came in and he saw E·liʹab, he said: “Surely here before Jehovah stands his anointed one.”

1-samuel/16/7.text: But Jehovah said to Samuel: “Do not pay attention to his appearance and how tall he is, for I have rejected him. For the way man sees is not the way God sees, because mere man sees what appears to the eyes, but Jehovah sees into the heart.”

1-samuel/16/8.text: Then Jesʹse called A·binʹa·dab and had him pass before Samuel, but he said: “Jehovah has not chosen this one either.”

1-samuel/16/9.text: Next Jesʹse presented Shamʹmah, but he said: “Jehovah has not chosen this one either.”

1-samuel/16/10.text: So Jesʹse had seven of his sons pass before Samuel, but Samuel said to Jesʹse: “Jehovah has not chosen any of these.”

1-samuel/16/11.text: Finally Samuel said to Jesʹse: “Are these all of your boys?” To this he said: “The youngest has been left out until now; he is pasturing the sheep.” Then Samuel said to Jesʹse: “Send for him, because we will not sit down for the meal until he comes here.”

1-samuel/16/12.text: So he sent for him and brought him in. Now he was ruddy, with beautiful eyes, and handsome in appearance. Then Jehovah said: “Get up, anoint him, for this is the one!”

1-samuel/16/13.text: So Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him in the presence of his brothers. And the spirit of Jehovah began to empower David from that day forward. Samuel later rose and went his way to Raʹmah.

1-samuel/16/14.text: Now the spirit of Jehovah had departed from Saul, and a bad spirit from Jehovah terrorized him.

1-samuel/16/15.text: The servants of Saul said to him: “You see that a bad spirit from God is terrorizing you.

1-samuel/16/16.text: Let our lord, please, command your servants before you to look for a man who is skilled at playing the harp. Whenever a bad spirit from God comes upon you, he will play it, and you will feel better.”

1-samuel/16/17.text: So Saul said to his servants: “Find me, please, a man who plays well, and bring him to me.”

1-samuel/16/18.text: One of the attendants said: “Look! I have seen how a son of Jesʹse the Bethʹle·hem·ite plays skillfully, and he is a courageous, mighty warrior. He can speak well, and he is handsome, and Jehovah is with him.”

1-samuel/16/19.text: Saul then sent messengers to Jesʹse and said: “Send to me your son David, who is with the flock.”

1-samuel/16/20.text: So Jesʹse loaded a donkey with bread, a skin bottle of wine, and a young goat and sent them to Saul with his son David.

1-samuel/16/21.text: Thus David came to Saul and began serving him. Saul grew to love him very much, and he became his armor-bearer.

1-samuel/16/22.text: Saul sent a message to Jesʹse: “Please let David remain in my service, for he has found favor in my eyes.”

1-samuel/16/23.text: Whenever a bad spirit from God came upon Saul, David took the harp and played it, and Saul found relief and felt better, and the bad spirit would depart from him.

1-kings/2/1.text: 2 When the time of David’s death drew near, he gave his son Solʹo·mon these instructions:

1-kings/2/2.text: “I am about to die. Therefore, be strong and prove yourself a man.

1-kings/2/3.text: You must keep your obligation to Jehovah your God by walking in his ways and by observing his statutes, his commandments, his judgments, and his reminders as they are written in the Law of Moses; then you will succeed in everything you do and everywhere you turn.

1-kings/2/4.text: And Jehovah will carry out his promise that he made concerning me: ‘If your sons pay attention to their way by walking faithfully before me with all their heart and soul, there will never fail to be a man of your line sitting on the throne of Israel.’

1-kings/2/5.text: “You also well know what Joʹab the son of Ze·ruʹiah did to me, what he did to two chiefs of the armies of Israel—Abʹner the son of Ner and A·maʹsa the son of Jeʹther. He killed them, shedding the blood of war in peacetime, and he put the blood of war on the belt around his waist and on the sandals on his feet.

1-kings/2/6.text: You must act according to your wisdom and not let his gray hairs go down in peace to the Grave.

1-kings/2/7.text: “But toward the sons of Bar·zilʹlai the Gilʹe·ad·ite, you should show loyal love, and they should be among those eating at your table, for that was how they stood by me when I ran away from your brother Abʹsa·lom.

1-kings/2/8.text: “There is also with you Shimʹe·i the son of Geʹra the Benʹja·min·ite from Ba·huʹrim. He was the one who cursed me with a vicious curse on the day that I was going to Ma·ha·naʹim; but when he came down to meet me at the Jordan, I swore to him by Jehovah: ‘I will not put you to death by the sword.’

1-kings/2/9.text: Now do not leave him unpunished, for you are a wise man and you know what you should do to him; you must bring his gray hairs down to the Grave with blood.”

1-kings/2/10.text: Then David was laid to rest with his forefathers and was buried in the City of David.

1-kings/2/11.text: The length of David’s reign over Israel was 40 years. In Hebʹron he reigned for 7 years, and in Jerusalem he reigned for 33 years.

1-kings/2/12.text: Solʹo·mon then sat down on the throne of David his father, and gradually his kingship became firmly established.

1-kings/2/13.text: In time Ad·o·niʹjah the son of Hagʹgith came to Bath-sheʹba, Solʹo·mon’s mother. She asked: “Is your coming peaceable?” He replied: “It is peaceable.”

1-kings/2/14.text: He then said: “I have something to say to you.” So she said: “Speak.”

1-kings/2/15.text: He continued: “You well know that the kingship was to become mine, and all Israel expected me to become king; but the kingship eluded me and became my brother’s, for it was from Jehovah that it became his.

1-kings/2/16.text: But now there is just one request that I am making of you. Do not turn me away.” So she said to him: “Speak.”

1-kings/2/17.text: He then said: “Please, ask Solʹo·mon the king—for he will not turn you away—to give me Abʹi·shag the Shuʹnam·mite as a wife.”

1-kings/2/18.text: To this Bath-sheʹba said: “Very well! I will speak for you to the king.”

1-kings/2/19.text: So Bath-sheʹba went in to King Solʹo·mon to speak to him for Ad·o·niʹjah. At once the king rose to meet her and bowed down to her. Then he sat down on his throne and had a throne set for the king’s mother, so that she could sit at his right.

1-kings/2/20.text: She then said: “There is one small request that I am making of you. Do not turn me away.” So the king said to her: “Make it, my mother; for I will not turn you away.”

1-kings/2/21.text: She said: “Let Abʹi·shag the Shuʹnam·mite be given as a wife to your brother Ad·o·niʹjah.”

1-kings/2/22.text: At this King Solʹo·mon answered his mother: “Why are you requesting Abʹi·shag the Shuʹnam·mite for Ad·o·niʹjah? You may as well request the kingship for him, for he is my older brother, and supporting him are A·biʹa·thar the priest and Joʹab the son of Ze·ruʹiah.”

1-kings/2/23.text: With that King Solʹo·mon swore by Jehovah: “So may God do to me and add to it if it was not at the cost of his own life that Ad·o·niʹjah made this request.

1-kings/2/24.text: And now, as surely as Jehovah is living, who has firmly established me and seated me on the throne of David my father and who made a house for me, just as he promised, Ad·o·niʹjah will be put to death today.”

1-kings/2/25.text: King Solʹo·mon immediately sent Be·naiʹah the son of Je·hoiʹa·da, who went out and struck Ad·o·niʹjah down, and he died.

1-kings/2/26.text: To A·biʹa·thar the priest, the king said: “Go to your fields in Anʹa·thoth! You deserve to die, but on this day I will not put you to death because you carried the Ark of the Sovereign Lord Jehovah before David my father and because you shared in all the hardships that my father suffered.”

1-kings/2/27.text: So Solʹo·mon drove A·biʹa·thar out from serving as a priest of Jehovah, to fulfill Jehovah’s word against the house of Eʹli in Shiʹloh.

1-kings/2/28.text: When the news reached Joʹab—for Joʹab had supported Ad·o·niʹjah but he had not supported Abʹsa·lom—Joʹab fled to the tent of Jehovah and grabbed hold of the horns of the altar.

1-kings/2/29.text: Then King Solʹo·mon was told: “Joʹab has fled to the tent of Jehovah, and he is there beside the altar.” So Solʹo·mon sent Be·naiʹah the son of Je·hoiʹa·da, saying: “Go, strike him down!”

1-kings/2/30.text: So Be·naiʹah went to the tent of Jehovah and said to him: “This is what the king says, ‘Come out!’” But he said: “No! I will die here.” Be·naiʹah brought word back to the king: “This is what Joʹab said, and this is what he answered me.”

1-kings/2/31.text: Then the king said to him: “Do just as he said; strike him down and bury him and remove from me and from the house of my father the blood that Joʹab spilled without just cause.

1-kings/2/32.text: Jehovah will bring his blood back on his own head, for without my father David’s knowledge, he struck down and killed with the sword two men more righteous and better than he was: Abʹner the son of Ner, the chief of the army of Israel, and A·maʹsa the son of Jeʹther, the chief of the army of Judah.

1-kings/2/33.text: Their blood will come back on the head of Joʹab and on the head of his offspring forever; but for David, his offspring, his house, and his throne, may there be peace from Jehovah forever.”

1-kings/2/34.text: Then Be·naiʹah the son of Je·hoiʹa·da went up and struck Joʹab down and put him to death, and he was buried at his own house in the wilderness.

1-kings/2/35.text: Then the king appointed Be·naiʹah the son of Je·hoiʹa·da over the army in his place, and the king appointed Zaʹdok the priest in place of A·biʹa·thar.

1-kings/2/36.text: Then the king summoned Shimʹe·i and said to him: “Build yourself a house in Jerusalem, and live there; do not go out from there to any other place.

1-kings/2/37.text: On the day you go out and cross the Kidʹron Valley, you can be sure that you will die. Your blood will be on your own head.”

1-kings/2/38.text: Shimʹe·i replied to the king: “What you have said is fair. Your servant will do just as my lord the king has said.” So Shimʹe·i stayed in Jerusalem for many days.

1-kings/2/39.text: But at the end of three years, two of Shimʹe·i’s slaves ran away to Aʹchish the son of Maʹa·cah the king of Gath. When Shimʹe·i was told: “Look! Your slaves are in Gath, ”

1-kings/2/40.text: Shimʹe·i immediately saddled his donkey and went to see Aʹchish in Gath to find his slaves. When Shimʹe·i returned from Gath with his slaves,

1-kings/2/41.text: Solʹo·mon was told: “Shimʹe·i has gone out of Jerusalem to Gath and has returned.”

1-kings/2/42.text: At that the king summoned Shimʹe·i and said to him: “Did I not put you under oath by Jehovah and warn you: ‘On the day you go out from here to any other place, you can be sure that you will die’? And did you not say to me, ‘What you are saying is fair; I will obey’?

1-kings/2/43.text: Why, then, did you not keep the oath of Jehovah and the commandment that I imposed on you?”

1-kings/2/44.text: The king then said to Shimʹe·i: “You know in your heart all the injury that you did to David my father, and Jehovah will bring back that injury on your own head.

1-kings/2/45.text: But King Solʹo·mon will be blessed, and the throne of David will be firmly established before Jehovah forever.”

1-kings/2/46.text: With that the king commanded Be·naiʹah the son of Je·hoiʹa·da, who went out and struck him down, and he died. Thus the kingdom was firmly established in the hand of Solʹo·mon.

2-kings/11/1.text: 11 Now when Ath·a·liʹah, A·ha·ziʹah’s mother, saw that her son had died, she rose up and destroyed the entire royal line.

2-kings/11/2.text: However, Je·hoshʹe·ba the daughter of King Je·hoʹram, A·ha·ziʹah’s sister, took Je·hoʹash the son of A·ha·ziʹah and stole him away from among the sons of the king who were to be put to death, keeping him and his nurse in an inner bedroom. They managed to keep him concealed from Ath·a·liʹah, so he was not put to death.

2-kings/11/3.text: He remained with her for six years, hidden at the house of Jehovah, while Ath·a·liʹah was ruling over the land.

2-kings/11/4.text: In the seventh year, Je·hoiʹa·da sent for the chiefs of hundreds of the Caʹri·an bodyguard and of the palace guards and had them come to him at the house of Jehovah. He made a pact with them and had them swear to it at the house of Jehovah, and then he showed them the son of the king.

2-kings/11/5.text: He ordered them: “This is what you are to do: One third of you will be on duty on the Sabbath and will keep strict watch over the king’s house,

2-kings/11/6.text: another third will be at the Gate of the Foundation, and another third will be at the gate behind the palace guards. You will take turns watching over the house.

2-kings/11/7.text: Your two divisions that are supposed to be off duty on the Sabbath must keep strict watch over the house of Jehovah to protect the king.

2-kings/11/8.text: You must surround the king on every side, each with his weapons in hand. Anyone entering within the ranks will be put to death. Stay with the king wherever he goes.”

2-kings/11/9.text: The chiefs of hundreds did exactly what Je·hoiʹa·da the priest had commanded. So each one took his men who were on duty on the Sabbath, together with those who were off duty on the Sabbath, and they came in to Je·hoiʹa·da the priest.

2-kings/11/10.text: The priest then gave the chiefs of hundreds the spears and the circular shields that had belonged to King David, which were in the house of Jehovah.

2-kings/11/11.text: And the palace guards took their positions, each with his weapons in hand, from the right side of the house to the left side of the house, by the altar and by the house, all around the king.

2-kings/11/12.text: Then Je·hoiʹa·da brought the king’s son out and put on him the crown and the Testimony, and they made him king and anointed him. They began to clap their hands and say: “Long live the king!”

2-kings/11/13.text: When Ath·a·liʹah heard the sound of the people running, she immediately came to the people at the house of Jehovah.

2-kings/11/14.text: Then she saw the king standing there by the pillar according to the custom. The chiefs and the trumpeters were with the king, and all the people of the land were rejoicing and blowing the trumpets. At this Ath·a·liʹah ripped her garments apart and cried out: “Conspiracy! Conspiracy!”

2-kings/11/15.text: But Je·hoiʹa·da the priest commanded the chiefs of hundreds, those appointed over the army, and said to them: “Take her out from among the ranks, and if anyone follows her, put him to death with the sword!” For the priest had said: “Do not put her to death in the house of Jehovah.”

2-kings/11/16.text: So they seized her, and when she reached the place where the horses enter the king’s house, she was put to death there.

2-kings/11/17.text: Then Je·hoiʹa·da made a covenant between Jehovah and the king and the people, that they would continue as the people of Jehovah, and he also made a covenant between the king and the people.

2-kings/11/18.text: After that all the people of the land came to the house of Baʹal and tore down his altars, completely smashed his images, and killed Matʹtan the priest of Baʹal in front of the altars. Then the priest appointed overseers over the house of Jehovah.

2-kings/11/19.text: Further, he took the chiefs of hundreds, the Caʹri·an bodyguard, the palace guards, and all the people of the land to escort the king down from the house of Jehovah, and they came to the king’s house by the way of the gate of the palace guard. He then sat on the throne of the kings.

2-kings/11/20.text: So all the people of the land rejoiced and the city was quiet, for they had put Ath·a·liʹah to death with the sword at the king’s house.

2-kings/11/21.text: Je·hoʹash was seven years old when he became king.
