1-chronicles/1/5.text: The sons of Jaʹpheth were Goʹmer, Maʹgog, Maʹda·i, Jaʹvan, Tuʹbal, Meʹshech, and Tiʹras.

1-chronicles/1/6.text: The sons of Goʹmer were Ashʹke·naz, Riʹphath, and To·garʹmah.

1-chronicles/1/7.text: The sons of Jaʹvan were E·liʹshah, Tarʹshish, Kitʹtim, and Roʹda·nim.

1-chronicles/1/8.text: The sons of Ham were Cush, Mizʹra·im, Put, and Caʹnaan.

1-chronicles/1/9.text: The sons of Cush were Seʹba, Havʹi·lah, Sabʹtah, Raʹa·mah, and Sabʹte·ca. The sons of Raʹa·mah were Sheʹba and Deʹdan.

1-chronicles/1/10.text: Cush became father to Nimʹrod. He was the first to become a mighty one on the earth.

1-chronicles/1/11.text: Mizʹra·im became father to Luʹdim, Anʹa·mim, Le·haʹbim, Naph·tuʹhim,

1-chronicles/1/12.text: Path·ruʹsim, Cas·luʹhim (from whom the Phi·lisʹtines came), and Caphʹto·rim.

1-chronicles/1/13.text: Caʹnaan became father to Siʹdon, his firstborn, and Heth,

1-chronicles/1/14.text: as well as the Jebʹu·site, the Amʹor·ite, the Girʹga·shite,

1-chronicles/1/15.text: the Hiʹvite, the Arkʹite, the Siʹnite,

1-chronicles/1/16.text: the Arʹvad·ite, the Zemʹa·rite, and the Haʹmath·ite.

1-chronicles/1/17.text: The sons of Shem were Eʹlam, Asʹshur, Ar·pachʹshad, Lud, and Aʹram, and Uz, Hul, Geʹther, and Mash.

1-chronicles/1/18.text: Ar·pachʹshad became father to Sheʹlah, and Sheʹlah became father to Eʹber.

1-chronicles/1/19.text: Two sons were born to Eʹber. The name of the one was Peʹleg, because in his lifetime the earth was divided. The name of his brother was Jokʹtan.

1-chronicles/1/20.text: Jokʹtan became father to Al·moʹdad, Sheʹleph, Ha·zar·maʹveth, Jeʹrah,

1-chronicles/1/23.text: Oʹphir, Havʹi·lah, and Joʹbab; all of these were the sons of Jokʹtan.

1-chronicles/1/28.text: The sons of Abraham were Isaac and Ishʹma·el.

1-chronicles/1/29.text: These are their family origins: Ishʹma·el’s firstborn Ne·baʹioth, then Keʹdar, Adʹbe·el, Mibʹsam,

1-chronicles/1/31.text: Jeʹtur, Naʹphish, and Kedʹe·mah. These were the sons of Ishʹma·el.

1-chronicles/1/32.text: The sons that Ke·tuʹrah, Abraham’s concubine, gave birth to were Zimʹran, Jokʹshan, Meʹdan, Midʹi·an, Ishʹbak, and Shuʹah. The sons of Jokʹshan were Sheʹba and Deʹdan.

1-chronicles/1/33.text: The sons of Midʹi·an were Eʹphah, Eʹpher, Haʹnoch, A·biʹda, and El·daʹah. All of these were the sons of Ke·tuʹrah.

1-chronicles/1/34.text: Abraham became father to Isaac. The sons of Isaac were Eʹsau and Israel.

1-chronicles/1/35.text: The sons of Eʹsau were Elʹi·phaz, Reuʹel, Jeʹush, Jaʹlam, and Korʹah.

1-chronicles/1/36.text: The sons of Elʹi·phaz were Teʹman, Oʹmar, Zeʹpho, Gaʹtam, Keʹnaz, Timʹna, and Amʹa·lek.

1-chronicles/1/37.text: The sons of Reuʹel were Naʹhath, Zeʹrah, Shamʹmah, and Mizʹzah.

1-chronicles/1/38.text: The sons of Seʹir were Loʹtan, Shoʹbal, Zibʹe·on, Aʹnah, Diʹshon, Eʹzer, and Diʹshan.

1-chronicles/1/39.text: The sons of Loʹtan were Hoʹri and Hoʹmam. Loʹtan’s sister was Timʹna.

1-chronicles/1/40.text: The sons of Shoʹbal were Alʹvan, Manʹa·hath, Eʹbal, Sheʹpho, and Oʹnam. The sons of Zibʹe·on were Aʹiah and Aʹnah.

1-chronicles/1/41.text: The son of Aʹnah was Diʹshon. The sons of Diʹshon were Hemʹdan, Eshʹban, Ithʹran, and Cheʹran.

1-chronicles/1/42.text: The sons of Eʹzer were Bilʹhan, Zaʹa·van, and Aʹkan. The sons of Diʹshan were Uz and Aʹran.

1-chronicles/1/43.text: These are the kings who reigned in the land of Eʹdom before any king reigned over the Israelites: Beʹla the son of Beʹor; the name of his city was Dinʹha·bah.

1-chronicles/1/44.text: When Beʹla died, Joʹbab the son of Zeʹrah from Bozʹrah began to reign in his place.

1-chronicles/1/45.text: When Joʹbab died, Huʹsham from the land of the Teʹman·ites began to reign in his place.

1-chronicles/1/46.text: When Huʹsham died, Haʹdad the son of Beʹdad, who defeated Midʹi·an in the territory of Moʹab, began to reign in his place. The name of his city was Aʹvith.

1-chronicles/1/47.text: When Haʹdad died, Samʹlah from Mas·reʹkah began to reign in his place.

1-chronicles/1/48.text: When Samʹlah died, Shaʹul from Re·hoʹboth by the River began to reign in his place.

1-chronicles/1/49.text: When Shaʹul died, Baʹal-haʹnan the son of Achʹbor began to reign in his place.

1-chronicles/1/50.text: When Baʹal-haʹnan died, Haʹdad began to reign in his place. The name of his city was Paʹu, and the name of his wife was Me·hetʹa·bel the daughter of Maʹtred, the daughter of Meʹza·hab.

1-chronicles/1/51.text: Then Haʹdad died. The sheikhs of Eʹdom were Sheikh Timʹna, Sheikh Alʹvah, Sheikh Jeʹtheth,

1-chronicles/1/52.text: Sheikh O·hol·i·baʹmah, Sheikh Eʹlah, Sheikh Piʹnon,

1-chronicles/1/53.text: Sheikh Keʹnaz, Sheikh Teʹman, Sheikh Mibʹzar,

1-chronicles/1/54.text: Sheikh Magʹdi·el, Sheikh Iʹram. These were the sheikhs of Eʹdom.

esther/1/1.text: 1 Now in the days of A·has·u·eʹrus, that is, the A·has·u·eʹrus who ruled over 127 provinces from Inʹdi·a to E·thi·oʹpi·a,

esther/1/2.text: in those days when King A·has·u·eʹrus was sitting on his royal throne in Shuʹshan the citadel,

esther/1/3.text: in the third year of his reign, he held a banquet for all his princes and his servants. The army of Persia and Meʹdi·a, the nobles, and the princes of the provinces were before him,

esther/1/4.text: and he showed them the wealth of his glorious kingdom and the grandeur and the splendor of his magnificence for many days, 180 days.

esther/1/5.text: And when these days were completed, the king held a banquet for seven days for all the people present in Shuʹshan the citadel, from the greatest to the least, in the courtyard of the garden of the king’s palace.

esther/1/6.text: There were linen, fine cotton, and blue material held fast in ropes of fine fabric, purple wool in silver rings, pillars of marble, and couches of gold and silver on a pavement of porphyry, marble, pearl, and black marble.

esther/1/7.text: Wine was served in gold cups; each cup was different from the other, and the royal wine was plentiful, according to the means of the king.

esther/1/8.text: The drinking was according to the rule that no one was under compulsion, for the king had arranged with the officials of his palace that each should do as he pleased.

esther/1/9.text: Queen Vashʹti also held a banquet for the women at the royal house of King A·has·u·eʹrus.

esther/1/10.text: On the seventh day, when the king’s heart was in a cheerful mood because of the wine, he told Me·huʹman, Bizʹtha, Har·boʹna, Bigʹtha, A·bagʹtha, Zeʹthar, and Carʹkas, the seven court officials who were personal attendants to King A·has·u·eʹrus,

esther/1/11.text: to bring before the king Queen Vashʹti, wearing the royal headdress, to show the peoples and the princes her beauty, for she was very beautiful.

esther/1/12.text: But Queen Vashʹti kept refusing to come at the king’s order that was conveyed through the court officials. At this the king became very angry, and his rage flared up within him.

esther/1/13.text: The king then spoke to the wise men who had insight with regard to precedents (for in this way the king’s matter came before all those versed in law and legal cases,

esther/1/14.text: and those closest to him were Car·sheʹna, Sheʹthar, Ad·maʹtha, Tarʹshish, Meʹres, Mar·seʹna, and Me·muʹcan, seven princes of Persia and Meʹdi·a, who had access to the king and who occupied the highest positions in the kingdom).

esther/1/15.text: The king asked: “According to law, what is to be done with Queen Vashʹti because she has not obeyed the order of King A·has·u·eʹrus conveyed through the court officials?”

esther/1/16.text: To this Me·muʹcan said in the presence of the king and the princes: “It is not against the king alone that Queen Vashʹti has done wrong, but against all the princes and against all the peoples in all the provinces of King A·has·u·eʹrus.

esther/1/17.text: For what the queen did will become known by all the wives, and they will despise their husbands and say, ‘King A·has·u·eʹrus said to bring in Queen Vashʹti before him, but she refused to come.’

esther/1/18.text: This very day the princesses of Persia and Meʹdi·a who know about what the queen did will talk to all the princes of the king, resulting in much contempt and indignation.

esther/1/19.text: If it seems good to the king, let a royal decree be issued from him, and let it be written among the laws of Persia and Meʹdi·a, which cannot be repealed, that Vashʹti may never again come in before King A·has·u·eʹrus; and let the king confer her royal position on a woman who is better than she is.

esther/1/20.text: And when the decree of the king is heard in all his vast realm, all the wives will give honor to their husbands, from the greatest to the least.”

esther/1/21.text: This proposal pleased the king and the princes, and the king did what Me·muʹcan said.

esther/1/22.text: So he sent letters to all the royal provinces, to each province in its own script and to each people in its own language, for every husband to be master in his own house and to speak in the language of his own people.

isaiah/51/1.text: 51 “Listen to me, you who are pursuing righteousness, You who are seeking Jehovah. Look to the rock from which you were hewnAnd to the quarry from which you were dug.

isaiah/51/2.text: Look to Abraham your fatherAnd to Sarah who gave birth to you. For he was only one when I called him, And I blessed him and made him many.

isaiah/51/3.text: For Jehovah will comfort Zion. He will bring comfort to all her ruins, And he will make her wilderness like EʹdenAnd her desert plain like the garden of Jehovah. Exultation and rejoicing will be found in her, Thanksgiving and melodious song.

isaiah/51/4.text: Pay attention to me, O my people, And give ear to me, my nation. For a law will go out from me, And my justice I will establish as a light to the peoples.

isaiah/51/5.text: My righteousness draws near. My salvation will go out, And my arms will judge the peoples. In me the islands will hope, And for my arm they will wait.

isaiah/51/6.text: Raise your eyes to the heavens, And look at the earth below. For the heavens will disperse in fragments like smoke;The earth will wear out like a garment, And its inhabitants will die like gnats. But my salvation will be eternal, And my righteousness will never fail.

isaiah/51/7.text: Listen to me, you who know righteousness, The people with my law in their heart. Do not be afraid of the taunts of mortal men, And do not be terrified because of their insults.

isaiah/51/8.text: For a moth will eat them up just like a garment;The clothes moth will devour them like wool. But my righteousness will last forever, And my salvation for all generations.”

isaiah/51/9.text: Awake! Awake! Clothe yourself with strength, O arm of Jehovah! Awake as in the days of long ago, as in past generations. Was it not you who broke Raʹhab to pieces, Who pierced the sea monster?

isaiah/51/10.text: Are you not the one who dried up the sea, the waters of the vast deep? The one who made the depths of the sea a roadway for the repurchased ones to cross?

isaiah/51/11.text: The redeemed ones of Jehovah will return. They will come to Zion with a joyful cry, And unending joy will crown them. Exultation and rejoicing will be theirs, And grief and sighing will flee away.

isaiah/51/12.text: “I myself am the One comforting you. Why should you be afraid of a mortal man who will dieAnd of a son of man who will wither like green grass?

isaiah/51/13.text: Why do you forget Jehovah your Maker, The One who stretched out the heavens and laid the foundation of the earth? And all day long you were in constant fear of the rage of the oppressor, As though he were in a position to bring you to ruin. Where, now, is the rage of the oppressor?

isaiah/51/14.text: The one bent over in chains will soon be set free;He will not die and go into the pit, Nor will his bread be lacking.

isaiah/51/15.text: But I am Jehovah your God, Who stirs up the sea and makes its waves boisterous—Jehovah of armies is his name.

isaiah/51/16.text: I will put my words in your mouth, And with the shadow of my hand I will cover you, In order to plant the heavens and to lay the foundation of the earthAnd to say to Zion, ‘You are my people.’

isaiah/51/17.text: Awake! Awake! Rise up, O Jerusalem, You who have drunk from the hand of Jehovah his cup of wrath. You have drunk the goblet;You have drained out the cup causing staggering.

isaiah/51/18.text: Not one of all the sons whom she bore is there to guide her, And not one of all the sons whom she raised has taken hold of her hand.

isaiah/51/19.text: These two things have befallen you. Who will sympathize with you? Destruction and devastation, hunger and sword! Who will comfort you?

isaiah/51/20.text: Your sons have fainted. They lie down at every street cornerLike wild sheep in the net. They are full of the wrath of Jehovah, the rebuke of your God.”

isaiah/51/21.text: So please listen to this, O woman afflicted and drunk, though not with wine.

isaiah/51/22.text: This is what your Lord Jehovah says, your God who defends his people: “Look! I will take from your hand the cup causing staggering, The goblet, my cup of wrath;You will never drink it again.

isaiah/51/23.text: I will put it into the hand of your tormentors, Those who said to you, ‘Bow down so that we may walk over you!’ So you made your back like the ground, Like a street for them to walk on.”

luke/2/1.text: 2 Now in those days a decree went out from Caesar Au·gusʹtus for all the inhabited earth to be registered.

luke/2/2.text: (This first registration took place when Qui·rinʹi·us was governor of Syria.)

luke/2/3.text: And all the people went to be registered, each one to his own city.

luke/2/4.text: Of course, Joseph also went up from Galʹi·lee, from the city of Nazʹa·reth, into Ju·deʹa, to David’s city, which is called Bethʹle·hem, because of his being a member of the house and family of David.

luke/2/5.text: He went to get registered with Mary, who had been given him in marriage as promised and who was soon to give birth.

luke/2/6.text: While they were there, the time came for her to give birth.

luke/2/7.text: And she gave birth to her son, the firstborn, and she wrapped him in strips of cloth and laid him in a manger, because there was no room for them in the lodging place.

luke/2/8.text: There were also in the same region shepherds living out of doors and keeping watch in the night over their flocks.

luke/2/9.text: Suddenly Jehovah’s angel stood before them, and Jehovah’s glory gleamed around them, and they became very fearful.

luke/2/10.text: But the angel said to them: “Do not be afraid, for look! I am declaring to you good news of a great joy that all the people will have.

luke/2/11.text: For today there was born to you in David’s city a savior, who is Christ the Lord.

luke/2/12.text: And this is a sign for you: You will find an infant wrapped in strips of cloth and lying in a manger.”

luke/2/13.text: Suddenly there was with the angel a multitude of the heavenly army, praising God and saying:

luke/2/14.text: “Glory in the heights above to God, and on earth peace among men of goodwill.”

luke/2/15.text: So when the angels had departed from them into heaven, the shepherds began saying to one another: “Let us by all means go over to Bethʹle·hem and see what has taken place, which Jehovah has made known to us.”

luke/2/16.text: And they went quickly and found Mary as well as Joseph, and the infant lying in the manger.

luke/2/17.text: When they saw this, they made known the message that they had been told concerning this young child.

luke/2/18.text: And all who heard were astonished at what the shepherds told them,

luke/2/19.text: but Mary began to preserve all these sayings, drawing conclusions in her heart.

luke/2/20.text: Then the shepherds went back, glorifying and praising God for all they had heard and seen, just as it had been told to them.

luke/2/21.text: After eight days, when it was time to circumcise him, he was named Jesus, the name given by the angel before he was conceived.

luke/2/22.text: Also, when the time came for purifying them according to the Law of Moses, they brought him up to Jerusalem to present him to Jehovah,

luke/2/23.text: just as it is written in Jehovah’s Law: “Every firstborn male must be called holy to Jehovah.”

luke/2/24.text: And they offered a sacrifice according to what is said in the Law of Jehovah: “a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons.”

luke/2/25.text: And look! there was a man in Jerusalem named Simʹe·on, and this man was righteous and devout, waiting for Israel’s consolation, and holy spirit was upon him.

luke/2/26.text: Furthermore, it had been divinely revealed to him by the holy spirit that he would not see death before he had seen the Christ of Jehovah.

luke/2/27.text: Under the power of the spirit, he now came into the temple, and as the parents brought the young child Jesus in to do for him according to the customary practice of the Law,

luke/2/28.text: he took the child into his arms and praised God and said:

luke/2/29.text: “Now, Sovereign Lord, you are letting your slave go in peace according to your declaration,

luke/2/30.text: because my eyes have seen your means of salvation

luke/2/31.text: that you have prepared in the sight of all the peoples,

luke/2/32.text: a light for removing the veil from the nations and a glory of your people Israel.”

luke/2/33.text: And the child’s father and mother continued wondering at the things being spoken about him.

luke/2/34.text: Also, Simʹe·on blessed them and said to Mary, the child’s mother: “Look! This child is appointed for the falling and the rising again of many in Israel and for a sign to be spoken against

luke/2/35.text: (yes, a long sword will be run through you), in order that the reasonings of many hearts may be revealed.”

luke/2/36.text: Now there was a prophetess, Anna the daughter of Phanʹu·el, of Ashʹer’s tribe. This woman was well along in years and had lived with her husband for seven years after they were married,

luke/2/37.text: and she was a widow now 84 years old. She was never missing from the temple, rendering sacred service night and day with fasting and supplications.

luke/2/38.text: In that very hour she came near and began giving thanks to God and speaking about the child to all who were waiting for Jerusalem’s deliverance.

luke/2/39.text: So when they had carried out all the things according to the Law of Jehovah, they went back into Galʹi·lee to their own city, Nazʹa·reth.

luke/2/40.text: And the young child continued growing and getting strong, being filled with wisdom, and God’s favor continued upon him.

luke/2/41.text: Now his parents were accustomed to go from year to year to Jerusalem for the festival of the Passover.

luke/2/42.text: And when he was 12 years old, they went up according to the custom of the festival.

luke/2/43.text: When the days of the festival were over and they were returning, the boy Jesus remained behind in Jerusalem, and his parents did not notice it.

luke/2/44.text: Assuming that he was in the group traveling together, they went a day’s journey and then began to search for him among the relatives and acquaintances.

luke/2/45.text: But not finding him, they returned to Jerusalem and made a diligent search for him.

luke/2/46.text: Well, after three days they found him in the temple, sitting in the midst of the teachers and listening to them and asking them questions.

luke/2/47.text: But all those listening to him were in constant amazement at his understanding and his answers.

luke/2/48.text: Now when his parents saw him, they were astounded, and his mother said to him: “Child, why did you treat us this way? Here your father and I have been frantically looking for you.”

luke/2/49.text: But he said to them: “Why were you looking for me? Did you not know that I must be in the house of my Father?”

luke/2/50.text: However, they did not understand what he was saying to them.

luke/2/51.text: Then he went down with them and returned to Nazʹa·reth, and he continued subject to them. Also, his mother carefully kept all these sayings in her heart.

luke/2/52.text: And Jesus went on progressing in wisdom and in physical growth and in favor with God and men.

acts/11/1.text: 11 Now the apostles and the brothers who were in Ju·deʹa heard that people of the nations had also accepted the word of God.

acts/11/2.text: So when Peter came up to Jerusalem, the supporters of circumcision began to criticize him,

acts/11/3.text: saying: “You went into the house of men who were not circumcised and ate with them.”

acts/11/4.text: At this Peter went on to explain the matter in detail to them, saying:

acts/11/5.text: “I was in the city of Jopʹpa praying, and while in a trance I saw a vision, something descending like a great linen sheet being let down by its four corners from heaven, and it came right down to me.

acts/11/6.text: Looking closely into it, I observed four-footed animals of the earth, wild beasts, reptiles, and birds of heaven.

acts/11/7.text: I also heard a voice say to me: ‘Get up, Peter, slaughter and eat!’

acts/11/8.text: But I said: ‘Certainly not, Lord, because a defiled or unclean thing has never entered my mouth.’

acts/11/9.text: The second time, the voice from heaven answered: ‘You stop calling defiled the things God has cleansed.’

acts/11/10.text: This happened a third time, and everything was pulled up again into heaven.

acts/11/11.text: Also just at that moment, three men were standing at the house where we were staying, having been sent to me from Caes·a·reʹa.

acts/11/12.text: Then the spirit told me to go with them, not doubting at all. But these six brothers also went with me, and we entered into the house of the man.

acts/11/13.text: “He reported to us how he saw the angel stand in his house and say: ‘Send men to Jopʹpa and summon Simon who is called Peter,

acts/11/14.text: and he will tell you things by which you and all your household may get saved.’

acts/11/15.text: But when I started to speak, the holy spirit fell on them just as it did also on us in the beginning.

acts/11/16.text: At this I recalled the saying of the Lord, how he used to say: ‘John baptized with water, but you will be baptized with holy spirit.’

acts/11/17.text: If, therefore, God gave the same free gift to them that he gave to us who have believed in the Lord Jesus Christ, who was I that I should be able to hinder God?”

acts/11/18.text: When they heard these things, they stopped objecting, and they glorified God, saying: “So, then, God has also granted to people of the nations repentance leading to life.”

acts/11/19.text: Now those who had been scattered by the tribulation that arose over Stephen went as far as Phoe·niʹcia, Cyʹprus, and Antioch, but they spoke the word only to the Jews.

acts/11/20.text: However, some of the men among them from Cyʹprus and Cy·reʹne came to Antioch and began talking to the Greek-speaking people, declaring the good news of the Lord Jesus.

acts/11/21.text: Furthermore, the hand of Jehovah was with them, and a great number became believers and turned to the Lord.

acts/11/22.text: The report about them reached the ears of the congregation in Jerusalem, and they sent out Barʹna·bas as far as Antioch.

acts/11/23.text: When he arrived and saw the undeserved kindness of God, he rejoiced and began to encourage them all to continue in the Lord with heartfelt resolve;

acts/11/24.text: for he was a good man and full of holy spirit and faith. And a considerable crowd was added to the Lord.

acts/11/25.text: So he went to Tarsus to make a thorough search for Saul.

acts/11/26.text: After he found him, he brought him to Antioch. So for a whole year they assembled with them in the congregation and taught quite a crowd, and it was first in Antioch that the disciples were by divine providence called Christians.

acts/11/27.text: In those days prophets came down from Jerusalem to Antioch.

acts/11/28.text: One of them named Agʹa·bus stood up and foretold through the spirit that a great famine was about to come on the entire inhabited earth, which, in fact, did take place in the time of Claudius.

acts/11/29.text: So the disciples determined, each according to what he could afford, to send relief to the brothers living in Ju·deʹa;

acts/11/30.text: and this they did, sending it to the elders by the hand of Barʹna·bas and Saul.

joshua/9/1.text: 9 When all the kings who were on the west side of the Jordan heard what had happened, those in the mountainous region, in the She·pheʹlah, along the entire coast of the Great Sea, and in front of Lebʹa·non—the Hitʹtites, the Amʹor·ites, the Caʹnaan·ites, the Perʹiz·zites, the Hiʹvites, and the Jebʹu·sites—

joshua/9/2.text: they formed an alliance to fight against Joshua and Israel.

joshua/9/3.text: The inhabitants of Gibʹe·on also heard what Joshua had done to Jerʹi·cho and Aʹi.

joshua/9/4.text: So they acted shrewdly and put provisions into worn-out sacks on their donkeys, along with worn-out wineskins that had burst and had been mended;

joshua/9/5.text: they also had worn-out and patched sandals on their feet, and they were wearing worn-out garments. All the bread of their provisions was dry and crumbly.

joshua/9/6.text: Then they went to Joshua at the camp at Gilʹgal and said to him and the men of Israel: “We have come from a distant land. Now make a covenant with us.”

joshua/9/7.text: But the men of Israel said to the Hiʹvites: “Perhaps you are living near us. So how can we make a covenant with you?”

joshua/9/8.text: They replied to Joshua: “We are your servants.” Then Joshua said to them: “Who are you, and where do you come from?”

joshua/9/9.text: At this they said to him: “Your servants have come from a very distant land out of regard for the name of Jehovah your God, because we have heard about his fame and about all he did in Egypt

joshua/9/10.text: and about all he did to the two kings of the Amʹor·ites who were on the other side of the Jordan, King Siʹhon of Heshʹbon and King Og of Baʹshan, who was in Ashʹta·roth.

joshua/9/11.text: So our elders and all the inhabitants of our land told us, ‘Take provisions with you for the journey and go to meet them. Tell them: “We will be your servants; now make a covenant with us.”’

joshua/9/12.text: This bread that we took as our provisions was still hot on the day we left our houses to come here to you. Now you can see it is dry and crumbly.

joshua/9/13.text: And these wineskins were new when we filled them, but now they have burst. And our garments and sandals have worn out because of the great length of the journey.”

joshua/9/14.text: At that the men took some of their provisions, but they did not inquire of Jehovah.

joshua/9/15.text: So Joshua made peace with them and made a covenant with them to let them live, and that is what the chieftains of the assembly swore to them in an oath.

joshua/9/16.text: At the end of three days, after they made a covenant with them, they heard that they lived nearby, in their vicinity.

joshua/9/17.text: Then the Israelites set out and came to their cities on the third day; their cities were Gibʹe·on, Che·phiʹrah, Be·erʹoth, and Kirʹi·ath-jeʹa·rim.

joshua/9/18.text: But the Israelites did not attack them, because the chieftains of the assembly had sworn an oath to them by Jehovah the God of Israel. So all the assembly began to murmur against the chieftains.

joshua/9/19.text: At this all the chieftains said to the entire assembly: “Since we swore an oath to them by Jehovah the God of Israel, we are not allowed to hurt them.

joshua/9/20.text: This is what we will do: We will let them live, so that there is no indignation against us because of the oath that we swore to them.”

joshua/9/21.text: And the chieftains added: “Let them live, but let them become gatherers of wood and drawers of water for all the assembly.” This is what the chieftains promised them.

joshua/9/22.text: Joshua now called them and said to them: “Why did you trick us by saying, ‘We are from a place very far away from you, ’ when you really live right among us?

joshua/9/23.text: From now on you are cursed, and you will always occupy a slave’s position as gatherers of wood and drawers of water for the house of my God.”

joshua/9/24.text: They answered Joshua: “It was because your servants were plainly told that Jehovah your God had commanded Moses his servant to give you all the land and to annihilate all its inhabitants from before you. So we were afraid for our lives because of you, and that is why we did this.

joshua/9/25.text: Now we are at your mercy. Do to us whatever you think is good and right.”

joshua/9/26.text: And that is what he did with them; he saved them from the hands of the Israelites, and they did not kill them.

joshua/9/27.text: But that day Joshua made them gatherers of wood and drawers of water for the assembly and for Jehovah’s altar at the place that He should choose, and they remain so to this day.

psalms/105/1.text: 105 Give thanks to Jehovah, call on his name, Make his deeds known among the peoples!

psalms/105/2.text: Sing to him, sing praises to him, Ponder over all his wonderful works.

psalms/105/3.text: Boast about his holy name. Let the hearts of those seeking Jehovah rejoice.

psalms/105/4.text: Search for Jehovah and his strength. Seek his face constantly.

psalms/105/5.text: Remember the wonderful works he has performed, His miracles and the judgments he has pronounced,

psalms/105/6.text: You offspring of Abraham his servant, You sons of Jacob, his chosen ones.

psalms/105/7.text: He is Jehovah our God. His judgments are throughout the earth.

psalms/105/8.text: He remembers his covenant forever, The promise he made, to a thousand generations,

psalms/105/9.text: The covenant he made with Abraham, And the oath he swore to Isaac,

psalms/105/10.text: Which he established as a decree to JacobAnd as a lasting covenant to Israel,

psalms/105/11.text: Saying, “I will give you the land of CaʹnaanAs your allotted inheritance.”

psalms/105/12.text: This was when they were few in number, Yes, very few, and they were foreigners in the land.

psalms/105/13.text: They walked about from nation to nation, From one kingdom to another people.

psalms/105/14.text: He did not allow any man to oppress them, But on their account he reproved kings,

psalms/105/15.text: Saying, “Do not touch my anointed ones, And to my prophets do nothing bad.”

psalms/105/16.text: He called down a famine on the land;He cut off their supply of bread.

psalms/105/17.text: He sent ahead of them a manWho was sold to be a slave, Joseph.

psalms/105/18.text: With fetters they bound his feet, His neck was put in irons;

psalms/105/19.text: Until the time that his word proved true, The saying of Jehovah is what refined him.

psalms/105/20.text: The king sent to release him, The ruler of the peoples set him free.

psalms/105/21.text: He made him master of his household, Ruler over all his property,

psalms/105/22.text: To have authority over his princes as he pleasedAnd to teach his elders wisdom.

psalms/105/23.text: Then Israel came into Egypt, And Jacob lived as a foreigner in the land of Ham.

psalms/105/24.text: God made his people very fruitful;He made them mightier than their adversaries,

psalms/105/25.text: Whose hearts he let change to hate his people, To plot against his servants.

psalms/105/26.text: He sent his servant Moses, And Aaron, whom he had chosen.

psalms/105/27.text: They performed his signs among them, His miracles in the land of Ham.

psalms/105/28.text: He sent darkness and the land became dark;They did not rebel against his words.

psalms/105/29.text: He changed their waters into bloodAnd killed their fish.

psalms/105/30.text: Their land swarmed with frogs, Even in the royal chambers.

psalms/105/31.text: He ordered the gadflies to invadeAnd gnats in all their territories.

psalms/105/32.text: He turned their rain to hailAnd sent lightning on their land.

psalms/105/33.text: He struck their vines and their fig treesAnd shattered the trees of their territory.

psalms/105/34.text: He said that the locusts should invade, Young locusts without number.

psalms/105/35.text: They devoured all the vegetation in the land, And they devoured the produce of the ground.

psalms/105/36.text: Then he struck down every firstborn in their land, The beginning of their procreative power.

psalms/105/37.text: He brought his people out with silver and gold;And no one among his tribes stumbled.

psalms/105/38.text: Egypt rejoiced when they left, For the dread of Israel had fallen on them.

psalms/105/39.text: He spread a cloud to screen them off And fire to give light by night.

psalms/105/40.text: They asked, and he brought quail;He kept satisfying them with bread from heaven.

psalms/105/41.text: He opened a rock, and waters flowed out;These flowed through the desert like a river.

psalms/105/42.text: For he remembered the holy promise he had made to Abraham his servant.

psalms/105/43.text: So he brought out his people with exultation, His chosen ones with a joyful cry.

psalms/105/44.text: He gave them the lands of nations;They inherited what other peoples had worked hard to produce,

psalms/105/45.text: So that they would keep his decreesAnd observe his laws. Praise Jah!

deuteronomy/23/1.text: 23 “No man who has been castrated by having his testicles crushed or who has had his male organ cut off may come into the congregation of Jehovah.

deuteronomy/23/2.text: “No illegitimate son may come into the congregation of Jehovah. Even to the tenth generation, none of his descendants may come into the congregation of Jehovah.

deuteronomy/23/3.text: “No Amʹmon·ite or Moʹab·ite may come into the congregation of Jehovah. Even to the tenth generation, none of their descendants may ever come into the congregation of Jehovah,

deuteronomy/23/4.text: because they did not come to your aid with food and water when you were on the way going out of Egypt, and because they hired against you Baʹlaam the son of Beʹor from Peʹthor of Mes·o·po·taʹmi·a to curse you.

deuteronomy/23/5.text: But Jehovah your God refused to listen to Baʹlaam. Rather, Jehovah your God changed the curse into a blessing for you, because Jehovah your God loved you.

deuteronomy/23/6.text: You should never seek their welfare or their prosperity all your days.

deuteronomy/23/7.text: “You must not hate an Eʹdom·ite, for he is your brother. “You must not hate an Egyptian, for you became a foreign resident in his country.

deuteronomy/23/8.text: The third generation of children born to them may enter the congregation of Jehovah.

deuteronomy/23/9.text: “When you are encamped against your enemies, you should avoid anything bad.

deuteronomy/23/10.text: If a man becomes unclean because of a nocturnal emission, he should go outside the camp and not reenter the camp.

deuteronomy/23/11.text: When evening falls, he should wash with water, and then he may return to the camp at sunset.

deuteronomy/23/12.text: A private place should be designated for use outside the camp, and there is where you should go.

deuteronomy/23/13.text: A peg should be part of your equipment. When you squat outside, you should dig a hole with it and then cover your excrement.

deuteronomy/23/14.text: For Jehovah your God is walking about within your camp to deliver you and to hand over your enemies to you, and your camp must be holy, so that he does not see anything indecent in you and turn away from accompanying you.

deuteronomy/23/15.text: “You should not hand over a slave to his master when he escapes from his master and comes to you.

deuteronomy/23/16.text: He may dwell among you in whatever place he chooses in one of your cities, wherever he likes. You must not mistreat him.

deuteronomy/23/17.text: “None of the daughters of Israel may become a temple prostitute, neither may anyone of the sons of Israel become a temple prostitute.

deuteronomy/23/18.text: You must not bring the price paid to a female prostitute or the price paid to a male prostitute into the house of Jehovah your God to fulfill a vow, for both of them are something detestable to Jehovah your God.

deuteronomy/23/19.text: “You must not make your brother pay interest, whether interest on money, on food, or on anything on which interest may be charged.

deuteronomy/23/20.text: You may make a foreigner pay interest, but you must not make your brother pay interest, so that Jehovah your God may bless you in every undertaking of yours in the land you are going to take possession of.

deuteronomy/23/21.text: “If you make a vow to Jehovah your God, do not be slow about paying it. For Jehovah your God will surely require it of you; otherwise, it will be a sin on your part.

deuteronomy/23/22.text: But if you refrain from making a vow, you will not be guilty of sin.

deuteronomy/23/23.text: The word of your lips you should keep, and you must carry out what your own mouth vowed as a voluntary offering to Jehovah your God.

deuteronomy/23/24.text: “If you enter your neighbor’s vineyard, you may eat enough grapes to satisfy your appetite, but you should not put any in your container.

deuteronomy/23/25.text: “If you go into your neighbor’s field of standing grain, you may pluck the ripe ears with your hand, but you should not put a sickle to your neighbor’s grain.

genesis/15/1.text: 15 After this the word of Jehovah came to Aʹbram in a vision, saying: “Do not fear, Aʹbram. I am a shield for you. Your reward will be very great.”

genesis/15/2.text: Aʹbram replied: “Sovereign Lord Jehovah, what will you give me, seeing that I continue childless and the one who will inherit my house is a man of Damascus, E·li·eʹzer?”

genesis/15/3.text: Aʹbram added: “You have given me no offspring, and a member of my household is succeeding me as heir.”

genesis/15/4.text: But look! Jehovah’s word in reply to him was, “This man will not succeed you as heir, but your own son will succeed you as heir.”

genesis/15/5.text: He now brought him outside and said: “Look up, please, to the heavens and count the stars, if you are able to do so.” Then he said to him: “So your offspring will become.”

genesis/15/6.text: And he put faith in Jehovah, and He counted it to him as righteousness.

genesis/15/7.text: Then he added: “I am Jehovah, who brought you out of Ur of the Chal·deʹans to give you this land as your possession.”

genesis/15/8.text: To this he said: “Sovereign Lord Jehovah, how will I know that I will take possession of it?”

genesis/15/9.text: He replied to him: “Take for me a three-year-old heifer, a three-year-old female goat, a three-year-old ram, a turtledove, and a young pigeon.”

genesis/15/10.text: So he took all of these and cut them in two and put each part opposite the other, but he did not cut up the birds.

genesis/15/11.text: Then the birds of prey began to descend on the carcasses, but Aʹbram kept driving them away.

genesis/15/12.text: When the sun was about to set, a deep sleep fell upon Aʹbram and a great and frightening darkness descended on him.

genesis/15/13.text: Then He said to Aʹbram: “Know for certain that your offspring will be foreigners in a land not theirs and that the people there will enslave them and afflict them for 400 years.

genesis/15/14.text: But I will judge the nation they will serve, and after that they will go out with many goods.

genesis/15/15.text: As for you, you will go to your forefathers in peace; you will be buried at a good old age.

genesis/15/16.text: But they will return here in the fourth generation, because the error of the Amʹor·ites has not yet reached its full measure.”

genesis/15/17.text: When the sun had set and it had become very dark, a smoking furnace appeared, and a fiery torch passed between the pieces.

genesis/15/18.text: On that day Jehovah made with Aʹbram a covenant, saying: “To your offspring I will give this land, from the river of Egypt to the great river, the river Eu·phraʹtes:

genesis/15/19.text: the land of the Kenʹites, the Kenʹiz·zites, the Kadʹmon·ites,

genesis/15/20.text: the Hitʹtites, the Perʹiz·zites, the Rephʹa·im,

genesis/15/21.text: the Amʹor·ites, the Caʹnaan·ites, the Girʹga·shites, and the Jebʹu·sites.”

numbers/31/2.text: “Take vengeance for the Israelites on the Midʹi·an·ites. Afterward you will be gathered to your people.”

numbers/31/3.text: So Moses spoke to the people, saying: “Equip men from among you for battle against Midʹi·an and to execute Jehovah’s vengeance on Midʹi·an.

numbers/31/4.text: You should send 1, 000 of each tribe of all the tribes of Israel into the army.”

numbers/31/5.text: So from the thousands of Israel, 1, 000 were assigned from each tribe, 12, 000 equipped for battle.

numbers/31/6.text: Then Moses sent them out, 1, 000 from each tribe to the army, along with Phinʹe·has the son of El·e·aʹzar the priest for the army, who had the holy utensils and the signal trumpets in his hand.

numbers/31/7.text: They waged war against Midʹi·an, just as Jehovah had commanded Moses, and they killed every male.

numbers/31/8.text: Along with the others slain, they killed the kings of Midʹi·an, namely, Eʹvi, Reʹkem, Zur, Hur, and Reʹba, the five kings of Midʹi·an. They also killed Baʹlaam the son of Beʹor with the sword.

numbers/31/9.text: But the Israelites carried off captive the women and children of Midʹi·an. They also plundered all their domestic animals, all their livestock, and all their possessions.

numbers/31/10.text: And all their cities in which they had settled and all their encampments they burned with fire.

numbers/31/11.text: And they took all the spoil and all the plunder, both humans and animals.

numbers/31/12.text: Then they brought the captives, the plunder, and the spoil to Moses and El·e·aʹzar the priest and to the assembly of the Israelites, to the camp in the desert plains of Moʹab near the Jordan at Jerʹi·cho.

numbers/31/13.text: Then Moses and El·e·aʹzar the priest and all the chieftains of the assembly went out to meet them outside the camp.

numbers/31/14.text: But Moses grew indignant at the appointed men of the combat forces, the chiefs of the thousands and the chiefs of the hundreds who were coming in from the military expedition.

numbers/31/15.text: Moses said to them: “Have you preserved all the females alive?

numbers/31/16.text: Look! They are the ones who by Baʹlaam’s word induced the Israelites to commit unfaithfulness toward Jehovah over the affair of Peʹor, so that the scourge came upon the assembly of Jehovah.

numbers/31/17.text: Now you should kill every male among the children and kill every woman who has had sexual relations with a man.

numbers/31/18.text: But you may keep alive all the young girls who have not had sexual relations with a man.

numbers/31/19.text: And you should camp outside the camp seven days. Every one of you who has killed someone and every one of you who has touched someone slain should purify himself on the third day and on the seventh day, you and your captives.

numbers/31/20.text: And you should purify from sin every garment, every article of skin, everything made of goat hair, and every article of wood.”

numbers/31/21.text: El·e·aʹzar the priest then said to the men of the army who had gone into the battle: “This is the statute of the law that Jehovah commanded Moses,

numbers/31/22.text: ‘Only the gold, the silver, the copper, the iron, the tin, and the lead,

numbers/31/23.text: everything that can be processed with fire, you should pass through the fire, and it will be clean. However, it should also be purified by the water for cleansing. Everything that cannot be processed with fire, you should pass through the water.

numbers/31/24.text: And you should wash your garments on the seventh day and be clean, and then you may come into the camp.’”

numbers/31/25.text: Jehovah then said this to Moses:

numbers/31/26.text: “Take an inventory of the plunder, counting the captives both of humans and animals; do this together with El·e·aʹzar the priest and the heads of the paternal houses of the assembly.

numbers/31/27.text: Divide what was plundered into two parts to be shared between those in the army who took part in the battle and all the rest of the assembly.

numbers/31/28.text: As a tax for Jehovah, you should take from the soldiers who went out into the battle one soul out of every 500, of the people, the herd, the donkeys, and the flock.

numbers/31/29.text: You should take it from their half and give it to El·e·aʹzar the priest as Jehovah’s contribution.

numbers/31/30.text: From the half given to the Israelites, you should take one out of 50, of the people, the herd, the donkeys, the flock, and every sort of domestic animal, and give them to the Levites, who care for the responsibilities connected with Jehovah’s tabernacle.”

numbers/31/31.text: So Moses and El·e·aʹzar the priest did just as Jehovah had commanded Moses.

numbers/31/32.text: The spoils, the rest of the plunder that the people of the expedition had taken, amounted to 675, 000 of the flock,

numbers/31/35.text: The women who had not had sexual relations with a man amounted to 32, 000 women.

numbers/31/36.text: The half that was the share of those who went out into the battle amounted to 337, 500 of the flock.

numbers/31/37.text: The tax for Jehovah from the flock amounted to 675.

numbers/31/38.text: And there were 36, 000 of the herd, and the tax on them for Jehovah was 72.

numbers/31/39.text: And there were 30, 500 donkeys, and the tax on them for Jehovah was 61.

numbers/31/40.text: And there were 16, 000 humans, and the tax on them for Jehovah was 32 persons.

numbers/31/41.text: Then Moses gave the tax as Jehovah’s contribution to El·e·aʹzar the priest, just as Jehovah had commanded Moses.

numbers/31/42.text: From the half belonging to the Israelites, which Moses had divided off from the portion that belonged to the men who waged war,

numbers/31/43.text: that half of the flock amounted to 337, 500,

numbers/31/47.text: Then Moses took from the half belonging to the Israelites one out of 50, of the people and of the animals, and gave them to the Levites, who cared for the responsibility of Jehovah’s tabernacle, just as Jehovah had commanded Moses.

numbers/31/48.text: Then the appointed men who were of the thousands of the army, the chiefs of the thousands and the chiefs of the hundreds, approached Moses,

numbers/31/49.text: and they said to Moses: “Your servants have taken the count of the men of war who are under our command, and not one has been reported missing from us.

numbers/31/50.text: So let us each present what he has found as Jehovah’s offering, articles of gold, ankle chains, bracelets, signet rings, earrings, and other jewelry, in order to make atonement for ourselves before Jehovah.”

numbers/31/51.text: So Moses and El·e·aʹzar the priest accepted the gold from them, all the jewelry.

numbers/31/52.text: All the gold of the contribution that they made to Jehovah amounted to 16, 750 shekels, from the chiefs of the thousands and the chiefs of the hundreds.

numbers/31/53.text: The men of the army had each taken plunder for himself.

numbers/31/54.text: Moses and El·e·aʹzar the priest accepted the gold from the chiefs of the thousands and of the hundreds and brought it into the tent of meeting as a reminder for the people of Israel before Jehovah.

joshua/13/1.text: 13 Now Joshua had grown old and was advanced in years. So Jehovah said to him: “You have grown old and are advanced in years; but much of the land remains to be taken in possession.

joshua/13/2.text: This is the land remaining: all the regions of the Phi·lisʹtines and all the Geshʹur·ites

joshua/13/3.text: (from the branch of the Nile that is east of Egypt up to the border of Ekʹron to the north, which used to be considered Caʹnaan·ite territory) including that of the five lords of the Phi·lisʹtines—the Gazʹites, the Ashʹdod·ites, the Ashʹke·lon·ites, the Gitʹtites, and the Ekʹron·ites; that of the Avʹvim

joshua/13/4.text: to the south; all the land of the Caʹnaan·ites; Me·arʹah, which belongs to the Si·doʹni·ans, as far as Aʹphek, to the border of the Amʹor·ites;

joshua/13/5.text: the land of the Geʹbal·ites and all of Lebʹa·non toward the east, from Baʹal-gad at the base of Mount Herʹmon to Leʹbo-haʹmath;

joshua/13/6.text: all the inhabitants of the mountainous region from Lebʹa·non to Misʹre·photh-maʹim; and all the Si·doʹni·ans. I will drive them out before the Israelites. You have only to assign it to Israel as an inheritance, just as I have commanded you.

joshua/13/7.text: Now you must apportion this land as an inheritance to the nine tribes and the half tribe of Ma·nasʹseh.”

joshua/13/8.text: With the other half tribe, the Reuʹben·ites and the Gadʹites took their inheritance that Moses gave them on the east side of the Jordan, just as Moses the servant of Jehovah had given them:

joshua/13/9.text: from A·roʹer, which is on the rim of the Arʹnon Valley, and the city that is in the middle of the valley, and all the tableland of Medʹe·ba as far as Diʹbon;

joshua/13/10.text: and all the cities of King Siʹhon of the Amʹor·ites, who reigned in Heshʹbon, up to the border of the Amʹmon·ites;

joshua/13/11.text: also Gilʹe·ad and the territory of the Geshʹur·ites and the Ma·acʹa·thites and all Mount Herʹmon and all Baʹshan as far as Salʹe·cah;

joshua/13/12.text: all the royal realm of Og in Baʹshan, who reigned in Ashʹta·roth and in Edʹre·i. (He was one of the last of the Rephʹa·im.) Moses defeated them and drove them out.

joshua/13/13.text: But the Israelites did not drive out the Geshʹur·ites and the Ma·acʹa·thites, for Geshʹur and Maʹa·cath live in the midst of Israel to this day.

joshua/13/14.text: It was only to the tribe of the Levites that he did not give an inheritance. The offerings made by fire to Jehovah the God of Israel are their inheritance, just as he promised them.

joshua/13/15.text: Then Moses gave an inheritance to the tribe of the Reuʹben·ites by their families,

joshua/13/16.text: and their territory was from A·roʹer, which is on the rim of the Arʹnon Valley, and the city in the middle of the valley, and all the tableland by Medʹe·ba;

joshua/13/17.text: Heshʹbon and all its towns on the tableland, Diʹbon, Baʹmoth-baʹal, Beth-baʹal-meʹon,

joshua/13/19.text: Kir·i·a·thaʹim, Sibʹmah, and Zeʹreth-shaʹhar on the mountain of the valley,

joshua/13/20.text: Beth-peʹor, the slopes of Pisʹgah, Beth-jeshʹi·moth,

joshua/13/21.text: all the cities of the tableland, and all the royal realm of King Siʹhon of the Amʹor·ites, who reigned in Heshʹbon. Moses defeated him and the Midʹi·an·ite chieftains Eʹvi, Reʹkem, Zur, Hur, and Reʹba, vassals of Siʹhon who were dwelling in the land.

joshua/13/22.text: Baʹlaam the son of Beʹor, the diviner, was one whom the Israelites killed with the sword along with the rest who were slain.

joshua/13/23.text: The boundary of the Reuʹben·ites was the Jordan; and this territory was the inheritance of the Reuʹben·ites by their families, with the cities and their settlements.

joshua/13/24.text: Furthermore, Moses gave an inheritance to the tribe of Gad, the Gadʹites by their families,

joshua/13/25.text: and their territory included Jaʹzer and all the cities of Gilʹe·ad and half of the land of the Amʹmon·ites as far as A·roʹer, which faces Rabʹbah;

joshua/13/26.text: and from Heshʹbon to Raʹmath-mizʹpeh and Betʹo·nim, and from Ma·ha·naʹim to the border of Deʹbir;

joshua/13/27.text: and in the valley, Beth-haʹram, Beth-nimʹrah, Sucʹcoth, and Zaʹphon, the rest of the royal realm of King Siʹhon of Heshʹbon, with the Jordan as the border from the lower end of the Sea of Chinʹne·reth on the east side of the Jordan.

joshua/13/28.text: This was the inheritance of the Gadʹites by their families, with the cities and their settlements.

joshua/13/29.text: Further, Moses gave an inheritance to the half tribe of Ma·nasʹseh, to half of the tribe of Ma·nasʹseh by their families.

joshua/13/30.text: And their territory extended from Ma·ha·naʹim and took in all of Baʹshan, all the royal realm of King Og of Baʹshan, and all the tent villages of Jaʹir in Baʹshan, 60 towns.

joshua/13/31.text: And half of Gilʹe·ad, and Ashʹta·roth and Edʹre·i, the cities of the royal realm of Og in Baʹshan, went to the sons of Maʹchir the son of Ma·nasʹseh, to half of the sons of Maʹchir by their families.

joshua/13/32.text: These were the inheritances that Moses gave them on the desert plains of Moʹab beyond the Jordan, east of Jerʹi·cho.

joshua/13/33.text: But to the tribe of the Levites, Moses did not give an inheritance. Jehovah the God of Israel is their inheritance, just as he promised them.

numbers/20/1.text: 20 In the first month, the entire assembly of the Israelites came into the wilderness of Zin, and the people began dwelling in Kaʹdesh. It was there that Mirʹi·am died and was buried.

numbers/20/2.text: Now there was no water for the assembly, and they gathered together against Moses and Aaron.

numbers/20/3.text: The people were quarreling with Moses, saying: “If only we had died when our brothers died before Jehovah!

numbers/20/4.text: Why have you brought Jehovah’s congregation into this wilderness for us and our livestock to die here?

numbers/20/5.text: And why have you led us up out of Egypt to bring us into this evil place? It is no place for seed and figs and vines and pomegranates, and there is no water to drink.”

numbers/20/6.text: Then Moses and Aaron came from before the congregation to the entrance of the tent of meeting and fell with their faces to the ground, and Jehovah’s glory began to appear to them.

numbers/20/8.text: “Take the rod and call the assembly together, you and Aaron your brother, and speak to the crag before their eyes that it may give its water, and you will bring out water for them from the crag and give the assembly and their livestock something to drink.”

numbers/20/9.text: So Moses took the rod from before Jehovah, just as He had commanded him.

numbers/20/10.text: Then Moses and Aaron called the congregation together before the crag, and he said to them: “Hear, now, you rebels! Must we bring out water for you from this crag?”

numbers/20/11.text: With that Moses lifted his hand up and struck the crag twice with his rod, and much water began to pour out, and the assembly and their livestock began to drink.

numbers/20/12.text: Jehovah later said to Moses and Aaron: “Because you did not show faith in me and sanctify me before the eyes of the people of Israel, you will not bring this congregation into the land that I will give them.”

numbers/20/13.text: These are the waters of Merʹi·bah, where the Israelites quarreled with Jehovah, so that he was sanctified among them.

numbers/20/14.text: Then Moses sent messengers from Kaʹdesh to the king of Eʹdom: “This is what your brother Israel says, ‘You well know all the hardship that we have experienced.

numbers/20/15.text: Our fathers went to Egypt, and we dwelled in Egypt many years, and the Egyptians mistreated us and our fathers.

numbers/20/16.text: Finally we cried out to Jehovah, and he heard us and sent an angel and brought us out of Egypt, and here we are in Kaʹdesh, a city on the border of your territory.

numbers/20/17.text: Please let us pass through your land. We will not pass through any field or vineyard, and we will not drink the water of any well. We will march on the King’s Road without turning to the right or the left until we pass through your territory.’”

numbers/20/18.text: However, Eʹdom said to him: “You may not pass through our territory. If you do, I will come out with the sword to meet you.”

numbers/20/19.text: In turn the Israelites said to him: “By the highway we will go up, and if we and our livestock drink your water, we will pay for it. We want nothing more than to pass through on foot.”

numbers/20/20.text: Still he said: “You may not pass through.” With that Eʹdom came out to encounter him with many people and a strong army.

numbers/20/21.text: So Eʹdom refused to allow Israel to pass through his territory; therefore, Israel turned away from him.

numbers/20/22.text: The people of Israel, the entire assembly, departed from Kaʹdesh and came to Mount Hor.

numbers/20/23.text: Then Jehovah said to Moses and Aaron in Mount Hor by the border of the land of Eʹdom:

numbers/20/24.text: “Aaron will be gathered to his people. He will not enter the land that I will give to the Israelites, because you both rebelled against my order regarding the waters of Merʹi·bah.

numbers/20/25.text: Take Aaron and his son El·e·aʹzar and bring them up into Mount Hor.

numbers/20/26.text: Remove Aaron’s garments and clothe El·e·aʹzar his son with them, and Aaron will die there.”

numbers/20/27.text: So Moses did just as Jehovah had commanded, and they climbed Mount Hor before the eyes of all the assembly.

numbers/20/28.text: Then Moses removed Aaron’s garments and clothed El·e·aʹzar his son with them. After that Aaron died there on the top of the mountain. And Moses and El·e·aʹzar came down from the mountain.

numbers/20/29.text: When all the assembly saw that Aaron had died, the entire house of Israel wept for Aaron for 30 days.

joshua/12/1.text: 12 Now these are the kings of the land whom the Israelites defeated, whose land they took possession of on the east side of the Jordan, from the Arʹnon Valley up to Mount Herʹmon and all the Arʹa·bah toward the east:

joshua/12/2.text: King Siʹhon of the Amʹor·ites, who lived in Heshʹbon and ruled from A·roʹer, which was on the rim of the Arʹnon Valley, and from the middle of the valley, and half of Gilʹe·ad as far as the Valley of Jabʹbok, the boundary of the Amʹmon·ites.

joshua/12/3.text: He also ruled over the Arʹa·bah as far as the Sea of Chinʹne·reth toward the east and as far as the Sea of the Arʹa·bah, the Salt Sea, to the east in the direction of Beth-jeshʹi·moth, and toward the south under the slopes of Pisʹgah.

joshua/12/4.text: Also the territory of King Og of Baʹshan, who was one of the last of the Rephʹa·im and who lived in Ashʹta·roth and Edʹre·i

joshua/12/5.text: and ruled in Mount Herʹmon, in Salʹe·cah, and in all Baʹshan, as far as the boundary of the Geshʹur·ites and the Ma·acʹa·thites, and half of Gilʹe·ad, to the territory of King Siʹhon of Heshʹbon.

joshua/12/6.text: Moses the servant of Jehovah and the Israelites defeated them, after which Moses the servant of Jehovah gave their land as a possession to the Reuʹben·ites, the Gadʹites, and the half tribe of Ma·nasʹseh.

joshua/12/7.text: These are the kings of the land whom Joshua and the Israelites defeated on the west side of the Jordan, from Baʹal-gad in the Valley of Lebʹa·non and as far as Mount Haʹlak, which goes up to Seʹir, after which Joshua gave their land to the tribes of Israel as a possession by their shares,

joshua/12/8.text: in the mountainous region, in the She·pheʹlah, in the Arʹa·bah, on the slopes, in the wilderness, and in the Negʹeb—the land of the Hitʹtites, the Amʹor·ites, the Caʹnaan·ites, the Perʹiz·zites, the Hiʹvites, and the Jebʹu·sites:

joshua/12/9.text: The king of Jerʹi·cho, one; the king of Aʹi, which was beside Bethʹel, one;

joshua/12/10.text: the king of Jerusalem, one; the king of Hebʹron, one;

joshua/12/11.text: the king of Jarʹmuth, one; the king of Laʹchish, one;

joshua/12/12.text: the king of Egʹlon, one; the king of Geʹzer, one;

joshua/12/13.text: the king of Deʹbir, one; the king of Geʹder, one;

joshua/12/14.text: the king of Horʹmah, one; the king of Aʹrad, one;

joshua/12/15.text: the king of Libʹnah, one; the king of A·dulʹlam, one;

joshua/12/16.text: the king of Mak·keʹdah, one; the king of Bethʹel, one;

joshua/12/17.text: the king of Tapʹpu·ah, one; the king of Heʹpher, one;

joshua/12/18.text: the king of Aʹphek, one; the king of Las·sharʹon, one;

joshua/12/19.text: the king of Maʹdon, one; the king of Haʹzor, one;

joshua/12/20.text: the king of Shimʹron-meʹron, one; the king of Achʹshaph, one;

joshua/12/21.text: the king of Taʹa·nach, one; the king of Me·gidʹdo, one;

joshua/12/22.text: the king of Keʹdesh, one; the king of Jokʹne·am in Carʹmel, one;

joshua/12/23.text: the king of Dor on the slopes of Dor, one; the king of Goiʹim in Gilʹgal, one;

joshua/12/24.text: the king of Tirʹzah, one; a total of 31 kings.

1-samuel/15/1.text: 15 Then Samuel said to Saul: “Jehovah sent me to anoint you as king over his people Israel; now listen to what Jehovah has to say.

1-samuel/15/2.text: This is what Jehovah of armies says: ‘I will call to account the A·malʹek·ites for what they did to Israel when they opposed them along their way coming up from Egypt.

1-samuel/15/3.text: Now go, and strike down the A·malʹek·ites, and devote them to destruction along with all that they have. You must not spare them; you are to put them to death, man as well as woman, child as well as infant, bull as well as sheep, camel as well as donkey.’”

1-samuel/15/4.text: Saul summoned the people and counted them in Te·laʹim: There were 200, 000 foot soldiers and 10, 000 men of Judah.

1-samuel/15/5.text: Saul advanced as far as the city of Amʹa·lek and set an ambush by the valley.

1-samuel/15/6.text: Saul then said to the Kenʹites: “Go, depart from among the A·malʹek·ites, so that I do not sweep you away with them. For you showed loyal love to all the people of Israel at the time they came up out of Egypt.” So the Kenʹites departed from the midst of Amʹa·lek.

1-samuel/15/7.text: After that Saul struck down the A·malʹek·ites from Havʹi·lah as far as Shur, which is next to Egypt.

1-samuel/15/8.text: He caught Aʹgag the king of Amʹa·lek alive, but all the other people he devoted to destruction with the sword.

1-samuel/15/9.text: However, Saul and the people spared Aʹgag and the best of the flock, the herd, the fattened animals, the rams, and all that was good. They did not want to devote them to destruction. But all the goods that were worthless and unwanted, these they devoted to destruction.

1-samuel/15/10.text: Then the word of Jehovah came to Samuel:

1-samuel/15/11.text: “I regret that I have made Saul king, for he has turned away from following me and he has not carried out my words.” Samuel became very upset, and he kept crying out to Jehovah all night long.

1-samuel/15/12.text: When Samuel got up early in the morning to meet Saul, Samuel was told: “Saul went to Carʹmel, and there he erected a monument for himself. Then he turned around and went down to Gilʹgal.”

1-samuel/15/13.text: When Samuel finally came to him, Saul said to him: “May Jehovah bless you. I have carried out the word of Jehovah.”

1-samuel/15/14.text: But Samuel said: “Then what is this sound of the flock in my ears and the sound of the cattle that I hear?”

1-samuel/15/15.text: To this Saul said: “They were brought from the A·malʹek·ites, because the people spared the best of the flock and the herd for sacrificing them to Jehovah your God; but what was left we devoted to destruction.”

1-samuel/15/16.text: At this Samuel said to Saul: “Stop! Let me tell you what Jehovah said to me last night.” So he said to him: “Speak!”

1-samuel/15/17.text: Samuel continued: “Were you not insignificant in your own eyes when you were made head of the tribes of Israel and when Jehovah anointed you as king over Israel?

1-samuel/15/18.text: Jehovah later sent you on a mission and said, ‘Go, and devote the sinful A·malʹek·ites to destruction. Fight against them until you have exterminated them.’

1-samuel/15/19.text: So why did you not obey the voice of Jehovah? Instead, you rushed greedily toward the spoil and did what was bad in the eyes of Jehovah!”

1-samuel/15/20.text: However, Saul said to Samuel: “But I have obeyed the voice of Jehovah! I went on the mission to which Jehovah sent me, and I brought back Aʹgag the king of Amʹa·lek, and I devoted the A·malʹek·ites to destruction.

1-samuel/15/21.text: But the people took sheep and cattle from the spoil, the best of what was devoted to destruction, to sacrifice to Jehovah your God at Gilʹgal.”

1-samuel/15/22.text: Samuel then said: “Does Jehovah take as much pleasure in burnt offerings and sacrifices as in obeying the voice of Jehovah? Look! To obey is better than a sacrifice, and to pay attention than the fat of rams;

1-samuel/15/23.text: for rebelliousness is the same as the sin of divination, and pushing ahead presumptuously the same as using magical power and idolatry. Because you have rejected the word of Jehovah, he has rejected you from being king.”

1-samuel/15/24.text: Then Saul said to Samuel: “I have sinned, for I have overstepped the order of Jehovah and your words, because I feared the people and listened to what they said.

1-samuel/15/25.text: And now, please, pardon my sin, and return with me so that I may bow down to Jehovah.”

1-samuel/15/26.text: But Samuel said to Saul: “I will not return with you, for you have rejected the word of Jehovah, and Jehovah has rejected you from continuing as king over Israel.”

1-samuel/15/27.text: As Samuel was turning to go, Saul grabbed hold of the hem of his sleeveless coat, but it ripped away.

1-samuel/15/28.text: At this Samuel said to him: “Jehovah has ripped away the royal rule of Israel from you today, and he will give it to one of your fellow men who is better than you.

1-samuel/15/29.text: Moreover, the Excellency of Israel will not prove false or change his mind, for He is not a mere man that he should change his mind.”

1-samuel/15/30.text: At this he said: “I have sinned. But honor me, please, in front of the elders of my people and in front of Israel. Return with me, and I will bow down to Jehovah your God.”

1-samuel/15/31.text: So Samuel returned behind Saul, and Saul bowed down to Jehovah.

1-samuel/15/32.text: And Samuel said: “Bring Aʹgag the king of Amʹa·lek near to me.” Then Aʹgag went to him reluctantly, for Aʹgag had been saying to himself: ‘Surely the threat of death is past.’

1-samuel/15/33.text: However, Samuel said: “Just as your sword has bereaved women of children, so your mother will be most bereaved among women.” With that Samuel hacked Aʹgag to pieces before Jehovah at Gilʹgal.

1-samuel/15/34.text: Samuel now went to Raʹmah, and Saul went up to his own house at Gibʹe·ah of Saul.

1-samuel/15/35.text: Samuel did not see Saul again until the day of his death, for Samuel went into mourning for Saul. And Jehovah regretted that he had made Saul king over Israel.

ezra/1/1.text: 1 In the first year of King Cyrus of Persia, in order that Jehovah’s word spoken by Jeremiah would be fulfilled, Jehovah stirred the spirit of King Cyrus of Persia to make a proclamation throughout his kingdom, which he also put in writing, saying:

ezra/1/2.text: “This is what King Cyrus of Persia says, ‘Jehovah the God of the heavens has given me all the kingdoms of the earth, and he has commissioned me to build him a house in Jerusalem, which is in Judah.

ezra/1/3.text: Whoever there is among you of all his people, may his God be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem, which is in Judah, and rebuild the house of Jehovah the God of Israel—he is the true God—whose house was in Jerusalem.

ezra/1/4.text: Anyone who is residing as a foreigner, wherever he may be, let him be helped by his neighbors by their giving him silver and gold, goods and livestock, along with the voluntary offering for the house of the true God, which was in Jerusalem.’”

ezra/1/5.text: Then the heads of the paternal houses of Judah and of Benjamin and the priests and the Levites—everyone whose spirit the true God had stirred—prepared to go up and rebuild the house of Jehovah, which was in Jerusalem.

ezra/1/6.text: All those around them supported them by giving them utensils of silver and of gold, goods, livestock, and valuable things, besides all the voluntary offerings.

ezra/1/7.text: King Cyrus also brought out the utensils of the house of Jehovah that Neb·u·chad·nezʹzar had taken from Jerusalem and had put in the house of his god.

ezra/1/8.text: King Cyrus of Persia brought them out under the supervision of Mithʹre·dath the treasurer, who made an inventory of them for Shesh·bazʹzar the chieftain of Judah.

ezra/1/9.text: Now this was the inventory: 30 basket-shaped vessels of gold, 1, 000 basket-shaped vessels of silver, 29 replacement vessels,

ezra/1/10.text: 30 small gold bowls, 410 small silver bowls, 1, 000 other utensils.

ezra/1/11.text: All the utensils of gold and of silver were 5, 400. Shesh·bazʹzar brought all of these up when the exiles were brought out of Babylon to Jerusalem.

joshua/15/1.text: 15 The land allotted to the tribe of Judah for their families extended to the boundary of Eʹdom, the wilderness of Zin, to the Negʹeb at its southern end.

joshua/15/2.text: Their southern boundary ran from the extremity of the Salt Sea, from the bay that faces southward.

joshua/15/3.text: And it extended south to the ascent of A·krabʹbim, passed over to Zin, then went up from the south to Kaʹdesh-barʹne·a, over to Hezʹron, up to Adʹdar, and went around toward Karʹka.

joshua/15/4.text: Then it passed on to Azʹmon and extended to the Wadi of Egypt, and the boundary ended at the Sea. This was their southern boundary.

joshua/15/5.text: The eastern boundary was the Salt Sea up to the end of the Jordan, and the boundary at the northern corner was at the bay of the sea, at the end of the Jordan.

joshua/15/6.text: The boundary went up to Beth-hogʹlah and passed over at the north of Beth-arʹa·bah, and the boundary went up to the stone of Boʹhan the son of Reuʹben.

joshua/15/7.text: The boundary went up to Deʹbir at the Valley of Aʹchor and turned northward to Gilʹgal, which is in front of the ascent of A·dumʹmim that is south of the wadi, and the boundary passed over to the waters of En-sheʹmesh and ended at En-roʹgel.

joshua/15/8.text: The boundary went up to the Valley of the Son of Hinʹnom to the slope of the Jebʹu·site at the south, that is, Jerusalem, and the boundary went up to the top of the mountain that faces the Valley of Hinʹnom to the west, which is at the extremity of the Valley of Rephʹa·im to the north.

joshua/15/9.text: And the boundary was marked from the top of the mountain to the spring of the waters of Neph·toʹah and extended to the cities of Mount Eʹphron; and the boundary was marked to Baʹal·ah, that is, Kirʹi·ath-jeʹa·rim.

joshua/15/10.text: The boundary went around from Baʹal·ah westward to Mount Seʹir and passed over to the slope of Mount Jeʹa·rim at the north, that is, Chesʹa·lon, and it went down to Beth-sheʹmesh and passed over to Timʹnah.

joshua/15/11.text: And the boundary extended to the slope of Ekʹron to the north, and the boundary was marked to Shikʹke·ron and passed over to Mount Baʹal·ah and extended to Jabʹne·el, and the boundary ended at the sea.

joshua/15/12.text: The western boundary was at the Great Sea and its coast. This was the boundary of the descendants of Judah by their families on all sides.

joshua/15/13.text: And to Caʹleb the son of Je·phunʹneh, he gave a share among the descendants of Judah at the order of Jehovah to Joshua, namely, Kirʹi·ath-arʹba (Arʹba was the father of Aʹnak), that is, Hebʹron.

joshua/15/14.text: So Caʹleb drove out from there the three sons of Aʹnak: Sheʹshai, A·hiʹman, and Talʹmai, descendants of Aʹnak.

joshua/15/15.text: Then he went up from there against the inhabitants of Deʹbir. (The name of Deʹbir was previously Kirʹi·ath-seʹpher.)

joshua/15/16.text: Caʹleb then said: “To the man who strikes Kirʹi·ath-seʹpher and captures it, I will give my daughter Achʹsah as a wife.”

joshua/15/17.text: And Othʹni·el the son of Keʹnaz, Caʹleb’s brother, captured it. So he gave him his daughter Achʹsah as a wife.

joshua/15/18.text: While she was going home, she urged him to ask her father for a field. Then she dismounted from her donkey. Caʹleb asked her: “What do you want?”

joshua/15/19.text: She said: “Please grant me a blessing, for you have given me a piece of land in the south; give me also Gulʹloth-maʹim.” So he gave her Upper Gulʹloth and Lower Gulʹloth.

joshua/15/20.text: This was the inheritance of the tribe of Judah by their families.

joshua/15/21.text: The cities at the extremity of the tribe of Judah toward the boundary of Eʹdom in the south were: Kabʹze·el, Eʹder, Jaʹgur,

joshua/15/25.text: Haʹzor-ha·datʹtah, and Keʹri·oth-hezʹron, that is, Haʹzor,

joshua/15/32.text: Le·baʹoth, Shilʹhim, Aʹin, and Rimʹmon—a total of 29 cities together with their settlements.

joshua/15/33.text: In the She·pheʹlah, there were: Eshʹta·ol, Zorʹah, Ashʹnah,

joshua/15/36.text: Shaʹa·raʹim, Ad·i·thaʹim, and Ge·deʹrah and Ged·e·ro·thaʹim—14 cities and their settlements.

joshua/15/41.text: Ge·deʹroth, Beth-daʹgon, Naʹa·mah, and Mak·keʹdah—16 cities and their settlements.

joshua/15/44.text: Keiʹlah, Achʹzib, and Ma·reʹshah—nine cities and their settlements.

joshua/15/45.text: Ekʹron and its dependent towns and its settlements;

joshua/15/46.text: from Ekʹron westward, all that is alongside Ashʹdod and their settlements.

joshua/15/47.text: Ashʹdod, its dependent towns and its settlements; Gazʹa, its dependent towns and its settlements, down to the Wadi of Egypt, the Great Sea, and the adjacent region.

joshua/15/48.text: And in the mountainous region, Shaʹmir, Jatʹtir, Soʹcoh,

joshua/15/51.text: Goʹshen, Hoʹlon, and Giʹloh—11 cities and their settlements.

joshua/15/54.text: Humʹtah, Kirʹi·ath-arʹba, that is, Hebʹron, and Ziʹor—nine cities and their settlements.

joshua/15/57.text: Kaʹin, Gibʹe·ah, and Timʹnah—ten cities and their settlements.

joshua/15/59.text: Maʹa·rath, Beth-aʹnoth, and Elʹte·kon—six cities and their settlements.

joshua/15/60.text: Kirʹi·ath-baʹal, that is, Kirʹi·ath-jeʹa·rim, and Rabʹbah—two cities and their settlements.

joshua/15/61.text: In the wilderness, Beth-arʹa·bah, Midʹdin, Se·caʹcah,

joshua/15/62.text: Nibʹshan, the City of Salt, and En-gedʹi—six cities and their settlements.

joshua/15/63.text: As for the Jebʹu·sites who were dwelling in Jerusalem, the men of Judah were not able to drive them away, so the Jebʹu·sites continue dwelling with the people of Judah in Jerusalem to this day.

ruth/1/1.text: 1 Now in the days when the judges administered justice, a famine occurred in the land; and a man went from Bethʹle·hem in Judah to reside as a foreigner in the fields of Moʹab, he along with his wife and his two sons.

ruth/1/2.text: The man’s name was E·limʹe·lech, his wife’s name was Na·oʹmi, and the names of his two sons were Mahʹlon and Chilʹi·on. They were Ephʹrath·ites from Bethʹle·hem in Judah. And they came to the fields of Moʹab and remained there.

ruth/1/3.text: After some time E·limʹe·lech, Na·oʹmi’s husband, died, and she was left with her two sons.

ruth/1/4.text: The men later married Moʹab·ite women; one was named Orʹpah, and the other was named Ruth. They remained there for about ten years.

ruth/1/5.text: Then the two sons, Mahʹlon and Chilʹi·on, also died, and the woman was left without her two children and her husband.

ruth/1/6.text: So she started out with her daughters-in-law to return from the fields of Moʹab, for she had heard in Moʹab that Jehovah had turned his attention to his people by giving them food.

ruth/1/7.text: She left the place where she had been living with both of her daughters-in-law. As they were walking on the road to return to the land of Judah,

ruth/1/8.text: Na·oʹmi said to both of her daughters-in-law: “Go, return, each of you to your mother’s home. May Jehovah show loyal love to you, just as you have shown it to the men who have died and to me.

ruth/1/9.text: May Jehovah grant that each of you finds security in the home of your husband.” Then she kissed them, and they wept loudly.

ruth/1/10.text: They kept saying to her: “No, but we will go with you to your people.”

ruth/1/11.text: But Na·oʹmi said: “Return, my daughters. Why should you go with me? Can I still give birth to sons who could become your husbands?

ruth/1/12.text: Return, my daughters. Go, for I have grown too old to marry. Even if I could hope to find a husband tonight and could also bear sons,

ruth/1/13.text: would you keep waiting for them until they could grow up? Would you refrain from getting remarried for their sakes? No, my daughters, I feel very bitter for you, because the hand of Jehovah has turned against me.”

ruth/1/14.text: Again they wept loudly, after which Orʹpah kissed her mother-in-law and departed. But Ruth stuck with her.

ruth/1/15.text: So Na·oʹmi said: “Look! Your widowed sister-in-law has returned to her people and her gods. Return with your sister-in-law.”

ruth/1/16.text: But Ruth said: “Do not plead with me to abandon you, to turn back from accompanying you; for where you go I will go, and where you spend the night, I will spend the night. Your people will be my people, and your God my God.

ruth/1/17.text: Where you die I will die, and there I will be buried. May Jehovah do so to me and add to it if anything but death should separate me from you.”

ruth/1/18.text: When Na·oʹmi saw that Ruth insisted on going with her, she stopped trying to convince her.

ruth/1/19.text: And they both continued on their way until they came to Bethʹle·hem. As soon as they arrived in Bethʹle·hem, the whole city became stirred up over them, and women were saying: “Is this Na·oʹmi?”

ruth/1/20.text: She would say to the women: “Do not call me Na·oʹmi. Call me Maʹra, for the Almighty has made life very bitter for me.

ruth/1/21.text: I was full when I went, but Jehovah made me return empty-handed. Why should you call me Na·oʹmi, when it is Jehovah who opposed me and the Almighty who caused me calamity?”

ruth/1/22.text: This is how Na·oʹmi returned from the fields of Moʹab, along with her Moʹab·ite daughter-in-law Ruth. They came to Bethʹle·hem at the beginning of the barley harvest.

judges/6/1.text: 6 But the Israelites again did what was bad in the eyes of Jehovah, so Jehovah gave them into the hand of Midʹi·an for seven years.

judges/6/2.text: The hand of Midʹi·an dominated over Israel. Because of Midʹi·an, the Israelites made hiding places for themselves in the mountains, in the caves, and in the places difficult to approach.

judges/6/3.text: If Israel sowed seed, Midʹi·an and Amʹa·lek and the Easterners would attack them.

judges/6/4.text: They would camp against them and ruin the produce of the land all the way to Gazʹa, and they left nothing for Israel to eat and no sheep or bull or donkey.

judges/6/5.text: For they would come up with their livestock and tents as numerous as the locusts, and they and their camels could not be numbered, and they would come into the land to destroy it.

judges/6/6.text: So Israel became greatly impoverished on account of Midʹi·an; and the Israelites called to Jehovah for help.

judges/6/7.text: When the Israelites called to Jehovah for help because of Midʹi·an,

judges/6/8.text: Jehovah sent to the Israelites a prophet who said to them: “This is what Jehovah the God of Israel says, ‘I brought you up from Egypt and thus brought you out of the house of slavery.

judges/6/9.text: So I rescued you from the hand of Egypt and from all your oppressors and drove them out from before you and gave you their land.

judges/6/10.text: And I said to you: “I am Jehovah your God. You must not fear the gods of the Amʹor·ites in whose land you are dwelling.” But you did not obey me.’”

judges/6/11.text: Later Jehovah’s angel came and sat under the big tree that was in Ophʹrah, which belonged to Joʹash the Abi-ezʹrite. His son Gidʹe·on was beating out wheat in the winepress in order to hide it from Midʹi·an.

judges/6/12.text: Jehovah’s angel appeared to him and said: “Jehovah is with you, you mighty warrior.”
