judges/6/13.text: At this Gidʹe·on said to him: “Pardon me, my lord, but if Jehovah is with us, why has all of this come upon us? Where are all his wonderful acts that our fathers related to us, saying, ‘Did Jehovah not bring us up out of Egypt?’ Now Jehovah has deserted us and given us into Midʹi·an’s hand.”

judges/6/14.text: Jehovah faced him and said: “Go with the strength you have, and you will save Israel out of Midʹi·an’s hand. Is it not I who send you?”

judges/6/15.text: Gidʹe·on answered him: “Pardon me, Jehovah. How can I save Israel? Look! My clan is the least in Ma·nasʹseh, and I am the most insignificant in my father’s house.”

judges/6/16.text: But Jehovah said to him: “Because I will be with you, you will strike down Midʹi·an as if they were one man.”

judges/6/17.text: Then he said to him: “If, now, I have found favor in your eyes, show me a sign that you are the one speaking with me.

judges/6/18.text: Please do not depart from here until I return with my gift and set it before you.” So he said: “I will stay here until you return.”

judges/6/19.text: And Gidʹe·on went in and prepared a young goat and made unleavened bread from an eʹphah of flour. He put the meat in the basket and the broth in the cooking pot; then he brought them out to him and served them under the big tree.

judges/6/20.text: The angel of the true God now said to him: “Take the meat and the unleavened bread and place them on the big rock there, and pour out the broth.” And he did so.

judges/6/21.text: Then Jehovah’s angel stretched out the tip of the staff that was in his hand and touched the meat and the unleavened bread, and fire flared up from the rock and consumed the meat and the unleavened bread. Jehovah’s angel then vanished from his sight.

judges/6/22.text: Gidʹe·on now realized that it was Jehovah’s angel. At once Gidʹe·on said: “Alas, Sovereign Lord Jehovah, for I have seen Jehovah’s angel face-to-face!”

judges/6/23.text: But Jehovah said to him: “Peace be with you. Have no fear; you will not die.”

judges/6/24.text: So Gidʹe·on built an altar there to Jehovah, and it is called Je·hoʹvah-shaʹlom down to this day. It is still in Ophʹrah of the Abi-ezʹrites.

judges/6/25.text: That night Jehovah said to him: “Take the young bull that belongs to your father, the second young bull that is seven years old, and tear down the altar of Baʹal that belongs to your father, and cut down the sacred pole next to it.

judges/6/26.text: After you build an altar to Jehovah your God on top of this stronghold with the row of stones, take the second young bull and offer it as a burnt offering on the pieces of wood from the sacred pole that you cut down.”

judges/6/27.text: So Gidʹe·on took ten men of his servants and did just as Jehovah told him. But he feared the household of his father and the men of the city too much to do it by day, so he did it at night.

judges/6/28.text: When the men of the city got up early the next morning, they saw that the altar of Baʹal had been pulled down and the sacred pole beside it had been cut down and the second young bull had been offered up on the altar that had been built.

judges/6/29.text: They asked one another: “Who did this?” After they investigated, they said: “Gidʹe·on the son of Joʹash did this.”

judges/6/30.text: So the men of the city said to Joʹash: “Bring your son out that he may die, because he pulled down the altar of Baʹal and cut down the sacred pole next to it.”

judges/6/31.text: Joʹash then said to all those who confronted him: “Do you have to defend Baʹal? Do you have to save him? Whoever defends him should be put to death this morning. If he is a god, let him defend himself, since someone pulled down his altar.”

judges/6/32.text: And he called Gidʹe·on Jer·ub·baʹal on that day, saying: “Let Baʹal defend himself, for someone has pulled down his altar.”

judges/6/33.text: All Midʹi·an and Amʹa·lek and the Easterners joined forces; and they crossed over into the Valley of Jezʹre·el and camped.

judges/6/34.text: Then Jehovah’s spirit came upon Gidʹe·on and he sounded the horn, and the Abi-ezʹrites rallied behind him.

judges/6/35.text: He sent out messengers through all of Ma·nasʹseh, and they too rallied behind him. He also sent out messengers through Ashʹer, Zebʹu·lun, and Naphʹta·li, and they came up to meet him.

judges/6/36.text: Then Gidʹe·on said to the true God: “If you are saving Israel by means of me, just as you have promised,

judges/6/37.text: here I am laying a fleece of wool on the threshing floor. If there is dew on the fleece only but all the ground around it is dry, then I will know that you will save Israel by means of me, just as you have promised.”

judges/6/38.text: And that is how it happened. When he rose up early the next day and wrung the fleece, he squeezed off enough dew from the fleece to fill a large banquet bowl with water.

judges/6/39.text: However, Gidʹe·on said to the true God: “Do not let your anger burn against me, but let me ask just once more. Let me, please, make just one more test with the fleece. Please let the fleece alone be dry while there is dew all over the ground.”

judges/6/40.text: So that is what God did that night; only the fleece was dry, and there was dew all over the ground.

2-kings/19/1.text: 19 As soon as King Hez·e·kiʹah heard this, he ripped his garments apart and covered himself with sackcloth and went into the house of Jehovah.

2-kings/19/2.text: Then he sent E·liʹa·kim, who was in charge of the household, Shebʹnah the secretary, and the elders of the priests, covered with sackcloth, to the prophet Isaiah, the son of Aʹmoz.

2-kings/19/3.text: They said to him: “This is what Hez·e·kiʹah says, ‘This day is a day of distress, of rebuke, and of disgrace; for the children are ready to be born, but there is no strength to give birth.

2-kings/19/4.text: Perhaps Jehovah your God will hear all the words of the Rabʹsha·keh, whom the king of As·syrʹi·a his lord sent to taunt the living God, and he will call him to account for the words that Jehovah your God has heard. So offer up a prayer in behalf of the remnant who have survived.’”

2-kings/19/5.text: So the servants of King Hez·e·kiʹah went in to Isaiah,

2-kings/19/6.text: and Isaiah said to them: “This is what you should say to your lord, ‘This is what Jehovah says: “Do not be afraid because of the words that you heard, the words with which the attendants of the king of As·syrʹi·a blasphemed me.

2-kings/19/7.text: Here I am putting a thought in his mind, and he will hear a report and return to his own land; and I will make him fall by the sword in his own land.”’”

2-kings/19/8.text: After the Rabʹsha·keh heard that the king of As·syrʹi·a had pulled away from Laʹchish, he returned to him and found him fighting against Libʹnah.

2-kings/19/9.text: Now the king heard it said about King Tir·haʹkah of E·thi·oʹpi·a: “Here he has come out to fight against you.” So he sent messengers again to Hez·e·kiʹah, saying:

2-kings/19/10.text: “This is what you should say to King Hez·e·kiʹah of Judah, ‘Do not let your God in whom you trust deceive you by saying: “Jerusalem will not be given into the hand of the king of As·syrʹi·a.”

2-kings/19/11.text: Look! You have heard what the kings of As·syrʹi·a did to all the lands by devoting them to destruction. Will you alone be rescued?

2-kings/19/12.text: Did the gods of the nations that my forefathers destroyed rescue them? Where are Goʹzan, Haʹran, Reʹzeph, and the people of Eʹden who were in Tel-asʹsar?

2-kings/19/13.text: Where is the king of Haʹmath, the king of Arʹpad, and the king of the cities of Seph·ar·vaʹim, and of Heʹna, and of Ivʹvah?’”

2-kings/19/14.text: Hez·e·kiʹah took the letters out of the hand of the messengers and read them. Hez·e·kiʹah then went up to the house of Jehovah and spread them out before Jehovah.

2-kings/19/15.text: And Hez·e·kiʹah began to pray before Jehovah and say: “O Jehovah the God of Israel, sitting enthroned above the cherubs, you alone are the true God of all the kingdoms of the earth. You made the heavens and the earth.

2-kings/19/16.text: Incline your ear, O Jehovah, and hear! Open your eyes, O Jehovah, and see! Hear the words that Sen·nachʹer·ib has sent to taunt the living God.

2-kings/19/17.text: It is a fact, O Jehovah, that the kings of As·syrʹi·a have devastated the nations and their lands.

2-kings/19/18.text: And they have thrown their gods into the fire, because they were not gods but the work of human hands, wood and stone. That is why they could destroy them.

2-kings/19/19.text: But now, O Jehovah our God, please save us out of his hand, so that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that you alone are God, O Jehovah.”

2-kings/19/20.text: Isaiah son of Aʹmoz then sent this message to Hez·e·kiʹah: “This is what Jehovah the God of Israel says, ‘I have heard your prayer to me concerning King Sen·nachʹer·ib of As·syrʹi·a.

2-kings/19/21.text: This is the word that Jehovah has spoken against him: “The virgin daughter of Zion despises you, she scoffs at you. The daughter of Jerusalem shakes her head at you.

2-kings/19/22.text: Whom have you taunted and blasphemed? Against whom have you raised your voiceAnd lifted your arrogant eyes? It is against the Holy One of Israel!

2-kings/19/23.text: Through your messengers you have taunted Jehovah and said, ‘With the multitude of my war chariotsI will ascend the heights of mountains, The remotest parts of Lebʹa·non. I will cut down its lofty cedars, its choice juniper trees. I will enter its farthest retreats, its densest forests.

2-kings/19/24.text: I will dig wells and drink foreign waters;I will dry up all the streams of Egypt with the soles of my feet.’

2-kings/19/25.text: Have you not heard? From long ago it was determined. From days gone by I have prepared it. Now I will bring it about. You will turn fortified cities into desolate piles of ruins.

2-kings/19/26.text: Their inhabitants will be helpless;They will be terrified and put to shame. They will become as vegetation of the field and green grass, As grass of the roofs that is scorched by the east wind.

2-kings/19/27.text: But I well know when you sit, when you go out, when you come in, And when you are enraged against me,

2-kings/19/28.text: Because your rage against me and your roaring have reached my ears. So I will put my hook in your nose and my bridle between your lips, And I will lead you back the way you came.”

2-kings/19/29.text: “‘And this will be the sign for you: This year you will eat what grows on its own; and in the second year you will eat grain that sprouts from that; but in the third year you will sow seed and reap, and you will plant vineyards and eat their fruitage.

2-kings/19/30.text: Those of the house of Judah who escape, those who are left, will take root downward and produce fruit upward.

2-kings/19/31.text: For a remnant will go out of Jerusalem and survivors from Mount Zion. The zeal of Jehovah of armies will do this.

2-kings/19/32.text: “‘Therefore this is what Jehovah says about the king of As·syrʹi·a: “He will not come into this cityOr shoot an arrow thereOr confront it with a shieldOr cast up a siege rampart against it.

2-kings/19/33.text: By the way he came he will return;He will not come into this city, ” declares Jehovah.

2-kings/19/34.text: “I will defend this city and save it for my own sakeAnd for the sake of my servant David.”’”

2-kings/19/35.text: On that very night the angel of Jehovah went out and struck down 185, 000 men in the camp of the As·syrʹi·ans. When people rose up early in the morning, they saw all the dead bodies.

2-kings/19/36.text: So King Sen·nachʹer·ib of As·syrʹi·a departed and returned to Ninʹe·veh and stayed there.

2-kings/19/37.text: And as he was bowing down at the house of his god Nisʹroch, his own sons A·dramʹme·lech and Shar·eʹzer struck him down with the sword and then escaped to the land of Arʹa·rat. And his son Eʹsar-hadʹdon became king in his place.

ezra/4/1.text: 4 When the enemies of Judah and Benjamin heard that the returned exiles were building a temple to Jehovah the God of Israel,

ezra/4/2.text: they immediately approached Ze·rubʹba·bel and the heads of the paternal houses and said to them: “Let us build along with you; for like you, we worship your God and we have been sacrificing to him since the days of King Eʹsar-hadʹdon of As·syrʹi·a, who brought us here.”

ezra/4/3.text: However, Ze·rubʹba·bel and Jeshʹu·a and the rest of the heads of the paternal houses of Israel said to them: “You have no share with us in building a house to our God, for we alone will build it to Jehovah the God of Israel, just as King Cyrus the king of Persia has commanded us.”

ezra/4/4.text: Then the people of the land were continually discouraging the people of Judah and disheartening them from building.

ezra/4/5.text: They hired advisers against them to frustrate their plans all the days of King Cyrus of Persia until the reign of King Da·riʹus of Persia.

ezra/4/6.text: At the beginning of the reign of A·has·u·eʹrus, they wrote an accusation against the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem.

ezra/4/7.text: And in the days of King Ar·ta·xerxʹes of Persia, Bishʹlam, Mithʹre·dath, Tabʹe·el, and the rest of his colleagues wrote to Ar·ta·xerxʹes the king; they translated the letter into Ar·a·maʹic, writing it with Ar·a·maʹic characters.

ezra/4/8.text: Reʹhum the chief government official and Shimʹshai the scribe wrote a letter against Jerusalem to King Ar·ta·xerxʹes, as follows:

ezra/4/9.text: (It was from Reʹhum the chief government official and Shimʹshai the scribe and the rest of their colleagues, the judges and the lesser governors, the secretaries, the people of Eʹrech, the Babylonians, the inhabitants of Suʹsa, that is, the Eʹlam·ites,

ezra/4/10.text: and the rest of the nations that the great and honorable Asʹe·nap·par took into exile and settled in the cities of Sa·marʹi·a, and the rest in the region Beyond the River, and now

ezra/4/11.text: this is a copy of the letter that they sent him.) “To King Ar·ta·xerxʹes from your servants, the men of the region Beyond the River: And now

ezra/4/12.text: let it be known to the king that the Jews who came up here from you to us have arrived at Jerusalem. They are rebuilding the rebellious and wicked city, and they are finishing the walls and repairing the foundations.

ezra/4/13.text: Now let it be known to the king that if this city should be rebuilt and its walls finished, they will not give tax, tribute, or toll, and it will result in a loss to the treasuries of the kings.

ezra/4/14.text: Since we eat the salt of the palace and it is not proper for us to see the king’s interests harmed, we have therefore sent to make this known to the king,

ezra/4/15.text: so that there may be an investigation of the book of records of your ancestors. You will find in the book of records and learn that this city is a rebellious city, injurious to kings and provinces, and within it have been those stirring up sedition from ancient times. That is why this city was destroyed.

ezra/4/16.text: We are making known to the king that if this city is rebuilt and its walls are finished, you will have no control of the region Beyond the River.”

ezra/4/17.text: The king sent word to Reʹhum the chief government official and Shimʹshai the scribe and the rest of their colleagues who were dwelling in Sa·marʹi·a and the rest of the region Beyond the River: “Greetings! And now

ezra/4/18.text: the official document that you sent us has been clearly read before me.

ezra/4/19.text: By my order an investigation was made, and it was found that from long ago the city has had uprisings against kings, and rebellions and revolts have taken place there.

ezra/4/20.text: There were powerful kings over Jerusalem who ruled the whole region Beyond the River, and tax, tribute, and toll were paid to them.

ezra/4/21.text: Now issue an order for these men to stop work, so that the city may not be rebuilt until I issue an order.

ezra/4/22.text: Be careful not to neglect acting in this regard, so that the king’s interests are not harmed any further.”

ezra/4/23.text: Now after the copy of the official document of King Ar·ta·xerxʹes had been read before Reʹhum and Shimʹshai the scribe and their colleagues, they quickly went to Jerusalem to the Jews and used force to stop them.

ezra/4/24.text: It was then that the work on the house of God, which was in Jerusalem, came to a halt; and it remained at a standstill until the second year of the reign of King Da·riʹus of Persia.

job/1/1.text: 1 There was a man in the land of Uz whose name was Job. He was an upright man of integrity; he feared God and shunned what was bad.

job/1/2.text: Seven sons and three daughters were born to him.

job/1/3.text: His livestock amounted to 7, 000 sheep, 3, 000 camels, 1, 000 cattle, and 500 donkeys, along with a very large number of servants, so that he became the greatest of all the people of the East.

job/1/4.text: Each of his sons would hold a banquet at his house on his own set day. They would invite their three sisters to eat and drink with them.

job/1/5.text: After a series of banquet days was complete, Job would send for them in order to sanctify them. Then he would get up early in the morning and offer up burnt sacrifices for each of them. For Job said: “Maybe my sons have sinned and have cursed God in their heart.” That is what Job would always do.

job/1/6.text: Now the day came when the sons of the true God entered to take their station before Jehovah, and Satan also entered among them.

job/1/7.text: Then Jehovah said to Satan: “Where have you come from?” Satan answered Jehovah: “From roving about on the earth and from walking about in it.”

job/1/8.text: And Jehovah said to Satan: “Have you taken note of my servant Job? There is no one like him on the earth. He is an upright man of integrity, fearing God and shunning what is bad.”

job/1/9.text: At that Satan answered Jehovah: “Is it for nothing that Job has feared God?

job/1/10.text: Have you not put up a protective hedge around him and his house and everything he has? You have blessed the work of his hands, and his livestock has spread out in the land.

job/1/11.text: But, for a change, stretch out your hand and strike everything he has, and he will surely curse you to your very face.”

job/1/12.text: Then Jehovah said to Satan: “Look! Everything that he has is in your hand. Only do not lay your hand on the man himself!” So Satan went out from the presence of Jehovah.

job/1/13.text: Now on the day when his sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine in their oldest brother’s house,

job/1/14.text: a messenger came to Job and said: “The cattle were plowing and the donkeys were grazing beside them

job/1/15.text: when the Sa·beʹans attacked and took them, and they killed the servants with the sword. I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”

job/1/16.text: While he was still speaking, another one came and said: “Fire from God fell from the heavens and blazed among the sheep and the servants and consumed them! I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”

job/1/17.text: While he was still speaking, another one came and said: “The Chal·deʹans formed three bands and made a raid on the camels and took them, and they killed the servants with the sword. I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”

job/1/18.text: While he was still speaking, yet another one came and said: “Your sons and your daughters were eating and drinking wine in their oldest brother’s house.

job/1/19.text: Suddenly a great wind came from the wilderness, and it struck the four corners of the house, so that it fell on the young people and they were killed. I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”

job/1/20.text: At that Job got up and ripped apart his garment and cut the hair off his head; then he fell to the ground and bowed down

job/1/21.text: and said: “Naked I came out of my mother’s womb, And naked I will return. Jehovah has given, and Jehovah has taken away. Let the name of Jehovah continue to be praised.”

job/1/22.text: In all of this, Job did not sin or accuse God of doing anything wrong.

ezra/7/1.text: 7 After these things, during the reign of King Ar·ta·xerxʹes of Persia, Ezʹra returned. He was the son of Se·raiʹah, son of Az·a·riʹah, son of Hil·kiʹah,

ezra/7/2.text: son of Shalʹlum, son of Zaʹdok, son of A·hiʹtub,

ezra/7/3.text: son of Am·a·riʹah, son of Az·a·riʹah, son of Me·raʹioth,

ezra/7/4.text: son of Zer·a·hiʹah, son of Uzʹzi, son of Bukʹki,

ezra/7/5.text: son of Ab·i·shuʹa, son of Phinʹe·has, son of El·e·aʹzar, son of Aaron the chief priest.

ezra/7/6.text: This Ezʹra came up from Babylon. He was a copyist who was well-versed in the Law of Moses, which Jehovah the God of Israel had given. The king granted everything he requested, for the hand of Jehovah his God was upon him.

ezra/7/7.text: Some of the Israelites, the priests, the Levites, the singers, the gatekeepers, and the temple servants, went up to Jerusalem in the seventh year of King Ar·ta·xerxʹes.

ezra/7/8.text: And Ezʹra came to Jerusalem in the fifth month, in the seventh year of the king.

ezra/7/9.text: On the first day of the first month, he began the journey from Babylon, and he arrived in Jerusalem on the first day of the fifth month, for the good hand of his God was upon him.

ezra/7/10.text: Ezʹra had prepared his heart to consult the Law of Jehovah and to practice it, and to teach its regulations and judgments in Israel.

ezra/7/11.text: This is a copy of the letter that King Ar·ta·xerxʹes gave to Ezʹra the priest and copyist, an expert in the study of the commandments of Jehovah and of his regulations to Israel:

ezra/7/12.text: “Ar·ta·xerxʹes, the king of kings, to Ezʹra the priest, the copyist of the Law of the God of the heavens: May you have perfect peace. And now

ezra/7/13.text: I have issued an order that everyone in my realm of the people of Israel and their priests and Levites who is willing to go with you to Jerusalem should go.

ezra/7/14.text: For you are sent by the king and his seven advisers to investigate whether the Law of your God, which is with you, is being applied in Judah and Jerusalem,

ezra/7/15.text: and to take the silver and the gold that the king and his advisers have voluntarily given to the God of Israel, whose residence is in Jerusalem,

ezra/7/16.text: with all the silver and the gold that you receive in all the province of Babylon, along with the gift that the people and the priests voluntarily give to the house of their God, which is in Jerusalem.

ezra/7/17.text: And you are to buy promptly with this money bulls, rams, lambs, along with their grain offerings and their drink offerings, and you are to present them on the altar of the house of your God in Jerusalem.

ezra/7/18.text: “And whatever seems good to you and to your brothers to do, you may do with the rest of the silver and the gold, according to the will of your God.

ezra/7/19.text: And all the vessels that are given to you for the service of the house of your God, you are to deliver before God at Jerusalem.

ezra/7/20.text: And the rest of the necessities of the house of your God that you are required to give, you will give out of the royal treasury.

ezra/7/21.text: “I, King Ar·ta·xerxʹes, have issued an order to all the treasurers in the region Beyond the River, that everything that Ezʹra the priest, the copyist of the Law of the God of the heavens, requests of you is to be done promptly,

ezra/7/22.text: up to 100 talents of silver, 100 cor measures of wheat, 100 bath measures of wine, 100 bath measures of oil, and salt without limit.

ezra/7/23.text: Let everything that is ordered by the God of the heavens be done with zeal for the house of the God of the heavens, so that there may be no wrath against the king’s realm and his sons.

ezra/7/24.text: And you are further advised that it is not permitted to impose any tax, tribute, or toll on any of the priests and Levites, musicians, doorkeepers, temple servants, and workers of this house of God.

ezra/7/25.text: “And you, Ezʹra, according to the wisdom that you possess from your God, appoint magistrates and judges to judge all the people in the region Beyond the River, all those who know the laws of your God; and you should instruct anyone who does not know them.

ezra/7/26.text: And everyone who does not observe the Law of your God and the law of the king should have judgment executed on him promptly, whether it is death, banishment, a fine, or imprisonment.”

ezra/7/27.text: May Jehovah the God of our forefathers be praised, who put it into the heart of the king to beautify the house of Jehovah in Jerusalem!

ezra/7/28.text: And he has shown me loyal love before the king and his advisers and all the mighty princes of the king. So I took courage because the hand of Jehovah my God was upon me, and I gathered out of Israel leading men to go up with me.

nehemiah/1/1.text: 1 The words of Ne·he·miʹah the son of Hac·a·liʹah: Now in the month of Chisʹlev, in the 20th year, I was in Shuʹshan the citadel.

nehemiah/1/2.text: At that time Ha·naʹni, one of my brothers, arrived with other men from Judah, and I asked them about the remaining Jews who had escaped the captivity, and also about Jerusalem.

nehemiah/1/3.text: They replied: “Those remaining there in the province who have survived the captivity are in a terrible situation and in disgrace. The walls of Jerusalem are broken down, and its gates have been burned with fire.”

nehemiah/1/4.text: As soon as I heard these words, I sat down and began to weep and mourn for days, and I kept fasting and praying before the God of the heavens.

nehemiah/1/5.text: I said: “O Jehovah, the God of the heavens, the great and awe-inspiring God who keeps his covenant and shows loyal love to those who love him and keep his commandments,

nehemiah/1/6.text: please, let your ear be attentive and your eyes open to listen to the prayer of your servant that I am praying to you today, day and night, concerning your servants the Israelites, all the while confessing the sins that the people of Israel have committed against you. We have sinned, both I and the house of my father.

nehemiah/1/7.text: We have certainly acted corruptly against you by not keeping the commandments, regulations, and judicial decisions that you gave to your servant Moses.

nehemiah/1/8.text: “Remember, please, the word that you commanded your servant Moses: ‘If you act unfaithfully, I will scatter you among the peoples.

nehemiah/1/9.text: But if you return to me and observe my commandments and obey them, though your dispersed people should be at the end of the heavens, I will gather them from there and bring them to the place that I have chosen to have my name reside.’

nehemiah/1/10.text: They are your servants and your people, whom you redeemed by your great power and by your mighty hand.

nehemiah/1/11.text: O Jehovah, please, let your ear be attentive to the prayer of your servant and to the prayer of your servants who take delight in fearing your name, and please, grant success to your servant today, and may this man show me compassion.” Now I was cupbearer to the king.

esther/2/1.text: 2 After these things, when the rage of King A·has·u·eʹrus had subsided, he remembered what Vashʹti had done and what had been decided against her.

esther/2/2.text: Then the king’s personal attendants said: “A search should be made for young, beautiful virgins for the king.

esther/2/3.text: And let the king appoint commissioners in all the provinces of his realm to bring together all the beautiful young virgins to Shuʹshan the citadel, to the house of the women. Let them be put in the care of Hegʹa·i the king’s eunuch and guardian of the women, and let them be given beauty treatments.

esther/2/4.text: And the young woman who is most pleasing to the king will be queen instead of Vashʹti.” The suggestion was pleasing to the king, and that is what he did.

esther/2/5.text: There was a certain Jewish man in Shuʹshan the citadel whose name was Morʹde·cai son of Jaʹir son of Shimʹe·i son of Kish, a Benʹja·min·ite,

esther/2/6.text: who had been taken into exile from Jerusalem with the people who were deported with King Jec·o·niʹah of Judah, whom King Neb·u·chad·nezʹzar of Babylon took into exile.

esther/2/7.text: He was the guardian of Ha·dasʹsah, that is, Esther, the daughter of his father’s brother, for she had neither father nor mother. The young woman was beautifully formed and attractive in appearance, and at the death of her father and her mother, Morʹde·cai took her as his daughter.

esther/2/8.text: When the king’s word and his law were proclaimed and when many young women were brought together at Shuʹshan the citadel under the care of Hegʹa·i, Esther was also taken to the king’s house under the care of Hegʹa·i the guardian of the women.

esther/2/9.text: Now the young woman was pleasing to him and won his favor, so he promptly arranged for her beauty treatments and her diet, and he assigned to her seven selected young women from the king’s house. He also transferred her and her young attendants to the best place in the house of the women.

esther/2/10.text: Esther did not say anything about her people or her relatives, for Morʹde·cai had instructed her not to tell anyone.

esther/2/11.text: Day after day Morʹde·cai would walk in front of the courtyard of the house of the women to learn about Esther’s welfare and about what was happening to her.

esther/2/12.text: Each young woman had her turn to go in to King A·has·u·eʹrus after completing the 12-month treatment that was prescribed for the women, for this was the way they had to fulfill their beauty treatment—six months with oil of myrrh and six months with balsam oil and various ointments for beauty treatment.

esther/2/13.text: Then the young woman was ready to go in to the king, and whatever she asked for would be given her when she went from the house of the women to the king’s house.

esther/2/14.text: In the evening she would go in, and in the morning she would return to the second house of the women, under the care of Sha·ashʹgaz the king’s eunuch, the guardian of the concubines. She would not go to the king again unless the king had been especially pleased with her and she was requested by name.

esther/2/15.text: And when the turn came for Esther the daughter of Abʹi·ha·il the uncle of Morʹde·cai, who had taken her as his daughter, to go in to the king, she did not request anything except what Hegʹa·i the king’s eunuch, the guardian of the women, recommended. (All the while Esther was winning the favor of everyone who saw her.)

esther/2/16.text: Esther was taken to King A·has·u·eʹrus at his royal house in the tenth month, that is, the month of Teʹbeth, in the seventh year of his reign.

esther/2/17.text: And the king came to love Esther more than all the other women, and she won his favor and approval more than any of the other virgins. So he put the royal headdress on her head and made her queen instead of Vashʹti.

esther/2/18.text: And the king held a great banquet for all his princes and his servants, the banquet of Esther. He then proclaimed an amnesty for the provinces, and he kept giving gifts according to the means of the king.

esther/2/19.text: Now when virgins were brought together a second time, Morʹde·cai was sitting in the king’s gate.

esther/2/20.text: Esther did not say anything about her relatives and her people, just as Morʹde·cai had instructed her; Esther continued to do what Morʹde·cai said, just as when she was under his care.

esther/2/21.text: In those days while Morʹde·cai was sitting in the king’s gate, Bigʹthan and Teʹresh, two court officials of the king, doorkeepers, got angry and plotted to do away with King A·has·u·eʹrus.

esther/2/22.text: But Morʹde·cai learned about it, and he immediately told Queen Esther. Esther then spoke to the king in Morʹde·cai’s name.

esther/2/23.text: So the matter was investigated and eventually confirmed, and both men were hanged on a stake; and this was all recorded in the book of the history of the times in the presence of the king.

hosea/12/1.text: 12 “Eʹphra·im is feeding on wind. He chases after the east wind all day long. He multiplies lies and violence. They make a covenant with As·syrʹi·a and take oil to Egypt.

hosea/12/2.text: Jehovah has a legal case against Judah;He will call for an accounting against Jacob according to his ways, And he will repay him according to his deeds.

hosea/12/3.text: In the womb he seized his brother by the heel, And with his vigor he contended with God.

hosea/12/4.text: He kept contending with an angel and prevailed. He wept and begged for his favor.” He found him at Bethʹel, and there He spoke with us,

hosea/12/5.text: Jehovah the God of armies, Jehovah is his memorial name.

hosea/12/6.text: “So return to your God, Maintain loyal love and justice, And always hope in your God.

hosea/12/7.text: But in the hand of the tradesman are deceptive scales;He loves to defraud.

hosea/12/8.text: Eʹphra·im keeps saying, ‘Indeed, I have become rich;I have found wealth. And in all my toil, they will not find anything wrong or sinful.’

hosea/12/9.text: But I am Jehovah your God from the land of Egypt. I will again make you dwell in tentsAs in the days of an appointed time.

hosea/12/10.text: I spoke to the prophets, I multiplied their visions, And I spoke parables through the prophets.

hosea/12/11.text: With Gilʹe·ad there has been deception and untruth. In Gilʹgal they have sacrificed bulls, And their altars are like piles of stones in the furrows of the field.

hosea/12/12.text: Jacob ran away to the territory of Aʹram;Israel served there for a wife, And for a wife he guarded sheep.

hosea/12/13.text: By a prophet Jehovah brought Israel up from Egypt, And by a prophet he was guarded.

hosea/12/14.text: Eʹphra·im has caused bitter offense;His bloodguilt remains on him;His Lord will repay him for his reproach.”

job/42/1.text: 42 Then Job said in reply to Jehovah:

job/42/2.text: “Now I know that you are able to do all thingsAnd that nothing you have in mind to do is impossible for you.

job/42/3.text: You said, ‘Who is this who is obscuring my counsel without knowledge?’ Therefore I spoke, but without understandingAbout things too wonderful for me, which I do not know.

job/42/4.text: You said, ‘Please listen, and I will speak. I will question you, and you inform me.’

job/42/5.text: My ears have heard about you, But now I do see you with my eyes.

job/42/6.text: That is why I take back what I said, And I repent in dust and ashes.”

job/42/7.text: After Jehovah had spoken these words to Job, Jehovah said to Elʹi·phaz the Teʹman·ite: “My anger burns against you and your two companions, for you have not spoken the truth about me as my servant Job has.

job/42/8.text: Now take seven bulls and seven rams and go to my servant Job, and offer up a burnt sacrifice for yourselves. And my servant Job will pray for you. I will surely accept his request not to deal with you according to your foolishness, for you have not spoken the truth about me as my servant Job has.”

job/42/9.text: So Elʹi·phaz the Teʹman·ite, Bilʹdad the Shuʹhite, and Zoʹphar the Naʹa·ma·thite went and did what Jehovah had told them to do. And Jehovah accepted Job’s prayer.

job/42/10.text: After Job had prayed for his companions, Jehovah removed Job’s tribulation and restored his prosperity. Jehovah gave him double what he had before.

job/42/11.text: All his brothers and sisters and all his former friends came to him and ate a meal with him in his house. They sympathized with him and comforted him over all the calamity that Jehovah had allowed to come upon him. Each of them gave him a piece of money and a gold ring.

job/42/12.text: So Jehovah blessed the last part of Job’s life more than the beginning, and Job came to have 14, 000 sheep, 6, 000 camels, 1, 000 pairs of cattle, and 1, 000 female donkeys.

job/42/13.text: He also came to have seven more sons and three more daughters.

job/42/14.text: He named the first daughter Je·miʹmah, the second Ke·ziʹah, and the third Kerʹen-hapʹpuch.

job/42/15.text: No women in all the land were as beautiful as Job’s daughters, and their father gave them an inheritance along with their brothers.

job/42/16.text: After this Job lived for 140 years, and he saw his children and his grandchildren—four generations.

job/42/17.text: Finally Job died, after a long and satisfying life.

ezekiel/27/1.text: 27 The word of Jehovah again came to me, saying:

ezekiel/27/2.text: “As for you, son of man, sing a dirge over Tyre,

ezekiel/27/3.text: and say to Tyre, ‘You who dwell at the gateways of the sea, The merchant for the peoples of many islands, This is what the Sovereign Lord Jehovah says: “O Tyre, you yourself have said, ‘I am perfect in beauty.’

ezekiel/27/4.text: Your territories are in the heart of the sea, And your builders have perfected your beauty.

ezekiel/27/5.text: They made all your planks from the juniper trees of Seʹnir, And they took a cedar from Lebʹa·non to make a mast for you.

ezekiel/27/6.text: They made your oars from oaks of Baʹshan, And your prow was of cypress inlaid with ivory from the islands of Kitʹtim.

ezekiel/27/7.text: Colorful linen from Egypt served as cloth for your sail, And your deck awnings were of blue thread and purple wool from the islands of E·liʹshah.

ezekiel/27/8.text: The inhabitants of Siʹdon and of Arʹvad were your rowers. Your own skilled men, O Tyre, were your sailors.

ezekiel/27/9.text: The experienced and skilled men of Geʹbal caulked your seams. All the ships of the sea and their mariners came to you to trade merchandise.

ezekiel/27/10.text: Men of Persia, Lud, and Put were in your army, your men of war. They hung their shields and helmets in you, and they brought you splendor.

ezekiel/27/11.text: The men of Arʹvad in your army were stationed on your walls all around, And brave men manned your towers. They hung circular shields all around your wallsAnd perfected your beauty.

ezekiel/27/12.text: “‘“Tarʹshish did business with you because of your abundant wealth. They exchanged silver, iron, tin, and lead for your goods.

ezekiel/27/13.text: Jaʹvan, Tuʹbal, and Meʹshech traded with you, exchanging slaves and articles of copper for your merchandise.

ezekiel/27/14.text: The house of To·garʹmah exchanged horses and steeds and mules for your goods.

ezekiel/27/15.text: The people of Deʹdan traded with you; you employed merchants on many islands; they gave ivory tusks and ebony as your tribute.

ezekiel/27/16.text: Eʹdom did business with you because of the abundance of your products. They gave turquoise, purple wool, colorful embroidery, fine fabric, corals, and rubies in exchange for your goods.

ezekiel/27/17.text: “‘“Judah and the land of Israel traded with you, giving the wheat of Minʹnith, choice foods, honey, oil, and balsam in exchange for your goods.

ezekiel/27/18.text: “‘“Damascus did business with you because of the abundance of your products and all your wealth, trading the wine of Helʹbon and wool of Zaʹhar.

ezekiel/27/19.text: Veʹdan and Jaʹvan from Uʹzal gave wrought iron, cassia, and cane in exchange for your goods.

ezekiel/27/20.text: Deʹdan traded with you in saddlecloths for riding.

ezekiel/27/21.text: You employed the Arabs and all the chieftains of Keʹdar, who were merchants of lambs and rams and goats.

ezekiel/27/22.text: The merchants of Sheʹba and Raʹa·mah traded with you; they gave all sorts of the finest perfumes, precious stones, and gold in exchange for your goods.

ezekiel/27/23.text: Haʹran, Canʹneh, Eʹden, the merchants of Sheʹba, Asʹshur, and Chilʹmad traded with you.

ezekiel/27/24.text: In your marketplace they traded beautiful garments, cloaks made of blue material and colorful embroidery, and multicolored carpets, all bound and secured with ropes.

ezekiel/27/25.text: The ships of Tarʹshish were the caravans for your merchandise, So that you were filled and loaded down in the heart of the open sea.

ezekiel/27/26.text: Your rowers have brought you into heavy seas;The east wind has wrecked you in the heart of the open sea.

ezekiel/27/27.text: Your wealth, your goods, your merchandise, your mariners, and your sailors, Those caulking your seams, those trading your merchandise, and all the men of war—The entire multitude within you—They will all sink in the heart of the open sea on the day of your downfall.

ezekiel/27/28.text: When your sailors cry out, the coastlands will shudder.

ezekiel/27/29.text: All the oarsmen, the mariners, and the seamenWill come down from their ships and stand on the land.

ezekiel/27/30.text: They will raise their voices and cry out bitterly over youAs they throw dust on their heads and wallow in ashes.

ezekiel/27/31.text: They will make themselves bald and put on sackcloth;They will weep bitterly over you with intense wailing.

ezekiel/27/32.text: In their lamentation they will sing a dirge and chant over you: ‘Who is like Tyre, now silent in the midst of the sea?

ezekiel/27/33.text: When your goods came in from the open sea, you satisfied many peoples. Your abundant wealth and your merchandise enriched earth’s kings.

ezekiel/27/34.text: Now you have been wrecked in the open sea, in the deep waters, And all your merchandise and your people have sunk with you.

ezekiel/27/35.text: All the inhabitants of the islands will stare at you in amazement, And their kings will shudder with horror—their faces will be troubled.

ezekiel/27/36.text: The merchants among the nations will whistle over what happened to you. Your end will be sudden and terrible, And you will cease to exist for all time.’”’”

zechariah/9/1.text: 9 A pronouncement: “The word of Jehovah is against the land of Haʹdrach, And Damascus is its target—For Jehovah’s eye is on mankindAnd on all the tribes of Israel—

zechariah/9/2.text: And against Haʹmath, which borders on her, And against Tyre and Siʹdon, for they are so wise.

zechariah/9/3.text: Tyre built herself a rampart. She piled up silver like dustAnd gold like the dirt of the streets.

zechariah/9/4.text: Look! Jehovah will take away her possessions, And he will strike down her army into the sea;And she will be consumed in the fire.

zechariah/9/5.text: Ashʹke·lon will see it and be afraid;Gazʹa will feel great anguish, Also Ekʹron, because her hope is put to shame. A king will perish from Gazʹa, And Ashʹke·lon will not be inhabited.

zechariah/9/6.text: An illegitimate son will settle in Ashʹdod, And I will do away with the pride of the Phi·lisʹtine.

zechariah/9/7.text: I will remove the bloodstained things from his mouthAnd the disgusting things from between his teeth, And he will be left remaining for our God;And he will become like a sheikh in Judah, And Ekʹron like the Jebʹu·site.

zechariah/9/8.text: I will encamp as a guard for my house, So that there will be no one passing through and no one returning;And no taskmaster will pass through again, For now I have seen it with my eyes.

zechariah/9/9.text: Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion. Shout in triumph, O daughter of Jerusalem. Look! Your king is coming to you. He is righteous, bringing salvation, Humble and riding on a donkey, On a colt, the foal of a female donkey.

zechariah/9/10.text: I will take away the war chariot from Eʹphra·imAnd the horse from Jerusalem. The battle bow will be taken away. And he will proclaim peace to the nations;His rulership will be from sea to seaAnd from the River to the ends of the earth.

zechariah/9/11.text: As for you, O woman, by the blood of your covenant, I will send your prisoners out of the waterless pit.

zechariah/9/12.text: Return to the stronghold, you prisoners with hope. Today I am telling you, ‘I will repay to you, O woman, a double portion.

zechariah/9/13.text: For I will bend Judah as my bow. The bow I will fill with Eʹphra·im, And I will awaken your sons, O Zion, Against your sons, O Greece, And I will make you like a warrior’s sword.’

zechariah/9/14.text: Jehovah will be seen over them, And his arrow will go out like lightning. The Sovereign Lord Jehovah will sound the horn, And he will advance with the windstorms of the south.

zechariah/9/15.text: Jehovah of armies will defend them, And they will devour and subdue the slingstones. They will drink and be boisterous, as if with wine;And they will be filled like the bowl, Like the corners of the altar.

zechariah/9/16.text: Jehovah their God will save them in that dayAs the flock of his people;For they will be like the gemstones of a crown glittering over his soil.

zechariah/9/17.text: For how great his goodness is, And how great his handsomeness is! Grain will make the young men thrive, And new wine the virgins.”

malachi/1/1.text: 1 A pronouncement: The word of Jehovah to Israel through Malʹa·chi:

malachi/1/2.text: “I have shown love to you people, ” says Jehovah. But you say: “How have you shown us love?” “Was not Eʹsau the brother of Jacob?” declares Jehovah. “But I loved Jacob,

malachi/1/3.text: and Eʹsau I hated; and I made his mountains desolate and left his inheritance for the jackals of the wilderness.”

malachi/1/4.text: “Though Eʹdom says, ‘We have been shattered, but we will return and rebuild the ruins, ’ this is what Jehovah of armies says, ‘They will build, but I will tear down, and they will be called “the territory of wickedness” and “the people whom Jehovah has forever condemned.”

malachi/1/5.text: Your own eyes will see it, and you will say: “May Jehovah be magnified over the territory of Israel.”’”

malachi/1/6.text: “‘A son honors a father, and a servant his master. So if I am a father, where is the honor due me? And if I am a master, where is the fear due me?’ Jehovah of armies says to you priests who are despising my name. “‘But you say: “How have we despised your name?”’

malachi/1/7.text: “‘By presenting polluted food on my altar.’ “‘And you say: “How have we polluted you?”’ “‘By saying: “The table of Jehovah is something to be despised.”

malachi/1/8.text: And when you present a blind animal as a sacrifice, you say: “It is nothing bad.” And when you present a lame animal or a sick one: “It is nothing bad.”’” “Try presenting them, please, to your governor. Will he be pleased with you or receive you with favor?” says Jehovah of armies.

malachi/1/9.text: “And now, please, appeal to God, that he may show us favor. With such offerings from your own hand, will he receive any of you with favor?” says Jehovah of armies.

malachi/1/10.text: “And who among you is willing to shut the doors? For you will not even light my altar without charge. I find no delight in you, ” says Jehovah of armies, “and I take no pleasure in any gift offering from your hand.”

malachi/1/11.text: “For from the rising of the sun to its setting, my name will be great among the nations. In every place sacrifices will be made to smoke, and offerings will be made to my name, as a pure gift; because my name will be great among the nations, ” says Jehovah of armies.

malachi/1/12.text: “But you are profaning it by saying, ‘The table of Jehovah is polluted, and its fruit, its food, is to be despised.’

malachi/1/13.text: You also say, ‘Look! How tiresome!’ and you sniff scornfully at it, ” says Jehovah of armies. “And you bring stolen, lame, and sick animals. Yes, you bring such things as a gift! Should I accept it from your hand?” says Jehovah.

malachi/1/14.text: “Cursed is the cunning one who has a sound male animal in his flock, but he makes a vow and sacrifices a blemished one to Jehovah. For I am a great King, ” says Jehovah of armies, “and my name will be awe-inspiring among the nations.”

haggai/1/1.text: 1 In the second year of King Da·riʹus, in the sixth month, on the first day of the month, the word of Jehovah came through Hagʹgai the prophet to Ze·rubʹba·bel son of She·alʹti·el, the governor of Judah, and to Joshua son of Je·hozʹa·dak, the high priest, saying:

haggai/1/2.text: “This is what Jehovah of armies says, ‘These people say, “The time has not yet come for the house of Jehovah to be built.”’”

haggai/1/3.text: And the word of Jehovah again came through Hagʹgai the prophet, saying:

haggai/1/4.text: “Is it the time for you to dwell in your paneled houses, while this house lies in ruins?

haggai/1/5.text: Now this is what Jehovah of armies says, ‘Set your heart on your ways.

haggai/1/6.text: You have sown much seed, but you harvest little. You eat, but it is not to satisfaction. You drink, but you do not drink your fill. You put on clothing, but no one gets warm. The one who hires himself out puts his wages in a bag full of holes.’”

haggai/1/7.text: “This is what Jehovah of armies says, ‘Set your heart on your ways.’

haggai/1/8.text: “‘Go up to the mountain and bring in lumber. And build the house, so that I may take pleasure in it and I may be glorified, ’ Jehovah says.”

haggai/1/9.text: “‘You were expecting much and receiving little; and when you brought it into the house, I blew it away. For what reason?’ declares Jehovah of armies. ‘Because my house is in ruins, while each of you runs around taking care of his own house.

haggai/1/10.text: So the heavens above you withheld their dew, and the earth withheld its produce.

haggai/1/11.text: And I kept calling for a drought on the earth, on the mountains, on the grain, on the new wine, on the oil, on what grows from the ground, on humans and livestock, and on all the labor of your hands.’”

haggai/1/12.text: Ze·rubʹba·bel son of She·alʹti·el and Joshua son of Je·hozʹa·dak, the high priest, and all the rest of the people listened to the voice of Jehovah their God and to the words of Hagʹgai the prophet, because Jehovah their God had sent him; and the people began to show fear because of Jehovah.

haggai/1/13.text: Then Hagʹgai, the messenger of Jehovah, gave this message to the people in harmony with his commission from Jehovah: “‘I am with you people, ’ declares Jehovah.”

haggai/1/14.text: So Jehovah stirred up the spirit of Ze·rubʹba·bel the son of She·alʹti·el, the governor of Judah, and the spirit of Joshua the son of Je·hozʹa·dak, the high priest, and the spirit of all the rest of the people; and they came and began to work on the house of Jehovah of armies, their God.

haggai/1/15.text: This was on the 24th day of the sixth month in the second year of King Da·riʹus.

psalms/90/1.text: 90 O Jehovah, you have been our dwelling place throughout all generations.

psalms/90/2.text: Before the mountains were bornOr you brought forth the earth and the productive land, From everlasting to everlasting, you are God.

psalms/90/3.text: You make mortal man return to dust;You say: “Return, you sons of men.”

psalms/90/4.text: For a thousand years are in your eyes just as yesterday when it is past, Just as a watch during the night.

psalms/90/5.text: You sweep them away; they become like mere sleep;In the morning they are like grass that sprouts.

psalms/90/6.text: In the morning it blossoms and is renewed, But by evening it withers and dries up.

psalms/90/7.text: For we are consumed by your angerAnd terrified by your rage.

psalms/90/8.text: You place our errors in front of you;Our secrets are exposed by the light of your face.

psalms/90/9.text: Our days ebb away because of your fury;And our years come to an end like a whisper.

psalms/90/10.text: The span of our life is 70 years, Or 80 if one is especially strong. But they are filled with trouble and sorrow;They quickly pass by, and away we fly.

psalms/90/11.text: Who can fathom the power of your anger? Your fury is as great as the fear you deserve.

psalms/90/12.text: Teach us how to count our daysSo that we may acquire a heart of wisdom.

psalms/90/13.text: Return, O Jehovah! How long will this last? Have pity on your servants.

psalms/90/14.text: Satisfy us with your loyal love in the morning, So that we may shout joyfully and rejoice during all our days.

psalms/90/15.text: Make us rejoice in proportion to the days you have afflicted us, For as many years as we have experienced calamity.

psalms/90/16.text: May your servants see your activity, And may their sons see your splendor.

psalms/90/17.text: May the favor of Jehovah our God be upon us;May you prosper the work of our hands. Yes, prosper the work of our hands.
